ProgramName: Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology degree program, prospective students must have a bachelor’s degree in Anthropology or a related field (e.g., Sociology, Geography, History, Political Science, Philosophy, Religious Studies, Women’s and Gender Studies, Environmental Studies). Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in a non-related field may be considered for admission if their undergraduate training or professional experience has provided appropriate background. Students who are admitted but lack sufficient background in anthropology may be required to complete preparatory coursework. Application to the MA in Applied Anthropology program is a two-part process requiring applicants to apply to both the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Anthropology. You must provide the following materials to the Toulouse Graduate School: An official transcript from each college or university you have attended. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing). You must provide the following materials to the Department of Anthropology: A current curriculum vita (CV) or resume. A Statement of Purpose that explains your academic and research background, your interest in the MA in Applied Anthropology program at UNT, and your career goals, as well as an identification of one or more faculty members with whom you would like to work and why (approximately 1,000 words). A writing sample (e.g., a paper or thesis from an undergraduate course). Three letters of recommendation. For international applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), IELTS score of 6.0, or PTE score of 53 is required. The departmental recommendation is a minimum TOEFL score of 90 (internet-based).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) program in Applied Anthropology offers two tracks: Cultural Anthropology and Public Archeology. The MA program helps students develop skills in grant writing, research design, project management, and cultural resource management. Students can also participate in fieldwork, internships, and laboratory research. The program prepares students for careers in cultural resource management, museums, non-profit agencies, community advocacy organizations, government agencies, international development, and more. A PhD in Applied Anthropology is also available.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Art Education
Requirements:
In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Art Education must meet the following program requirements:
* A strong interest in art education.
* Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in undergraduate work.
* Resume or CV
* Statement of purpose explaining your interest in art education and professional goals.
* Two letters of recommendation, with at least one from a university faculty member.
* Writing sample of an academic paper completed during undergraduate or previous graduate work (5-10 pages).
* Portfolio of 10-15 images of recent artwork. Include a list of images (title, medium, dimensions, date). Applicants will upload their writing sample and portfolio to their personal Slideroom account, accessed through the application.
* Official GRE scores are not required for admission.
* International applicants must fulfill requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School regarding English proficiency.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The MA in Art Education allows students to tailor their graduate studies to suit their interests and career goals. Students choose courses from the fields of art education, art history, studio art and related areas. The program offers thesis and non-thesis options. Graduates are prepared for a range of professional opportunities as art educators in K-12 schools, community organizations, museums, galleries and other institutions.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: ~$486/credit hour; Non-Resident: ~$1025/credit hour (based on 1-9 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Graduate), Fellowships (Merit-based, Doctoral, Master's, External), UNT Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Art History
Requirements:
In addition to the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants to the MA in Art History must meet the following departmental requirements:
1. An undergraduate major in art history or 18 semester hours of advanced courses in art history that are approved by the department.
2. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0.
3. Three letters of recommendation submitted directly to the Graduate School.
4. A statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum) outlining the student’s interests in art history and reasons for pursuing graduate study.
5. A writing sample (8-10 pages) that demonstrates the student’s ability to write critically and clearly about art history. This should be an essay written for an advanced undergraduate art history course.
6. A CV or resume.
7. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
8. GRE scores are NOT required for admission to the MA program in Art History.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Master of Arts in Art History degree program offers two paths to completion: a thesis option and a non-thesis option. In both cases, the program is a 30-hour course of study for students interested in advanced work in art history. Students pursuing the M.A. in Art History work closely with faculty in their areas of interest, are involved in research and critical analysis, and have opportunities to develop their teaching skills and gain professional experience. The M.A. prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, and archives, as well as for further graduate study at the doctoral level.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Communication Studies
Requirements: Admission to the M.A. program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better and a combined Verbal and Quantitative score of 300 or better on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE). The analytical writing score from the GRE is also taken into consideration. To apply for the M.A. in Communication Studies, you must submit the following: A completed application for graduate admission. Official transcripts of all college-level work. Official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing). A statement of purpose (1,000 words max) that explains your interest in the MA program in Communication Studies at UNT, your research interests, and your professional goals. A current resume or CV. A writing sample (e.g., a scholarly paper, a research paper, a chapter from an undergraduate thesis, etc.) that demonstrates your ability to write clearly and persuasively. For additional information, see the Communication Studies Graduate Catalog.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: Health Communication, Intercultural Communication, Mediated Communication
Description: The Master of Arts in Communication Studies program prepares students for a diverse range of careers in higher education, research, and for positions within private and public organizations. The program allows students to specialize within the areas of Health Communication, Intercultural Communication, and Mediated Communication, while preparing them for doctoral work. The curriculum helps students develop knowledge and skills in critical inquiry, research design, theory, and professional presentation within and beyond the communication discipline. Faculty expertise includes intercultural communication, health communication, rhetorical studies, media studies, organizational communication, and interpersonal communication.
MinimumGreScore: combined verbal and quantitative GRE score of at least 290 and an analytical writing score of at least 3.5
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Competitive Scholarships, Graduate Tuition Benefit Plan

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Creative Writing
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MA in Creative Writing, applicants must meet the following requirements in addition to the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 grade point average on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Statement of Purpose that explains the applicant's reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in Creative Writing, outlining previous experience in the field and discussing literary influences. Resume (or curriculum vitae) listing academic and professional achievements. Writing Sample of 15-25 pages of original fiction, poetry or creative nonfiction. Applicants must identify the genre of the writing sample. Three letters of recommendation from former professors or professionals who can attest to the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional aptitudes.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Creative Writing at UNT provides advanced study in the writing of fiction, poetry, and literary nonfiction. Our program emphasizes work in one primary genre, as well as the study of literature and literary theory, culminating in the composition of a book-length manuscript or thesis. Graduates of our program teach creative writing and English at the high school and college levels, work in editing and publishing, or continue on to Ph.D. programs.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MA in English program, an applicant must satisfy the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, hold a bachelor’s degree with an undergraduate major in English, or at least 18 hours of upper-division English credit, including a minimum of three hours in American literature, three hours in British literature, and three hours in advanced writing. Applicants are also required to submit a personal statement (300-500 words) and a critical writing sample (8-10 pages) demonstrating their ability to formulate and support an argument about literary texts. Applicants must also provide three letters of recommendation from faculty members familiar with their academic work.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts program in English at UNT provides graduate students with a rigorous, comprehensive education in literary studies. Students engage in advanced critical thinking and research, developing expertise in various literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches. The curriculum emphasizes analytical skills, clear communication, and scholarly writing, preparing graduates for doctoral studies, teaching positions, and diverse professional careers.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and the following program requirements: One official transcript of all college work. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and/or a 3.5 GPA on all graduate work. GRE revised General Test required. A minimum score of 153 on the verbal portion, 144 on the quantitative portion, and 4.0 on the analytical writing portion is recommended. A statement of purpose (1,000 words, double-spaced) describing your previous academic and/or professional training, the areas of history you propose to study at UNT, and your future career goals. A writing sample (8-15 pages, double-spaced) demonstrating your ability to conduct research and write a scholarly paper. Three letters of recommendation from former professors who are familiar with your academic work. Resume/CV (optional).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (Department of History)
Description: The Department of History offers a Master of Arts degree that provides advanced training in historical research and writing. The program prepares students for continued graduate work at the Ph.D. level or for a variety of public and private sector careers, including teaching at the community college level, work in museums, archives, or government agencies. Students select a major field (American History, European History, or Latin American History) and a minor field from a different region (American, European, or Latin American) or from a topical field (African History, Asian History, Ancient/Classical History, or Public History). Students also select a subfield, which may be a specific time period or a particular approach to history (e.g., gender history, environmental history, etc.).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Fellowships, Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Graduate)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
Requirements: A formal application to The Graduate School and the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to The Graduate School. GRE is required.
Department: Toulouse Graduate School
Description:
The MA in Interdisciplinary Studies is a research-based, customizable graduate program that provides students with the opportunity to pursue an individualized course of study. The curriculum is constructed around three academic areas, or fields of study, chosen by the student. These fields of study draw from the rich and diverse faculty and departmental offerings across the university.
The MA in Interdisciplinary Studies is designed for students seeking a graduate program that transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries and fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and cross-disciplinary communication skills. Graduates are prepared for careers that require adaptability, creativity, and the ability to synthesize knowledge from multiple perspectives.
Students work closely with an Interdisciplinary Studies faculty advisor and a faculty committee chosen by the student, ensuring personalized guidance throughout their academic journey.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Applied Gerontology
Requirements: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) general test is required. Statement of Purpose. Two letters of recommendation. Resume.
Department: Toulouse Graduate School
Fees: Resident: $4,917.48/semester (for 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $9,711.48/semester (for 9 credit hours)
Fees.1: Resident: $4,917.48/semester (for 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $9,711.48/semester (for 9 credit hours)
Description: The Interdisciplinary Studies (M.A.) with a concentration in Applied Gerontology combines the expertise of UNT’s Gerontology program with the flexibility of the Interdisciplinary Studies M.A. The program is designed for students interested in working with older adults in a variety of settings, as well as those pursuing further graduate education in gerontology. Coursework is designed to provide students with a strong theoretical and practical understanding of gerontology.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Doctoral Fellowships, Master's Fellowships, Tuition Waivers, Graduate Student Health Insurance, Travel Grants, Research Grants

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Digital Social Science
Requirements: Completion of a bachelor's degree. A strong academic record, typically a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic abilities and/or professional experience. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that addresses: Why you are interested in the MAIS program and the Digital Social Science concentration specifically; How your academic and professional background has prepared you for this interdisciplinary program; Your research interests and career goals, and how this program aligns with them. A curriculum vitae or resume. GRE scores are NOT required.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies (MAIS) degree program is designed for students whose intellectual and professional interests require a unique combination of courses from three academic disciplines at UNT. This degree provides flexibility in course selection and research options. Students, with the help of a faculty advisory committee, design a plan of study that crosses departmental, college and institutional boundaries. The MAIS degree allows for flexibility in course selection and research options within areas such as Digital Humanities, Information Science, Music, Public Administration, Public Relations, Rehabilitation Counseling, Sociology, Technical Communication and Urban Planning.
ScholarshipType: Departmental, Excellence, Tuition Grant, International Student, External, Need-based

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities
Requirements: Admission to the master’s program is open to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, which are listed in the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog. In addition to meeting the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants for the MA in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Humanities must submit: An essay (2-5 pages) explaining how the applicant's prior academic and/or professional experiences have prepared them for interdisciplinary study in the humanities and what they hope to achieve through the program. This essay serves as a writing sample and statement of purpose. Three letters of recommendation, at least two from university faculty familiar with the applicant’s academic performance. Official transcripts of all college-level work. An academic resume or curriculum vitae (CV) describing previous education, employment history and any other information relevant to graduate study. GRE Scores: Applicants whose undergraduate GPA is less than 3.0 must also submit official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Applicants who are required to take the GRE must also include an unofficial copy of their scores in their application packet.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies (MAIS) is a custom-designed master's degree program that allows students to combine graduate-level courses from three academic disciplines into a unified program of study based on a central theme, problem or issue. The humanities concentration allows students to pursue courses related to Art, Dance, English, History, Journalism, Media Arts, Music, Philosophy and Religion, Second Language Acquisition, Sociology, and Technical Communication.
ScholarshipType: Tuition Scholarships, Fellowships, Assistantships (Teaching, Research), Grants (Travel)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication
Requirements: You must meet the general requirements for admission to the graduate school and specific requirements for the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication. General Admission Requirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. (You may also be admitted if you demonstrate equivalent academic achievement.) An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (or a minimum score on the GRE). Satisfactory performance on the GRE General Test, if required by the program. Degree-specific Admission Requirements: For the M.A. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication, you must also: Possess a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA on 12 hours of graduate coursework (or a GRE total score of 292 with a minimum of 146 on both the verbal and quantitative sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing section).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences and the College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: Our Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication is available in a convenient 100% online format. In this program, you’ll focus on how humans communicate and interact with digital technologies to create virtual experiences. The digital communication concentration helps students understand and critically analyze digital communication and media, as well as design and develop digital interactive and virtual experiences. You'll learn about: Digital communication in society, Communication in digital environments, Virtual environments and experiences, Media and digital communication ethics, Interactive media theory, Research methods in digital communication. UNT offers students the opportunity to: Study with faculty from various departments and colleges across the university. Work with an interdisciplinary team to apply skills in a practical setting. Prepare for a career in interactive and virtual communication, marketing, public relations or digital media.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Program Leadership
Requirements:
Admission to the Interdisciplinary Studies, M.A. program requires the following:
*   GRE general test scores. Official GRE scores are required for all applicants.
*   Statement of purpose. Required.
*   Writing sample. Required.
*   Three letters of recommendation. Required.
*   Resume or curriculum vitae. Required.
*   Application to the Toulouse Graduate School. All prospective graduate students must apply for admission to UNT’s Toulouse Graduate School.
Department: The Graduate School
Description: UNT's Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Program Leadership prepares you to lead programs in a variety of settings. Organizations across all sectors (government, non-profit, corporate, educational) need skilled program leaders to plan, manage, evaluate and lead the initiatives that serve their missions. Program leadership is an evolving field that demands individuals with both conceptual and practical skills. In this concentration, you will explore the knowledge and skills necessary to be an effective program leader, including program planning, development, implementation, evaluation, fundraising, strategic planning, human resources, budgeting and assessment. Our unique curriculum allows students to integrate the study of program leadership with another area of interest such as business, communication, higher education, public administration or another field. It is a highly customizable degree that can be tailored to meet your specific career goals. We offer courses fully online.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Tuition support, Research/Travel Grants, Assistantships (with tuition remission)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the M.A. program in International Studies, applicants should apply online through the Toulouse Graduate School and submit the following documents directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Transcripts must be sent directly from the institution in a sealed envelope or through a secure electronic method to the Toulouse Graduate School. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability and potential for success in graduate school. Letters of recommendation should be submitted directly by the recommenders to the Toulouse Graduate School. Statement of Purpose: A two-page (double-spaced) statement outlining your academic and professional goals, research interests, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in International Studies at UNT. The statement should demonstrate your writing ability and analytical skills. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV): A current resume or CV highlighting your educational background, work experience, research projects, publications, presentations, and any other relevant experience. Writing Sample: An academic paper, essay, or research project (8-15 pages in length) that demonstrates your research, analytical, and writing skills. The writing sample should preferably be on a topic related to international studies or political science. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores are NOT required for admission to the MA in International Studies program. For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency is required (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test scores). Please refer to the Toulouse Graduate School website for specific requirements.
Department: College of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences
Fees: $5,780.00 - $10,244.00/Semester (based on 9 credit hours, 2024-2025 rates for Texas Resident / Non-Resident)
Description: The Master of Arts in International Studies (MAIS) program at the University of North Texas provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of global issues and prepares them for careers in international affairs, government, non-governmental organizations, and further graduate study. Students develop advanced analytical skills, critical thinking, and a comprehensive understanding of international political, economic, and cultural dynamics. The curriculum is designed to offer both breadth in international studies and the opportunity for specialization through elective courses and thesis/professional paper options.
CostPerCredit: $530.60 - $938.60/credit hour (2024-2025 rates for Texas Resident / Non-Resident)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Journalism
Requirements: Review the University requirements for graduate admission. Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores. If required by the department, official GRE scores must be sent directly from the Educational Testing Service (ETS) to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School (code 6480). For more information, visit the GRE General Test website. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International students may be required to submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. 3.0 GPA minimum in the last 60 undergraduate hours. Writing sample – maximum 10 pages. Please choose work that reflects your best writing ability, whether academic or professional. If you do not have any writing that you feel showcases your best work, consider writing a new piece specifically for this application. Resume (Required). Statement of Purpose (Required). Three (3) letters of recommendation.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Journalism program gives students the opportunity to advance their knowledge and skills to lead and innovate in the ever-evolving fields of media and communication. Students gain expertise in media theory, research, ethics, and practices across a variety of traditional and emerging platforms. Through advanced coursework and scholarly inquiry, students develop a deep understanding of the role of journalism in a democratic society, critical thinking skills, and proficiency in creating high-quality, impactful content. This program is ideal for professionals seeking career advancement, individuals preparing for doctoral studies, or those looking to transition into the dynamic world of journalism and strategic communication. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in news organizations, public relations, advertising, media management, content creation, and related fields, or for further academic pursuits.
ScholarshipType: Texas Public Education Grant (TPEG), Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Media Industry and Critical Studies
Requirements: Admission to the master’s program in Media Industry and Critical Studies is contingent on admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and on the recommendation of the department. The decision to admit a student to the program is based on a holistic review of all application materials and considers factors related to the applicant’s background and aptitude for graduate study in media studies. Applicants must satisfy the following additional requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are not required to have an undergraduate degree in media studies or a related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) that describes the applicant’s academic interests and goals, relevant experiences, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in Media Industry and Critical Studies at UNT. A writing sample (e.g., an academic paper, professional report, or published article) that demonstrates the applicant’s analytical and writing abilities. Official GRE scores are not required. A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
Fees.1: Estimated $15,316/Year for Texas Residents (Fall 2024, 18 credit hours)
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Media Industry and Critical Studies prepares students for further graduate study in media studies or related fields, as well as for work in a variety of industries (including the media industry) that require advanced analytical, communication, and research skills. Drawing upon a critical and interdisciplinary approach, the MA curriculum grounds students in the history, theory, and methods of media studies, while also providing them with knowledge of the shifting landscape of media industries and their cultural, economic, and political significance. Required coursework provides a foundation in media industry and critical studies research. Students then choose electives from a wide range of courses in media theory and history, media industries and institutions, and media and culture. The program provides two options for completing the MA: the thesis option and the professional paper option. In consultation with a graduate advisor, students choose the option best suited to their academic and professional goals.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music
Department: College of Music
CostPerCredit: $288.87 per credit hour (Estimated for Texas Resident, includes tuition and per-credit fees, Fall 2024-Spring 2025 rates)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: To apply for this program, you must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School through the ApplyUNT portal. The following items are required for your application: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation addressing your academic abilities. A statement of purpose outlining your philosophical interests and your reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in philosophy at UNT. A writing sample of 10-20 pages (preferably philosophical).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: This program is designed for students whose intellectual interests are best served by broad, rather than highly specialized, study within philosophy. Students will explore traditional areas of philosophy (e.g., epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, logic, history of philosophy) and will gain an awareness of current work in these areas. The program provides a broad-based, rigorous education in philosophy suitable for students who wish to teach philosophy at community colleges, pursue a Ph.D. in philosophy, or obtain an M.A. as preparation for other professional or academic careers.
CostPerCredit: $569.22/Credit Hour (Texas Resident, based on 9 credit hours)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: Applicants must meet the following general requirements to be considered for admission to the M.A. program in political science. Meeting these requirements does not guarantee admission. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale over the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework (or 3.0 overall for students with less than 60 hours of undergraduate coursework). A strong letter of intent (statement of purpose). Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional potential. A writing sample of no more than 20 pages. A background in political science, history, economics, or another relevant discipline. Minimum scores on the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test are required for students with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0. For students with an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher, the GRE is optional. International applicants must also meet UNT's English Language Proficiency requirements.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The M.A. in Political Science offers students training in the discipline's major fields as well as an opportunity to deepen their understanding of political phenomena. Students can elect to write a thesis or complete a non-thesis option. The program is designed to prepare students for a Ph.D. program or for employment in government, think tanks, or the private sector. Students in the M.A. program take 30 hours of graduate work, including courses in American politics, comparative politics, and international relations, as well as political theory and methodology. All students must complete PSCI 5000: Political Science Research and Methods. At the completion of their coursework, students take comprehensive examinations in two of the three subfields (American politics, comparative politics, or international relations) or submit a thesis.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science with a concentration in Advocacy, Politics and Policy
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts program in political science is open to students holding a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the following requirements for unconditional admission:
1. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate hours.
2. A combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE).
3. Two letters of recommendation from former instructors who can attest to the applicant’s academic preparedness and scholarly potential. Applicants with a period of professional work experience may substitute one letter from a professional supervisor.
4. A statement of purpose (approximately 500-700 words) describing the applicant’s academic interests and career goals. The statement should also address how the applicant’s academic and/or professional background has prepared them for graduate study in political science at UNT.
5. A writing sample demonstrating the applicant’s ability to conduct research and write an analytical essay. Typically, this is a research paper prepared for a previous political science course. No minimum or maximum length is specified, but the applicant should choose a sample that best demonstrates their writing and analytical skills.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Political Science with a concentration in Advocacy, Politics and Policy is designed to provide students with a strong theoretical and practical understanding of political processes, public policy and advocacy. The program will equip students with the necessary skills to analyze complex political issues, develop effective advocacy strategies, and contribute to public discourse and policymaking. Students will engage with core concepts in political science, including political theory, comparative politics, international relations, and American politics, while also gaining specialized knowledge in areas such as grassroots organizing, lobbying, campaign management, and policy analysis.
ScholarshipType: Competitive Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Assistantships, Travel Grants

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Professional and Technical Communication
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate School requires a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution and a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission. Additional requirements for the Professional and Technical Communication MA program include: A two-page, single-spaced statement of purpose addressing your academic and professional experience and how the Professional and Technical Communication program will help you meet your career goals; An updated résumé or curriculum vitae; An academic or professional writing sample of approximately 10-20 pages; Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; The GRE is not required for admission to the MA program.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Professional and Technical Communication is an interdisciplinary degree that enables students to develop their skills as communicators, researchers, and critical thinkers. Students in the program develop practical and theoretical knowledge that prepares them for careers in fields such as: corporate communications, technical writing, editing, grant writing, digital content creation, information architecture, usability, web design, and digital publication. Students in our program also learn how to engage in ethical and critical communication across various contexts, and they learn how to apply their skills as professional communicators to a variety of workplaces and organizations. Coursework provides students with the opportunity to pursue individualized interests in a range of relevant areas, including: rhetoric, writing and editing, digital media, digital humanities, and communication for social justice.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Spanish
Requirements: An applicant must meet the university requirements for admission to graduate school as well as the following departmental requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework. A minimum of 24 upper-level undergraduate hours in Spanish, including courses in composition, culture, civilization, literature and linguistics, with a minimum grade of B in all Spanish courses. An academic writing sample, preferably in Spanish. A statement of purpose, preferably in Spanish, describing their interest in graduate study in Spanish at UNT. A letter of recommendation (optional). Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test, with a minimum of 145 (quantitative) and 153 (verbal) on the revised test (or equivalent on the previous test); or a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in 12 hours of graduate coursework.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The M.A. program in Spanish is designed to develop in students a broad knowledge of Hispanic literatures and cultures, as well as an advanced command of the Spanish language. Students may choose either the Latin American literature and cultures option or the Peninsular literature and cultures option. Both options prepare students for doctoral work in Spanish or related fields and for careers requiring expertise in Spanish language, literature and culture. They are particularly relevant for those seeking to teach Spanish at the college or secondary level. The M.A. in Spanish requires 30 credit hours. Students may choose a thesis or non-thesis option.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Women's and Gender Studies
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements:
A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are not required to have an undergraduate major in women's and gender studies, but must demonstrate previous coursework or experience in the field.
An undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
GRE scores are not required for admission to the MA in Women's and Gender Studies.
Three letters of recommendation addressing academic qualifications and scholarly potential.
Applicants must submit the following materials through the Toulouse Graduate School’s online application system:
- A 1-2 page statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic interests and preparation for graduate work.
- A 10-20 page writing sample (e.g., a term paper or publication) that demonstrates the applicant’s research abilities and writing proficiency.
- A current curriculum vitae (CV) or resume.
- Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The M.A. in Women’s and Gender Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to meet the needs of students interested in the history, theory, and cultural dimensions of women’s lives; gender as a social and cultural construction; feminist theory and methods; and the study of sexuality. The M.A. in Women’s and Gender Studies at UNT aims to prepare students for professional work as well as for further graduate study. It trains students in research skills, including critical and theoretical analysis, qualitative and quantitative methodologies, and the ethical issues involved in humanistic and social scientific scholarship. By emphasizing an interdisciplinary approach, students learn to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to issues affecting women and gender in diverse contexts and to translate theory into practice for professional and personal development. The M.A. in Women’s and Gender Studies program will enhance students’ understanding of the historical and cross-cultural constructions of gender and sexuality, enable them to apply feminist theoretical approaches and methodologies to a range of research topics, and prepare them to be successful in a diverse array of professional fields.

Requirements: Our holistic admissions process reviews each candidate’s entire application to assess academic abilities, professional accomplishments, leadership potential, and personal qualities. Every part of your application provides valuable insights into your qualifications, and we encourage you to spend time preparing each component. Requirements: Students applying for the accelerated online MBA in Business Analytics program must have earned a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution and have at least 24 months of full-time, professional work experience. Official transcripts from ALL colleges and universities attended. Complete the graduate school application online at applytexas.org.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description:
Advance your career with an online MBA from the University of North Texas. Our 36-credit online Master of Business Administration with a concentration in Business Analytics gives you the tools to succeed in today’s evolving data economy. The curriculum is designed to help you become a business leader who understands how to apply analytical methods and tools to derive actionable insights from business data.
Upon completion of the MBA in Business Analytics, you will be able to:
* Analyze business problems and formulate solutions by applying a variety of analytics tools and techniques.
* Communicate analytical findings clearly and concisely, orally and in writing, to business professionals.
* Lead business organizations and teams in developing and implementing data analytics strategies.
* Demonstrate awareness of ethical and societal issues related to the use of business analytics.

The UNT MBA combines the traditional rigor of a master of business administration degree with innovative, current business practices focusing on data analytics and critical thinking. The program prepares students to meet the challenges of an evolving global economy with a variety of specialized concentration options to meet individual career goals. This program is offered completely online or in a face-to-face format.
Accredidation: The UNT G. Brint Ryan College of Business is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Education in Counseling
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Education in Counseling program requires students to meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Education and Human Development and the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to these general requirements, applicants must also meet the following program requirements:

*   Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   Have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in previous graduate coursework.
*   Submit scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE), taken within the last five years.
*   Submit a two-page, double-spaced essay discussing career goals and professional experiences.
*   Submit three letters of recommendation with at least two from a faculty member and one from a supervisor in a professional setting.
*   Submit a resume or curriculum vita (CV) that highlights relevant experience.
*   Complete an interview with the admissions committee.

Department: College of Education
Description: As a student in the Master of Education in Counseling program, you'll gain the skills and experience necessary to work as a professional counselor in a variety of settings. The program is designed to meet the growing demand for qualified counselors in schools and other organizations. Our Council for the Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited Master of Education in Counseling program offers the School Counseling specialization. This specialization prepares students to work as school counselors in K-12 settings. In addition, students in the School Counseling program meet the academic requirements for the Licensed Professional Counselor credential in Texas.
Accredidation: Council for the Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited

ProgramName: Master of Education in Curriculum and Instruction

ProgramName: Master of Education in Educational Leadership
Requirements: The following materials should be submitted as part of your online application: Official Transcripts; GRE test scores (optional based on GPA); Upload a current resume or vita.; Upload a personal statement describing career goals, relevant experience, and reasons for pursuing a master’s degree in educational leadership.; A copy of your valid teaching certificate.; Letter of recommendation from your current supervisor or principal.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Educational Leadership degree is designed for students who desire leadership positions in schools, school districts and other educational agencies. The program is committed to preparing high quality school leaders to serve as principals, assistant principals and other administrative positions. The program leads to principal certification if required state examinations are passed and all other certification requirements are met. The program prepares students to meet requirements for Texas principal certification, including the Texas Principal as Instructional Leader certification exam.
ScholarshipType: Dean's Excellence Scholarships, Doctoral Fellowships, Master's Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships/Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Education in Higher Education
Requirements: All applicants must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to the Graduate School requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants may be admitted to the program provisionally or conditionally while completing remaining undergraduate coursework, not to exceed 12 hours. Provisional/conditional admission requires a minimum GPA of 2.8 and approval of the program coordinator. Full admission requires a minimum GPA of 3.0. Three letters of recommendation are required from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic and/or professional potential. Letters of recommendation must be submitted through the ApplyTexas online application system. Admission to the program is competitive. Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Higher Education provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work in a variety of higher education settings, including colleges and universities. The program prepares students for professional positions in areas such as student affairs, academic advising, admissions, alumni relations, institutional research, and administration. The program also serves as excellent preparation for doctoral studies in higher education.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships, Fellowships, External Scholarships, Travel Grants, Financial Aid

ProgramName: Master of Education in Special Education
Requirements: In addition to the Graduate School admission requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Hold a bachelor’s degree. Have a minimum 2.8 undergraduate GPA or a 3.0 GPA on the last 60 undergraduate hours. If GPA is less than 2.8, must submit GRE scores. Have a valid Texas Teacher Certification in Special Education EC-12 (preferred but not required). Submit a professional resume/CV. Submit an essay (statement of purpose) clearly articulating your purpose for pursuing a master’s degree in special education, including the relationship to your professional goals. Submit a signed copy of the Department of Educational Psychology’s Disclaimer Form. Provide three (3) letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of your academic ability and/or professional experience. Have a minimum of two years of teaching experience (preferred but not required). Interview with faculty.
Department: College of Education
Fees: Texas Resident: $3,242.67/Semester (for 9 credit hours, 2023-2024); Non-Resident: $8,561.67/Semester (for 9 credit hours, 2023-2024)

Concentration: High Incidence Disabilities, Low Incidence Disabilities
Description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Special Education with a concentration in either high-incidence or low-incidence disabilities prepares educators and related service professionals for advanced leadership positions in settings that serve individuals with disabilities from early childhood through adulthood. Our graduates become leaders as teachers, advocates, consultants, and policymakers in public and private schools, higher education, human services agencies, private organizations, and correctional facilities. We also prepare students who want to continue their studies in doctoral programs. The program offers thesis and non-thesis options. Each concentration has a unique curriculum with courses that provide advanced skills and knowledge of research-based practices for individuals with disabilities. The M.Ed. in Special Education provides the foundation for those who aspire to work in areas such as: Teacher leaders in K-12 public and private schools, Teacher of children and youth with disabilities, Teacher in adult education and post-secondary settings, Advocates in non-profit and parent organizations, Consultants in education and human service agencies, Policy makers in state and federal agencies, Graduate students in doctoral studies in special education or related fields.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: ~$360.30/credit hour (based on 9 credit hours, 2023-2024); Non-Resident: ~$951.30/credit hour (based on 9 credit hours, 2023-2024)
ScholarshipType: Dean's Fellowships, Tuition Awards (for TAs/RAs), Departmental Scholarships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Education in Teaching

A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential or professional experience. A personal statement (500 words maximum) indicating the applicant's reasons for pursuing graduate study in education. Current resume/curriculum vitae (CV) detailing educational background, work experience, volunteer activities, and any relevant achievements. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For international students, TOEFL/IELTS scores as required by the university.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Design with a concentration in Fashion Design
Requirements:

*   A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and a 3.0 GPA on any previous graduate work.
*   Submission of the following directly to the CVAD Graduate Office (cvadgrad@unt.edu):
    *   Statement of Purpose
    *   Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume
    *   Portfolio
    *   Three letters of recommendation
*   Optional: Scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). While optional, strong GRE scores can strengthen an application to the M.A. or M.F.A. in Design.

Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The MFA program in Design prepares students for careers as creative professionals, educators and leaders within a highly diverse range of fields. With courses ranging from traditional studio practice to emerging technologies, students learn to develop critical thinking, creative problem-solving and effective communication skills. A wide variety of research opportunities are available in topics such as user experience design, sustainability, cultural studies and new media.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Design with a concentration in Interior Design

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Documentary Production and Studies
Requirements: Apply to the Toulouse Graduate School through the ApplyTexas application. Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Transcripts must be sent directly to UNT from the issuing institution. The GRE is not required for admission. Submit three (3) letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability and potential for success in a graduate program. Submit a statement of purpose (2-3 pages, double-spaced) that addresses the following: why you are interested in the program, how you expect to benefit from it, what you believe you will contribute to the field, and your career goals. Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae (CV). Submit a portfolio of creative work. This can include: short films, documentaries, video art, photography, sound art, published articles, scripts, essays, research papers, etc. Please specify your role in all work submitted. If the work is collaborative, please explain your role and contributions.
Department: College of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Documentary Production and Studies program at the University of North Texas is designed to offer a unique, interdisciplinary approach to the practice and study of documentary. This three-year, 60-credit hour terminal degree will train a new generation of documentarians and scholars in both the creative and critical aspects of documentary, leading to careers as independent media makers, documentarians working within the media industry, and documentary scholars and teachers. Graduates will be prepared to produce, analyze, teach, and disseminate documentary in the 21st century. The program is specifically tailored to meet the needs of a diverse student population, including those with media production and/or academic backgrounds.
ScholarshipType: UNT Tuition Grants, Graduate Student Scholarships (GSS), Departmental Scholarships, Doctoral Fellowships, Assistantships (TA/RA)

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Studio Art
Requirements: You must submit a non-refundable application fee. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic and professional accomplishments are required. These are submitted directly by your recommenders through the online application portal. A statement of purpose outlining your goals, interests and reasons for pursuing an MFA in Studio Art is required. You must provide official transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended. A CV or Resume is required for your application to the MFA in Studio Art program. An artist statement (500 words maximum) is required describing your current artistic practice and interests. A portfolio is required and submitted through Slideroom.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The UNT Master of Fine Arts program in Studio Art is a rigorous studio-based curriculum that prepares students for professional careers as practicing artists. This program provides students with the opportunity to pursue advanced studies in ceramics, drawing and painting, new media, photography, printmaking, and sculpture.
