ProgramName: Master of Music in Performance
Requirements: Students applying to any of the graduate programs in the College of Music must have an undergraduate degree in music or its equivalent. Students must be fully admitted to The Graduate School AND the College of Music to pursue a graduate degree in music. Official transcripts must be submitted from all universities and colleges previously attended, including a bachelor’s degree in music. Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency. Two letters of recommendation from individuals able to assess your academic potential are required. An audition is required for all MM, DMA, and Performer’s Certificate applicants in Performance, including concentrations in Jazz Performance and Instrumental/Vocal Performance; contact the area for specifics.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Master of Music (MM) in Performance is a 30-credit-hour program offered through the College of Music. Students hone their skills in a chosen instrument, voice or conducting and deepen their knowledge of music history and theory. Graduate students prepare for careers as professional performers or college instructors. Many graduates go on to doctoral studies. Students may pursue a specialization in a number of areas including brass, guitar, harp, keyboard, organ, percussion, strings, voice and woodwinds. The UNT College of Music is one of the largest and most comprehensive music schools in the world and offers an unrivaled diversity of musical experiences and opportunities. With a faculty of more than 100 celebrated artists and scholars, and a student body of more than 1,600, UNT provides an ideal learning environment for talented musicians.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships, TGS Internal Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Music Education
Requirements: All graduate students applying to the University of North Texas College of Music must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School AND complete a College of Music Application. Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an institution accredited by a recognized U.S. accrediting agency or an equivalent international institution, with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (or the last 2 years) and in any previous graduate work. Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities are required. Three (3) letters of recommendation are required for all graduate applicants. For the Master of Music Education program, applicants must have completed an undergraduate degree in music education, or a bachelor’s degree in music with at least 15 semester hours of professional music education coursework and one year of successful teaching experience.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Master of Music Education (M.M.E.) degree is designed to enhance the professional competence of music teachers who wish to continue developing as scholars and practitioners. The M.M.E. degree is offered with thesis and non-thesis options. The M.M.E. can be completed entirely online. The online option for the M.M.E. is especially designed for professional music educators seeking to develop advanced skills in research, critical thinking, teaching, and musicianship.

ProgramName: Master of Public Administration (MPA)
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. These include: a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution, official transcripts from all institutions attended, and an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. Additionally, three letters of recommendation are required. International Applicants must meet additional requirements specific to international applicants, including English language proficiency as evidenced by an official TOEFL score of 79 on the internet-based test or an official IELTS score of 6.0 overall. The deadline for applications to the MPA program is February 1st for fall admissions and October 1st for spring admissions.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) degree prepares students for careers in public service and nonprofit management. Students develop leadership and management skills, analytical and decision-making abilities, and an understanding of public policy processes and implementation. The program emphasizes ethical practice and social equity in public service. The MPA program is housed within the Department of Public Administration, a part of the College of Health and Public Service at the University of North Texas.
Accredidation: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at the University of North Texas is fully accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).
ScholarshipAmount: Range from $1,000 to $5,000 per academic year

ProgramName: Master of Science in Accounting with a concentration in Audit and Data Analytics
Requirements: General Admission Requirements: Minimum GPA: 3.0. Upload your current resume or curriculum vitae (CV). Statement of Purpose. Three letters of recommendation. Official GRE or GMAT scores (optional, but encouraged). Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. International students may be required to submit a TOEFL or IELTS score. Departmental Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in accounting or an equivalent degree. Completion of undergraduate course work comparable to UNT's BBA in Accounting requirements with a grade of "B" or better. Satisfactory performance on the CPA exam's business environment and concepts section may substitute for certain prerequisite courses.
Department: College of Business
Description: The Department of Accounting offers a Master of Science in Accounting (M.S.) degree program designed for students who have completed an undergraduate degree and wish to continue their education in accounting. Our program is designed to provide students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary for successful careers in public accounting, industry, government, and not-for-profit organizations. The M.S. in Accounting offers two tracks: Audit and Data Analytics or Tax. Both tracks prepare students to meet the 150-hour education requirement for the CPA exam in Texas.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Accounting with a concentration in Corporate Accounting
Requirements: All applicants must meet the UNT Texas Graduate School admission requirements. Students seeking admission to the M.S. in Accounting program must submit the following materials directly to the Department of Accounting for review: Official GMAT scores (Minimum GMAT score of 500 required for full admission; Minimum GMAT score of 450 required for conditional admission), official academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, undergraduate grade point average (GPA) (Minimum 3.0 GPA for full admission; Minimum 2.8 GPA for conditional admission), a personal statement that describes your background, interests and goals regarding graduate study in accounting at UNT, as well as your career aspirations, a current resume, and two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic and professional accomplishments.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science in accounting offers two concentrations: Corporate Accounting and Taxation. This degree provides students with advanced study in accounting and business beyond the baccalaureate degree and helps prepare them to take a position as an accounting professional in industry, government or public accounting. For Texas residents, the degree helps satisfy the 150-semester hour educational requirement for certification as a Certified Public Accountant (CPA).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics
Requirements: You must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 undergraduate semester hours and in any previous graduate work. GRE is NOT REQUIRED. Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable about the applicant’s academic preparation and ability to succeed in graduate school. A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic objectives, professional goals, and reasons for pursuing the program. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Advanced Data Analytics is an interdisciplinary program designed to meet the growing need for data scientists and analysts in various sectors. The program provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to collect, process, analyze, and interpret large and complex datasets. Graduates of the program will be equipped to apply data-driven approaches to solve real-world problems, make informed decisions, and develop innovative solutions in fields such as business, healthcare, government, and scientific research. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, covering topics such as statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, big data technologies, and ethical considerations in data analytics. The program is suitable for students with diverse academic backgrounds, including computer science, statistics, mathematics, information science, and other quantitative disciplines.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Analytics Project Management
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science degree program in Advanced Data Analytics is contingent on admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and satisfaction of the following requirements:
*   Baccalaureate degree: An undergraduate degree in a related field from an accredited institution (e.g., business, computer science, economics, engineering, mathematics, statistics).
*   GPA: A minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a 3.0 GPA on previous graduate work.
*   Prerequisites: Completion of undergraduate courses in programming (e.g., Python, R, Java, C++, SAS, SQL), linear algebra, and statistics with a grade of B or better, or completion of equivalent graduate courses. Students without these prerequisites will be required to take them.
*   English Language Proficiency: International applicants must satisfy the UNT International Admissions English Language Proficiency requirements.
Additional materials required for all applicants:
1.  Resume: A current resume highlighting education, work experience, research, volunteer activities, and any relevant data analytics skills or projects.
2.  Statement of Purpose: A 750-1000 word statement explaining your interest in the Advanced Data Analytics program, your career goals, and how your academic and professional experiences have prepared you for success in the program.
3.  Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can assess your academic and/or professional capabilities and potential for success in a graduate program.
4.  Official Transcripts: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
5.  GRE/GMAT: Official GRE or GMAT scores. The GRE/GMAT requirement may be waived for eligible applicants.
Department: College of Information
Description:
The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics degree program is a STEM-designated, research-oriented program leading to the degree of Master of Science (MS). The program prepares students with knowledge, skills and abilities required to apply data science concepts and techniques to solve real-world problems. Graduates from the program will possess strong analytical skills and be able to effectively communicate with executives, managers, and data analysts across various domains. The program has concentrations in analytics project management, business analytics and health data analytics.
Analytics Project Management Concentration provides students with knowledge and skills to manage analytics projects by integrating business and analytics knowledge. The concentration covers data analytics methods, data analysis tools, project management techniques, and business communication skills. Graduates from the program will be able to manage various types of analytics projects from project initiation to project closure. They will also be able to communicate effectively with stakeholders and lead diverse project teams.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Dean's Scholarship, Doctoral Fellowship, Summer Research Fellowship, Dissertation Fellowship, Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantship, Service Assistantship, External Scholarships and Fellowships, College/Departmental Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Applied Artificial Intelligence
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics program with a concentration in Applied Artificial Intelligence, applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program-specific requirements: Official transcripts from all previously attended universities and colleges. A resume or curriculum vitae (CV). A statement of purpose (up to 750 words) that describes your academic interests, career goals, and how the program aligns with your aspirations. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field such as computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, economics, or a related discipline from an accredited institution. Applicants with degrees in other fields may be considered if they have a strong quantitative background, demonstrated by coursework in calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics. Prerequisite courses should include proficiency in at least one high-level programming language (e.g., Python, R, Java) and database concepts (e.g., SQL). A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale in the last 60 credit hours of undergraduate work and in any graduate work. GRE General Test scores are not required but may be submitted to strengthen the application. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit a satisfactory score on an approved English language proficiency test (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic, Duolingo, or other approved tests).
Department: College of Information
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Applied Artificial Intelligence is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students to contribute to the rapidly growing field of AI and data science. The program will enable students to gain the skills needed to collect, process, manage, analyze, and interpret large volumes of data and to leverage data to build intelligent systems with AI techniques and tools. The program is specifically tailored for those who want to advance or start a career in the field of data analytics and artificial intelligence. This program is offered by the College of Engineering. For more information, visit the departmental website.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Digital Retailing
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics program with a concentration in Digital Retailing prepares students to address the significant and increasing demand for data scientists with analytics expertise in the global retailing industry. Data scientists and data analysts are among the most sought-after professionals in the workforce, and this program builds on the strong foundation of the College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism to provide an in-depth understanding of the retail industry through the lens of data analytics. The curriculum focuses on critical and current issues in retailing, including e-commerce, digital marketing, supply chain and logistics, and consumer experience, providing students with advanced analytical skills to extract insights from complex data sets. Graduates will be equipped to identify, interpret, and present data-driven solutions to real-world business challenges in a global and fast-paced retail environment.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all undergraduate work or a 3.0 on the last 60 undergraduate hours. Applicants must demonstrate quantitative analytical ability. This can be met by: A GRE revised General Test score of 300 (verbal + quantitative) with a minimum of 150 on the quantitative portion. An undergraduate or graduate degree in a quantitative field such as mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, economics, or finance. At least three years of professional work experience in data analytics or a related quantitative field. Successfully completing a 3-credit graduate-level quantitative course (e.g., MATH 5000, CSCI 5000) with a grade of B or better. A statement of purpose outlining the student’s career goals and how the M.S. in Advanced Data Analytics will help them achieve those goals. A current resume or curriculum vitae highlighting professional, academic, and research experience. Three letters of recommendation are required from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic potential and/or professional competence.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) focuses on the principles and applications of advanced data analytics through the lens of GIS. This program is designed to provide students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary to analyze, interpret, and visualize complex spatial data using advanced analytical techniques and GIS software. Graduates will be prepared for careers in fields requiring expertise in spatial data science, geoinformatics, urban planning, environmental science, and public health, among others. The curriculum integrates core concepts of data analytics, statistics, machine learning, and data visualization with specialized courses in GIS, remote sensing, and spatial modeling. Students will engage in hands-on projects, case studies, and a culminating experience that applies their skills to real-world spatial data challenges.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Geospatial Intelligence
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the following general university requirements: An undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate proficiency in English.
And the following program requirements: GRE General Test (verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing scores) are required. GRE verbal score of at least 150. GRE quantitative score of at least 150. GRE analytical writing score of at least 3.0. Applicants with a master’s degree or higher from an accredited U.S. institution are exempt from the GRE requirement. Applicants with a 3.5 GPA or higher from an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited U.S. institution (with at least 60 credit hours) may be eligible for a waiver of the GRE. Waivers are not automatically granted and must be requested to the department for review. A Statement of Purpose. Three letters of recommendation. A current CV or Resume. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended.
Department: College of Engineering and College of Information
Description: The Master of Science degree in Advanced Data Analytics focuses on preparing students to become specialists in the rapidly expanding field of data analytics in a variety of industries. This program provides students with the critical skills needed to gather, process, and analyze complex data sets across multiple disciplines, to identify trends and patterns, and to communicate data-driven insights effectively. This curriculum is designed to produce students with a deep knowledge of the application of data analytics, including the ethical and social implications inherent in the use of data. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications through a rigorous curriculum that incorporates various tools and techniques such as statistical analysis, machine learning, data visualization, and predictive modeling.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Health Data Analytics
Requirements: Admission to the M.S. in Advanced Data Analytics program requires: An undergraduate degree with an adequate quantitative background in mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering or a related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all previous graduate coursework. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE), general test. Two letters of recommendation from faculty or professionals familiar with the applicant’s academic or professional capabilities. A statement of purpose of approximately 500 words describing the applicant’s career goals and how the M.S. in Advanced Data Analytics will help achieve these goals. A resume showing relevant professional experience, if applicable. English language proficiency requirement: International applicants must meet the English language proficiency requirements as stated by the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Admission to the Advanced Data Analytics program is a two-step process: Applicants must first meet the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, and then meet the specific requirements of the Advanced Data Analytics program. More information about how to apply can be found here: How to Apply
Department: College of Information, College of Engineering, and College of Science
Description: The Master of Science program in Advanced Data Analytics is an interdisciplinary program designed to meet the growing demand for professionals skilled in using data to make informed decisions across a variety of fields. Students gain a comprehensive understanding of data collection, storage, processing, analysis, interpretation, and visualization, along with the ethical considerations and privacy issues surrounding data. The program emphasizes the practical application of data analytics techniques and tools through hands-on projects and real-world case studies. Students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for success in data-driven careers. Students in the MS in Advanced Data Analytics program may choose from one of eight concentrations designed to provide specialized knowledge and skills in particular application areas.
ScholarshipType: Diversity Grants, Docking Doctoral and Master’s Student Fellowships, Emergency Aid, International and Study Abroad Grants, Outstanding Graduate Student Teaching and Service Awards, Ritch Scholarship, Toulouse Dissertation Fellowships, Graduate Assistantships (Teaching Fellow, Research Assistant, Teaching Assistant), Tuition Scholarships (for GAs)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Management
Requirements: To apply for the MS in Advanced Data Analytics, students should meet the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited university; Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities; An undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 credit hours of coursework completed; GRE/GMAT scores (Optional); A current professional resume outlining academic history, work experience, research, volunteer activities, and publications; A statement of purpose (500-1000 words) describing your academic background, career goals, and reasons for pursuing a master’s degree in data analytics at UNT; Letters of recommendation (Optional); English language proficiency for international applicants (TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE scores); Undergraduate coursework: Introduction to Programming (e.g., Python or R), Introduction to Statistics (e.g., BANA 3030 or equivalent), Calculus I (e.g., MATH 1710 or equivalent), Linear Algebra (e.g., MATH 2700 or equivalent).
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics provides students with the fundamental knowledge and advanced skills to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret large volumes of data. Graduates will be prepared to contribute to the analysis of complex data and to use data science principles to improve decision-making. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and hands-on experience using industry-standard tools and techniques. Students are trained to use a variety of programming languages, statistical software, and database systems. The program is designed to meet the growing demand for data scientists and analysts in a variety of industries. The program is offered fully online.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Sports
Requirements:
Students must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements:
*   A bachelor's degree in an analytical field such as mathematics, statistics, economics, engineering, computer science, business, or other closely related field.
*   A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
*   Successful completion of a college-level course in calculus and linear algebra with a grade of C or better.
*   Successful completion of a college-level course in statistics or probability with a grade of C or better.
*   Programming experience in a high-level language such as C++, Java, Python, R, or SAS is recommended.
*   GRE is waived for applicants who have:
    *   an earned graduate degree (Master's or Ph.D.) from an accredited institution located in the United States or
    *   a 3.5 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work or
    *   a 3.0 GPA for a UNT undergraduate degree.
*   All other applicants may request a GRE waiver if they demonstrate significant work experience involving data analytics.
Description: The Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics is designed to train students in the most current techniques for extracting knowledge from large data sets and to provide in-depth training in the latest industry-standard software and analytical methodologies. This degree can be completed entirely online. The M.S. in Advanced Data Analytics offers a concentration in Sports. This concentration prepares students to analyze data in the sports industry, from player performance to fan engagement, and to apply data-driven insights to strategic decision-making in sports organizations.
ScholarshipType: Academic Scholarships (Merit-based, Need-based), Assistantships (Teaching Fellow, Research Assistant, Teaching Assistant)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Statistics
Requirements: Applicants to the M.S. in Advanced Data Analytics with a concentration in Statistics are expected to have a strong undergraduate background in mathematics, statistics, computer science, or a related field. Specifically, applicants must have: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework. Prerequisites: Calculus I and II; Linear Algebra; Introduction to Programming (e.g., Python, R, Java); Introduction to Statistics (calculus-based preferred); Data Structures (preferred, but not required).
Department: College of Science
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Advanced Data Analytics program is designed for students seeking to develop advanced skills in the fields of business analytics, health analytics, applied analytics, and statistics. The program provides a strong foundation in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. The program prepares students for careers in fields such as data scientist, data analyst, business intelligence analyst, and analytics consultant. Students will learn to apply advanced statistical and machine learning techniques to real-world problems, interpret and communicate findings, and make data-driven decisions.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Behavior Analysis
Requirements: A minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 undergraduate hours of coursework. GRE scores are not required for admission. Three (3) letters of recommendation. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For international students, a TOEFL or IELTS score.
Department: Department of Psychology
Description: The Master of Science program in Applied Behavior Analysis trains students in the scientific principles of behavior and their application to a wide range of human behaviors, including autism and related disabilities, behavioral medicine, education, and organizational behavior management. Students will be prepared to work in a variety of settings, including schools, clinics, homes, and organizations. Graduates of the program are eligible to apply for certification as Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBA) by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board® (BACB®). As a student in the Applied Behavior Analysis master’s program, you’ll learn: About the principles and methods of behavior analysis, including behavioral assessment, intervention, and research. How to apply these principles to a variety of populations and settings. The ethical and professional standards of behavior analysis. The skills to design, implement, and evaluate behavior analytic interventions. About current research and literature in applied behavior analysis.
Accredidation: The Master of Science program in Applied Behavior Analysis at the University of North Texas includes a Verified Course Sequence (VCS) that meets the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) Examination. This VCS has been verified by the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI) and meets the requirements for eligibility to take the BCBA® Examination.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence
Requirements: Applicants must meet the Admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following requirements to be considered for admission to the master’s program in Artificial Intelligence. Departmental requirements include: * A bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a closely related field. Students with bachelor’s degrees in other fields (e.g., mathematics, physics, or other engineering disciplines) must have completed a minimum of 24 credit hours of undergraduate computer science courses including courses in data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and computer organization/architecture. * A minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. * Official GRE scores: A minimum of 153 on the verbal portion and 155 on the quantitative portion. The analytical writing portion is not used in the admission decision. * International applicants must also fulfill the English Language Proficiency requirements set by the Toulouse Graduate School. Refer to the Toulouse Graduate School website for more information.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence (MS in AI) is an interdisciplinary degree between Computer Science and Information Science. It prepares students for a career in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. The program gives students an in-depth understanding of theoretical and practical aspects of Artificial Intelligence. Graduates will be equipped to apply AI and Machine Learning techniques in various fields through data analytics, deep learning, natural language processing, intelligent agent development, and human-computer interaction. The program emphasizes the design, development, and application of artificial intelligence techniques for solving real-world problems. The MS in AI program focuses on cutting-edge topics that empower students with the skills and knowledge to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI professionals in industry, government, and research.
CostPerCredit: Approximately $644.44 (Texas Resident) to $1222.22 (Non-Resident) per credit hour
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships), Tuition Waivers, Fellowships (Presidential, Toulouse, Dissertation), Departmental Scholarships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Behavior Analysis
Requirements: Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for admission to a master’s degree program: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better on a 4.0 scale. The MS in Behavior Analysis program also requires applicants to submit the following materials directly to the Department of Behavior Analysis: 3 letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a current resume/curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Behavior Analysis at the University of North Texas is designed to provide graduate training in the experimental and applied analysis of behavior. The program helps prepare students for careers in research, teaching and practice (e.g., as Board Certified Behavior Analysts). Our program is designed for students who are interested in developing expertise in the application of behavioral principles to a wide variety of human behaviors (e.g., developmental disabilities, autism, education, child behavior, health & fitness, traumatic brain injury, organizational behavior management). As a result of this training, students will be qualified to enter various doctoral programs, teach at the university level, conduct research and work in a variety of settings applying the principles of behavior analysis. Students in the Master of Science in Behavior Analysis program will engage in course work, practicum experiences, and research that will result in the attainment of the following: Knowledge of the philosophical assumptions of behavior analysis, experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and professional practice. Skills in the experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and professional practice. Abilities to apply knowledge and skills in behavior analysis in professional and ethical ways.
Accredidation: The Association for Behavior Analysis International has verified the following courses toward the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® or Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst® examination. Applicants will need to meet additional requirements before they can be deemed eligible to take the examination.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships, Fellowships, Awards (Teaching, Service, Research), Travel Grants, Professional Development Grants

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Requirements: Students must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School along with the following program-specific requirements. All applicants are required to have: An undergraduate degree in Biochemistry, Biology, Chemistry, or a related field. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. A Statement of Purpose. Three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required.
Department: College of Science
Description: A Master of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from the University of North Texas will prepare you to be a skilled and innovative professional in a wide range of biology-related careers. You will perform research in modern laboratories and acquire skills in critical thinking, experimental design, scientific methodology, data analysis and interpretation, and oral and written communication of scientific concepts. This program will provide you with a solid foundation in biochemistry and molecular biology, along with a deep understanding of experimental principles and practices. You will gain experience in a variety of laboratory techniques and technologies, including protein purification, electrophoresis, chromatography, spectroscopy, cloning, DNA sequencing, PCR, cell culture, microscopy, and bioinformatics. Our graduates pursue diverse career paths in areas such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, clinical research, forensics, agriculture, environmental science, and government. Many also continue their education in Ph.D. programs or medical school.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $276.70 per credit hour (tuition only); Non-Resident: $726.70 per credit hour (tuition only)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biology
Requirements: Application to the Toulouse Graduate School requires several steps. For admission to the M.S. in Biology program, applicants must have: A bachelor's degree in Biology or a related field. A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all previous graduate work. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) should be submitted if the applicant's GPA is below 3.0. Official GRE scores are highly recommended for all applicants. International applicants must also meet the requirements for international admission. Prospective students are required to contact a faculty member whose research interests align with their own to discuss research opportunities and secure a faculty sponsor prior to applying to the program. A letter of support from the faculty sponsor should be uploaded with your application materials.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Master of Science (MS) degree in Biology. This program is designed to provide advanced training and research opportunities in various biological disciplines. Our faculty members conduct research in areas such as cell biology, developmental biology, ecology, evolution, microbiology, molecular biology, neurobiology, plant biology, physiology and zoology. The program prepares students for further graduate study toward a doctoral degree, for careers in research, industry or government, or for teaching positions. Thesis and non-thesis options are available, though the thesis option is strongly encouraged.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership-based, Talent-based, Departmental Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biology (Teaching in the Life Sciences)
Requirements: Graduate School Requirements: An undergraduate degree; GRE Scores: Verbal: 146, Quantitative: 144, Analytical: Not required; GPA: 3.0. Departmental Requirements: All applicants for the Biology (Teaching in the Life Sciences) M.S. degree must submit an application through the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to meeting the Graduate School general admission requirements, applicants must also submit the following to the Department of Biological Sciences (details will be sent to the applicant once their application is received by the department): Letter of intent; Official Transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities; Three letters of recommendation.
Department: College of Science
Description: This program is designed for current or prospective teachers of biology or related life sciences subjects at the secondary, community college or university levels. The curriculum for the M.S. degree in Biology (Teaching in the Life Sciences) includes course work in biology, biochemistry, science education, and research. Students can choose to complete either a thesis or a non-thesis option for the degree. This degree also has the flexibility to meet the needs of those seeking professional development or graduate work to meet their professional goals.
MinimumGreScore: 40th percentile on Verbal and Quantitative sections
ScholarshipAmount: Ranges from $500-$4,000 per semester (Graduate Tuition Scholarship); $15,000 (Toulouse Dissertation Fellowship); up to $750 (Travel Grants)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biology with a concentration in Computational Life Science
Requirements:
Graduate School Requirements (minimum)
* Bachelor's degree
* Undergraduate GPA of at least 2.8 for unconditional admission (or 3.0 on last 60 hours)
* Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for admission.
* International applicants: Evidence of English Language Proficiency (unless exempt) and Financial Certification. More information for international applicants.

Program Requirements
* The Biology Department prefers a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Applicants with a GPA below 3.0 are strongly encouraged to provide additional supporting documents beyond the minimum to demonstrate their ability to succeed in the graduate program (e.g., strong letters of recommendation, publication record, excellent GRE scores, etc.).
Department: College of Science
Description: The Master of Science in Biology provides students with advanced training in biology at the graduate level, encompassing a broad range of topics from molecular biology to ecology and evolution. Students gain in-depth knowledge and research experience through coursework, seminars, and thesis or dissertation research. The program prepares students for careers in research, education, industry, and further doctoral studies. Concentrations allow students to specialize in areas such as Computational Life Science, Forensic Science, or General Biology.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biology with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and the following program requirements: GPA of 3.0 or better in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours (excluding developmental coursework). Official GRE scores. There is no minimum score requirement; however, competitive applicants typically score in the 50th percentile or higher on the Verbal and Quantitative sections and 3.5 or higher on the Analytical Writing section. Statement of Purpose that includes specific details regarding the applicant's research interests, experience, and why they want to pursue the MS with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation degree at the University of North Texas. Three letters of recommendation submitted directly from the evaluator. Completed application to the Graduate School. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit a TOEFL score of at least 79 (internet-based) or an IELTS score of at least 6.5. This requirement may be waived for international applicants who have received a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an accredited institution in the United States or from a country where English is the official language. A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Science
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Biology with a concentration in Sub-Antarctic Biocultural Conservation is a joint program offered in collaboration with the University of Magallanes, Chile (UMAG) and the Millennium Institute of Ecology and Biogeography (IEB). The program is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and practical skills in biological and sociocultural conservation issues relevant to the Sub-Antarctic region. Students will engage in interdisciplinary coursework, research, and fieldwork, fostering a deep understanding of the unique ecosystems and cultural heritage of the Sub-Antarctic. The curriculum emphasizes a biocultural approach, integrating biological sciences with social sciences and humanities to address complex conservation challenges. Graduates will be prepared for careers in academia, research, non-governmental organizations, government agencies, and other institutions focused on conservation, sustainable development, and environmental policy in polar and sub-polar regions.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science program in Biomedical Engineering is open to qualified students holding a bachelor’s degree in engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Biomedical Engineering. Applicants must have: A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Official GRE general test scores. Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Three letters of recommendation. A personal statement describing background, interests and goals. A resume or curriculum vitae (CV). TOEFL/IELTS scores, if applicable. Additional requirements for international students (see International Admissions). Applicants with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0 may be considered for conditional admission. Please refer to the Toulouse Graduate School website for additional information.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering program prepares students to meet the growing need for highly qualified engineers in the medical device, biotechnology, and pharmaceutical industries. Students in the program will be exposed to coursework and research covering areas such as medical imaging, neural engineering, biomaterials, biomechanics, biomedical instrumentation, drug delivery, and computational biology. The program emphasizes both foundational biomedical engineering principles and practical applications through hands-on research and design projects. Graduates of the program will be well-prepared for advanced careers in industry, research, or further doctoral studies.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Business Analytics
Requirements: For unconditional admission to the master’s program in business analytics, applicants must satisfy the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and hold a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all work completed for a master’s degree. Students who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in a related field such as engineering, computer science, mathematics, statistics or business are eligible to apply. Applicants whose backgrounds are in other fields may be admitted after a review of their prior academic work. In addition to the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants must have a minimum GMAT score of 500 or a minimum GRE score of 300 (quantitative plus verbal). Applicants with a master’s degree from a U.S. accredited university may have the GMAT/GRE requirement waived. GMAT/GRE scores are waived for applicants with a terminal degree (Ph.D., M.D., J.D., etc.) from an accredited institution.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
CostPerCredit: Resident: $553.00 per credit hour (estimated for Fall 2024/Spring 2025, includes tuition and general fees); Non-Resident: $1,113.00 per credit hour (estimated for Fall 2024/Spring 2025, includes tuition and general fees)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Donor-specific criteria, Dean's Excellence Scholarships, Diversity Scholarships, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: Admission to the master's program is open to students with an undergraduate degree in chemistry from an accredited institution. Students with degrees in related fields may be admitted on a provisional basis with a requirement to complete undergraduate coursework as determined by the department. Applicants must satisfy the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following departmental requirements: Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 undergraduate hours and a 3.0 in undergraduate chemistry courses. A Graduate Record Examination (GRE) score report is required for unconditional admission. Applicants with exceptional academic records may be admitted conditionally without a GRE score if the undergraduate GPA is 3.5 or higher and 3.5 or higher in chemistry courses. GRE scores are good for 5 years. All applicants must submit two letters of recommendation. It is the applicant’s responsibility to contact their recommenders and request that the letters be sent to the department. All international students must satisfy TOEFL/IELTS requirements. For more information on the admission process, please contact the Graduate Advisor or consult the department website.
Department: College of Science
Description:
The Department of Chemistry offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. Graduate studies emphasize research that expands the understanding of all aspects of chemistry and its application to other fields of science.
The Master of Science in chemistry provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to pursue careers in industry, government, or academia, or to prepare for further doctoral study in chemistry or related fields. The program offers thesis and non-thesis options, allowing students to tailor their degree plan to their individual goals and interests. Students will develop a strong foundation in advanced chemical principles, laboratory techniques, and scientific communication.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must meet the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the College of Engineering. In addition to meeting the standard requirements, applicants must also provide: Official Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Résumé, and Three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are waived for admission. International applicants must meet the UNT international admission requirements.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The master’s degree in computer engineering prepares students for leadership roles in industry, government and education. Our multidisciplinary approach draws on the expertise of faculty in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Department of Electrical Engineering. This enables students to combine courses from both disciplines to tailor a master’s program that meets their career goals. You’ll gain knowledge and skills in areas such as computer architecture, digital system design, embedded systems, very large scale integration (VLSI) design, testing, computer networks, digital signal processing, distributed processing, network-on-chip, VLSI circuit design and data communication. As a student in the program, you’ll be able to participate in a variety of research projects. Many faculty members in computer engineering are conducting research in areas such as embedded and real-time systems, VLSI design, fault-tolerant computing, computer networks, wireless networks, network security, computer architecture and performance evaluation.
ScholarshipAmount: Ranging from $100 to $10,000 for one academic year.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements:
In addition to the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants for the Master of Science in Computer Science must meet the following requirements:
Applicants must provide official scores for the GRE General Test, taken within the last five years. There are no minimum GRE scores required for admission to the MS program. However, students who score below the 30th percentile on any of the three sections (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing) will be denied regular admission and will be subject to conditional admission, as described below, or denied admission.
Applicants for the Master of Science in Computer Science must hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in other fields may be admitted to the program on a conditional basis, with the condition being that they complete undergraduate foundation courses specified by the department and earn a minimum grade of B in each. The number of such courses will depend on the applicant’s background.
Applicants must have earned a minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
International students must satisfy the TOEFL requirement as stated in the Admission section of the Toulouse Graduate School catalog.
Department: College of Engineering
Description:
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering offers a Master of Science degree with a major in computer science. The program’s educational objectives are to prepare graduates to:

*   Obtain leadership positions in industry, government and academia through advanced knowledge and skills in computer science.
*   Become involved in lifelong learning as demonstrated by continued professional growth and development, including entrepreneurial pursuits.
*   Participate in professional activities ethically and responsibly.
*   Provide technical leadership in areas of professional practice.
*   Continue on to a Ph.D. program.
ScholarshipType: Dean's Graduate Fellowships, UNT Alumni Association Scholarships, External Scholarships, Departmental Scholarships, Assistantships (Research, Teaching, Graduate)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Counseling
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a 3.0 GPA on previous graduate coursework, is preferred. Applicants with a lower GPA may be conditionally admitted. Applicants must submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation. Applicants must submit a statement of purpose. Applicants must submit a resume/CV. Applicants must meet minimum admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. The GRE is not required for admission to the MS in Counseling Program.
Department: College of Education
Concentration: Clinical Mental Health Counseling, School Counseling, Play Therapy
Description: The UNT M.S. in Counseling program provides students with the academic and experiential knowledge and skills required for careers in a variety of settings. Students completing the program may become licensed professional counselors, school counselors, or registered play therapists in Texas. Our program is a Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling. We focus on preparing professional counselors who are grounded in theory, research, and best practices. As a student, you will have the opportunity to engage in meaningful scholarly discourse and fieldwork experiences within a supportive and collaborative environment.
Accredidation: Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Criminal Justice with a concentration in Justice Policy and Administration
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Barbra L. & G. Brint Ryan College of Business and for the Toulouse Graduate School and departmental requirements. Students must have satisfied the minimum course requirements for a major in criminal justice at UNT, or a related field (e.g., sociology, political science, psychology, public administration). Students with baccalaureate degrees in other fields (e.g., business, history) are encouraged to apply, but may be required to take up to 12 semester credit hours of undergraduate criminal justice courses (e.g., CJUS 3100, CJUS 3200, CJUS 3300, CJUS 3400) prior to being unconditionally admitted to the program. An applicant must have a 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work OR a combined verbal and quantitative GRE score of 290. All applicants must meet the UNT English Language Proficiency requirements as outlined on the UNT International Admissions website.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Master of Science in Criminal Justice provides students with an advanced education in the criminal justice field. The degree is designed to prepare students for careers in criminal justice, for doctoral studies in criminal justice or related fields, and for research positions in justice agencies and organizations. The concentration in Justice Policy and Administration prepares students for leadership and administrative positions in the criminal justice system. The concentration focuses on a variety of topics relevant to administration, policy, and evaluation, including personnel management, financial management, policy analysis and implementation, and program evaluation. Students will develop skills in critical thinking, research, and analysis to address complex issues in criminal justice administration and policy. The degree requires 30 semester hours of course work beyond the bachelor’s degree.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Criminal Justice with a concentration in Theory and Research
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Applicants for the Master of Science in Criminal Justice, Theory and Research Concentration, must submit the following materials directly to the Department of Criminal Justice through the UNT graduate school application portal: Official academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. All transcripts must be received by the Toulouse Graduate School prior to acceptance. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. Applicants must take the GRE within five years of the application date. The analytical writing portion of the GRE is not considered in the admission decision. A statement of purpose (1,000-1,500 words) addressing the following: Research interests, including a brief summary of a research problem the applicant would like to explore if admitted to the program. Explanation of how the applicant’s academic and/or professional background prepares them to successfully conduct graduate-level research. Explanation of how the applicant’s skills, experience, and research interests align with the program’s mission and faculty expertise. A current curriculum vitae (CV) or resume detailing prior education, academic/professional work experience, publications, presentations, and any research activities. A writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, a published article, or a research paper that demonstrates research and writing capabilities related to criminal justice. Letters of Recommendation (3) from individuals who can speak to the applicant’s academic and research abilities. At least two letters must be from academic sources.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Department of Criminal Justice offers graduate work leading to the Master of Science degree in Criminal Justice with concentrations in Cybercrime, Homeland Security, or Theory and Research. The program provides students with knowledge of the criminal justice system and the theoretical and empirical underpinnings of justice studies. Students pursuing the M.S. degree prepare for careers in various criminal justice agencies, for further study in a doctoral program, or for teaching positions in community colleges. The department is a part of the College of Health and Public Service.
MinimumGreScore: Combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 or higher and an analytical writing score of 4.0 or higher

ProgramName: Master of Science in Cybersecurity
Department: College of Engineering, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Fees: Texas Resident: $5,128.75/semester; Non-Resident: $10,391.75/semester (based on 9 SCH for FY2024 College of Engineering)
Fees.1: Texas Resident: $2,436.75/semester; Non-Resident: $7,706.25/semester (based on 9 SCH for FY2024 College of Engineering)
