ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Grants, Assistantships (Teaching, Research), Departmental Scholarships, Private Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Data Engineering
Requirements:
All applicants must meet the UNT Texas Graduate School admission requirements. Admission to the MS in Data Engineering program is competitive. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.

Applicants must also meet the following requirements:
*   A bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, information technology, computer engineering, or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with an undergraduate degree in other fields may be considered for conditional admission.
*   Undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
*   A Statement of Purpose
*   A Resume/CV
*   Three letters of recommendation
*   GRE General Test is required. International students who have a 4-year degree from a U.S. institution are exempt from the GRE. Also, if an applicant has a previous graduate degree from a U.S. institution, they are exempt from the GRE.
*   International applicants must also meet the graduate admission requirements for international applicants. This includes proof of English language proficiency. Please visit the UNT International page for more details.

Provisional Admission:
Applicants who do not meet all regular admission requirements but demonstrate potential for success in graduate study may be considered for provisional admission.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) program with a major in Data Engineering prepares students for careers as data engineers, data scientists and other related data-intensive professions in industry and government. Data engineering is a broad field of study at the intersection of computer science, data science, information science, and statistics focused on the acquisition, integration, management, and analysis of large volumes of data. The curriculum provides students with expertise in data analytics, data science, big data management, machine learning, and cloud computing. This is a STEM designated program.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Data Science
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science in Data Science program requires students to meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Admission to the Master of Science in Data Science program is a competitive process and is based on a holistic review of all application materials, including prior academic performance, professional and research experience, statement of purpose, and recommendation letters.
Department: Department of Information Science
Description: The Department of Information Science offers a Master of Science (MS) in Data Science program. This program is designed for individuals who want to develop strong theoretical and practical expertise in data science, including the skills needed to collect, store, retrieve, process, analyze, visualize and interpret large amounts of data. This interdisciplinary degree prepares students for a career as a data scientist, business intelligence analyst, machine learning engineer, data analyst, data architect and more, across various industries. Students will learn how to apply various data science methods and tools to derive valuable insights, create models and make decisions in real-world applications.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Design with a concentration in Interaction Design
Requirements:
Admission to the master's program in Design with concentrations in Communication Design, Design Research, or Interaction Design is determined by the faculty based on review of the following documents:
1. Official transcripts
2. Official GRE scores. There is no minimum score required, but competitive applicants typically score above the 50th percentile on the Verbal and Quantitative sections.
3. Statement of purpose. A statement outlining your reasons for pursuing graduate study, your research interests, and your career goals (2-3 pages recommended).
4. Portfolio. A portfolio of recent work (10-20 pieces submitted through an online service such as SlideRoom; detailed instructions will be provided after you apply).
5. Resume or curriculum vitae. A current resume or curriculum vitae outlining your education, work experience, accomplishments, and skills.
6. Three letters of recommendation.

Please note that this program does not accept applications for Spring or Summer admission. All applications are considered for Fall admission only. The application deadline for Fall admission is February 15. The admissions committee begins to review applications in late February. You will be notified of an admission decision by April 15.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design (Department of Design)
Description: Interaction Design focuses on designing interactive digital products, environments, systems, and services. Students learn to apply user-centered design principles and processes, develop prototypes, conduct user research, and evaluate user experiences. The curriculum covers areas such as usability, accessibility, information architecture, interface design, and emerging technologies. Graduates are prepared for careers as UX designers, product designers, interaction designers, and design researchers in various industries, including technology, healthcare, education, and entertainment.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships, TGS-Managed Departmental Scholarships), Research-based (Dissertation Completion Fellowship, Research Travel Grant), Professional Development Grants, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Digital Communication Analytics
Requirements:
UNT's accelerated online Master of Science in Digital Communication Analytics program is designed for students with or without a communication background, providing the skills to address organizational and societal communication challenges.

Application requirements for this program include:
*   Official transcripts: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
*   Statement of Purpose: A well-written, one-page personal statement describing your interest in the program and how it aligns with your career goals.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from academic or professional references who can speak to your abilities and potential for success in a graduate program.
*   Resume: A current resume highlighting your professional experience, academic achievements, and any relevant skills.
*   International Applicants: In addition to the above, international applicants must meet specific requirements regarding English language proficiency and financial certification. Refer to the UNT International Admissions website for more details.
Department: Frank W. and Sue Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: Digital communication analytics is a rapidly expanding field that explores how data informs, defines, and transforms communication strategy and practice in organizational and professional contexts. Through coursework rooted in communication, analytics, and business, you'll learn how to leverage social media data, web analytics, and other sources of information to enhance an organization's strategic communication efforts. Our online Master of Science (MS) in Digital Communication Analytics prepares students for leadership roles that require the ability to conduct, interpret, and apply advanced digital communication data analysis. Graduates emerge with a strong professional skill set that integrates theoretical knowledge with practical application. The MS in Digital Communication Analytics will empower you to collect and analyze complex data, generate actionable insights, and develop effective communication strategies for an evolving digital landscape.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Teaching assistantships, Research assistantships, Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Early Childhood Education
Requirements:
Admission to the master's degree program in Early Childhood Education is a two-step process. Students must be admitted to the Toulouse Graduate School and to the College of Education Early Childhood Education program.
Requirements for Admission to the Toulouse Graduate School:
Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants whose undergraduate degree is not in education or related areas may be required to take up to 12 semester hours of deficiency coursework related to education, as determined by the faculty advisor. Students must have a 3.0 grade point average (GPA) in the last 60 undergraduate semester hours. Applicants must submit a statement of intent to the department faculty. Students who do not meet the GPA requirement may be provisionally admitted if they submit a composite GRE score of 292 (verbal plus quantitative) with a 3.0 on the analytical writing portion (on the revised GRE) or a 950 composite score on the verbal and quantitative portions of the prior GRE and achieve a 3.0 GPA in the first 12 hours of graduate coursework.
Requirements for Admission to the Early Childhood Education Program:
Applicants must be admitted to the Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants for the M.S. in Early Childhood Education must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are required to submit a written essay that includes the following: Reasons for applying to the graduate program in Early Childhood Education; A brief biographical sketch; Professional and personal goals; How the graduate degree will help the applicant meet these goals; Future plans relative to the field; Applicant's strengths and weaknesses. Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation concerning academic and professional qualifications on the forms provided by the department. A personal interview may be requested by the program coordinator.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) with a major in Early Childhood Education (M.S. in ECE) provides advanced professional and scholarly studies in the education and development of young children. Through this program, students develop advanced knowledge and skills in evidence-based early childhood education, including early childhood curriculum, teaching, policy, and research. This program provides expertise in the development of young children from birth through age 8.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Tuition awards, Stipends, Doctoral Dissertation Completion Fellowship, Graduate Research Fellowship, Master’s Thesis Completion Fellowship, Texas Public Education Grants, Out-of-State Tuition Waivers

ProgramName: Master of Science in Economics
Requirements: Applying for admission to the UNT Economics M.S. degree requires a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit official transcripts, GRE scores (the general test verbal, quantitative and analytical sections are required), and three letters of recommendation to the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition, applicants should submit a statement of purpose outlining career goals, research interests, and why they want to pursue an M.S. in Economics at UNT. International applicants must also meet the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School for admission. International applicants whose native language is not English must provide proof of English proficiency by submitting scores from the TOEFL or IELTS examinations.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Fees: Resident: $4,980 - $6,370/Semester; Non-Resident: $10,140 - $13,570/Semester (based on 9-12 credit hours for 2023-2024)
Fees.1: Resident: $4,980 - $6,370/Semester; Non-Resident: $10,140 - $13,570/Semester (based on 9-12 credit hours for 2023-2024)
Description: The Master of Science in Economics program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in economic theory, econometrics, and quantitative methods. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers in both the public and private sectors, including roles as economists, data analysts, researchers, and consultants. The program also serves as excellent preparation for doctoral studies in economics or related fields. Our faculty members are active researchers dedicated to both teaching and advancing the frontiers of economic knowledge across a wide range of fields. The Department of Economics is committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment that encourages critical thinking, analytical rigor, and independent research.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships (stipend, tuition waivers, health insurance benefits)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Educational Psychology
Requirements:
Applications for admission to the Master of Science in Educational Psychology program are reviewed by the Department of Educational Psychology. In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants must meet the following program requirements:
*   A cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better from an accredited institution. Applicants with a GPA below 3.0 may be considered for probationary admission based on the program coordinator's recommendation.
*   A graduate GPA of 3.4 or better, if applicable.
*   Submission of official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) taken within the last five years. Scores for applicants with a GPA of 3.5 or higher (undergraduate or graduate) may be waived with the recommendation of the program coordinator.
*   Submission of a statement of purpose that explains the applicant’s interest in the field and the program, as well as career aspirations.
*   Submission of a current résumé or curriculum vitae.
*   Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable about the applicant’s academic abilities and potential for success in graduate school. Letters of recommendation are submitted electronically through the application system.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Master of Science in Educational Psychology program helps students understand how people learn and develop throughout their lives, focusing on the cognitive, social, and emotional factors that influence learning. Our program emphasizes the practical application of theory, research, and assessment methods to solve problems across diverse educational and developmental settings. The M.S. in Educational Psychology program offers both a thesis and non-thesis option for students interested in research, academia, or professional roles related to educational psychology. Graduates are prepared for careers in educational settings, research organizations, government agencies, and non-profit organizations. This program is offered completely online.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: General Admissions Requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution recognized by UNT, official transcripts from all higher education institutions attended, Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test Scores (Note: Many departments have specific requirements or waivers for the GRE. Check with your program for details.), proof of English Language Proficiency (for international applicants), application for Admission, and application fee.
Department: College of Engineering
Concentration: communication and signal processing, control systems, digital systems, electronic devices and circuits, electromagnetics, power systems
Description: The Master of Science program in Electrical Engineering provides students with an advanced background in either communication and signal processing, control systems, digital systems, electronic devices and circuits, electromagnetics, or power systems. The program provides advanced studies to students interested in careers in industry and government, or in continued studies leading to the PhD degree. The Department of Electrical Engineering offers thesis and non-thesis options for the M.S. degree.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Emergency Management and Disaster Science
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, as well as the following program-specific requirements:
Undergraduate degree: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
Undergraduate GPA: A minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
GRE: The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission.
Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation are required.
Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose is required.
Resume/CV: A resume or curriculum vitae (CV) is required.
Transcripts: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Additional requirements apply for international applicants, including English proficiency and financial certification.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Fees: Texas Resident: $6,377/Semester (based on 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $12,017/Semester (based on 9 credit hours)
Fees.1: Texas Resident: $6,377/Semester (based on 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $12,017/Semester (based on 9 credit hours)
Description: The Master of Science in Emergency Management and Disaster Science prepares students to be leaders and innovators in the emergency management and disaster fields. The degree is designed to prepare students for careers in complex and dynamic emergency environments, addressing the multi-disciplinary needs of organizations and communities. Students will gain knowledge in the latest theory and practice, including topics such as: social vulnerability to disaster, emergency planning, hazard mitigation, disaster response and recovery, public policy, and risk assessment.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships (e.g., Graduate Dean's, Terminal Degree, Toulouse Dissertation), Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Engineering Management
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science in Engineering Management (MSEM) program is offered through the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to the graduate school's general admission requirements, applicants must provide: Resume (or CV), Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Official GRE Scores (optional based on the applicant's academic history), and Official Transcripts (from all previously attended institutions).
Department: College of Engineering
Fees.1: Resident: $4,776/semester (for 9 credit hours); Non-Resident: $9,936/semester (for 9 credit hours)
Description: The Master of Science in Engineering Management provides students with a broad and in-depth education in the management of engineering and technical enterprises. The program is designed for engineers and other professionals with technical backgrounds to gain skills and knowledge in leadership, business strategy, project management, operations, and organizational behavior. It prepares graduates for management and leadership positions in technology-intensive organizations.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, College and Departmental, External

ProgramName: Master of Science in Environmental Science
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science program in Environmental Science requires a bachelor's degree in a natural science (e.g., biology, chemistry, geology, physics, geography), engineering (e.g., environmental, civil, mechanical, chemical), or closely related field (e.g., public health, public administration, business management) from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School, as well as the following program-specific requirements: Undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test (Verbal, Quantitative and Analytical Writing sections). The GRE will be waived for applicants with a GPA of 3.5 or higher on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose (one to two pages) addressing the applicant's interest in environmental science, career goals and research interests. A current résumé. International applicants must fulfill the same requirements as domestic applicants, with the following additions: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) scores, as required by the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Submission of official transcripts and degree certificates (if applicable) in both the original language and in English, along with professional evaluations, if applicable, to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Documentation of financial support.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Department of Environmental Science offers programs leading to the Master of Science degree (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy degree (Ph.D.) in Environmental Science. The Master of Science degree is designed to prepare graduates for careers in environmental assessment and management within a variety of governmental agencies, private companies and consulting firms. Students are required to complete a thesis for the M.S. degree. The Ph.D. degree is designed to prepare graduates for careers in academia, industry and government that require advanced research and analysis capabilities. A terminal M.S. degree is offered to students who do not desire to continue in the Ph.D. program. A student must maintain an overall 3.0 grade point average or better in all courses taken that count toward the degree.
ScholarshipAmount: $1,000 or $2,000 per semester (for Dean's Excellence Scholarships)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Finance
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Graduate School, including Official transcripts from all universities attended, as well as the following program-specific requirements. Program-specific requirements for the M.S. in Finance program: GMAT or GRE required. (For details on waivers, see the G. Brint Ryan College of Business website.) The applicant must have earned a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 2.8 GPA over the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA over the last 30 hours of undergraduate coursework. The applicant must have successfully completed prerequisite coursework, including calculus and statistics, and a minimum of 18 hours of business courses from an AACSB-accredited program, with a minimum 3.0 GPA in those courses. A Statement of Purpose, A Resume, Two letters of recommendation are required. (These can be waived in some cases.)
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science in Finance program provides advanced training in finance for students seeking careers in corporate finance, investment management, or risk management. The program is designed to provide students with the quantitative and analytical skills necessary to succeed in a dynamic global financial environment. The curriculum covers a broad range of financial topics, including financial modeling, valuation, portfolio management, risk management, and financial institutions. Graduates of the program are prepared for a variety of finance-related positions in corporations, financial institutions, and government agencies.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Research potential, Financial need

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geography
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School as well as the following departmental requirements: Baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework (exceptions may be granted). GRE Scores are no longer required for admission to the Master of Science in Geography program. Three letters of recommendation submitted directly from the evaluator. Statement of Purpose that describes academic interests and career goals. Resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: Our Master of Science program offers students the opportunity for advanced study in theoretical and applied geography. Graduates of our program are well prepared for careers in fields such as GIS, remote sensing, environmental management, urban and regional planning, and other areas where geographic skills are in demand. Many of our graduates also continue their education in doctoral programs. Thesis and non-thesis options are available in our programs.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships, Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geography with a Concentration in Data Analytics
Requirements: Admission to the master's program in Geography is based on the following: A bachelor's degree in geography or a related field (e.g., environmental science, political science, computer science, urban planning, geology) from an accredited institution. Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework and in any previous graduate coursework. Submission of all required documents to the Toulouse Graduate School by the stated deadlines. Applicants are required to submit an online application through ApplyTexas (applytexas.org) or the Common App along with the application fee. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic and professional capabilities. Statement of Purpose: An essay (1-2 pages) describing the applicant's academic and professional background, research interests, and career goals, specifically addressing how the M.S. in Geography aligns with these aspirations. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating relevant academic, professional, and research experience. GRE Scores (optional): While not required, applicants may submit GRE scores to support their application. Strong GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) can enhance an application, especially for those with GPAs slightly below the recommended minimum or limited academic experience in geography or related fields. For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test) is required. Specific score requirements can be found on the Toulouse Graduate School website.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Geography master's program offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree with thesis or non-thesis options and a concentration in data analytics. The program prepares students for professional careers and doctoral studies. Our curriculum emphasizes the acquisition of knowledge in theoretical geography, quantitative methods, and geographic information science (GISc), with applications to a variety of human and physical geography topics. Students learn to apply geographic concepts, theories, and methods to interpret spatial patterns and processes. Our graduates have pursued careers in fields such as GIS and remote sensing, data science, environmental management, urban and regional planning, and international development, as well as positions in government agencies, non-profits, and private industry.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Geography with a Concentration in Technical Communication
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in geography or a related field; minimum 3.0 GPA for the last 60 undergraduate hours. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Official GRE scores. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose regarding your interest in the program and career goals. A writing sample (10-15 pages). A resume/CV. Contact the department prior to applying.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Geography offers a flexible course of study and a variety of concentration areas. The graduate program provides rigorous training in geographic theory and methods and opportunities for students to apply this training to problems related to spatial analysis, environmental geography, and human-environment interactions. Students completing the MS in Geography will be well-prepared for a variety of careers in government, nonprofit, and private sectors; and for Ph.D. studies in Geography or related fields.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Data Analytics
Requirements: Admission to the M.S. in Health Data Analytics program is a two-step process. First, apply to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Second, apply to the Department of Biological Sciences. To apply for the M.S. in Health Data Analytics, you will need to meet the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. One official transcript from each institution previously attended. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose (500 words or less). A resume or curriculum vitae. International applicants have additional requirements.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Fees: ~$12,000 - $15,000/Year (in-state estimate for most online graduate programs)
Description: The Master of Science in Health Data Analytics at the University of North Texas equips students with critical data science and analytics skills while developing a deeper understanding of the processes and operations within the healthcare system. With courses in health informatics, data analytics, and statistics, students will learn to derive insights from health data and apply them to healthcare challenges. This program offers practical skills for working with big data, including advanced statistical analysis, machine learning, deep learning, data visualization, and information technology relevant to the healthcare industry. Our curriculum is designed to prepare students to advance their careers and become leaders in the rapidly growing field of health data analytics.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Informatics
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School. Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 undergraduate hours. No GRE requirement for admission to the M.S. in Health Informatics program. International students must meet the English Language Proficiency requirements. Statement of Purpose. 3 Letters of Recommendation. Resume/Vita.
Department: College of Engineering, College of Health and Public Service
Description: The graduate program in Health Informatics provides an interdisciplinary approach to the design, development, and application of technology to improve patient care, enhance health care delivery, and improve population health. The master's program focuses on the core areas of health informatics including: health data analysis, health information systems, health care delivery systems, and health care policy. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to become successful health informatics professionals in a variety of settings, including hospitals, clinics, public health agencies, and research institutions. The program offers both thesis and non-thesis options.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Services Administration
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) program in Health Services Administration (HSA) prepares students to become leaders in healthcare organizations and related enterprises. This program prepares students for positions in various healthcare organizations and settings. Students acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to contribute to the efficient and effective delivery of high-quality, accessible and affordable healthcare. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in healthcare management, economics, finance, policy, law, ethics, marketing, human resources and information systems. The program provides the knowledge and skills necessary to succeed in a dynamic and challenging healthcare environment. Graduates are prepared for careers as administrators, managers, and policy analysts in hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, public health agencies, and other healthcare organizations. The HSA program provides students with the opportunity to specialize in a particular area of healthcare administration through their internship and capstone project. In addition, the HSA program prepares students for doctoral study in health services research, health policy, or other related fields.
ScholarshipType: Diversity Scholarships, Recruitment Scholarships, Retention Scholarships, Dissertation Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Hospitality and Tourism Data Analytics
Requirements: An undergraduate degree from an accredited institution in hospitality management, business, science, technology, engineering, mathematics, or related fields. International applicants must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores, if the applicant's cumulative GPA is below 3.0. CV/Resume. Statement of Purpose. Two letters of recommendation from former professors or supervisors. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Concentration: Digital Hospitality and Tourism Management, Revenue Management and Analytics
Description: The M.S. in Hospitality and Tourism Data Analytics program at UNT prepares students for advanced careers in the rapidly growing fields of hospitality, tourism, and data analytics. Students gain expertise in data-driven decision-making, predictive analytics, revenue management, digital marketing, and strategic management through a comprehensive curriculum. The program caters to individuals seeking to lead in the digital transformation of the hospitality and tourism industry, offering a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical application. This program prepares graduates to thrive in an era where data-driven insights are paramount. Graduates are equipped with skills in data interpretation, strategic forecasting, and digital innovation, making them highly sought after in various sectors of the hospitality and tourism industry.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $1,100.50/credit hour (for 1 SCH); Non-Resident: $1,558.50/credit hour (for 1 SCH)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Hospitality Management
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work is required; lower GPA applicants may be conditionally admitted based on a holistic review of all application materials. Required documents include three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose outlining academic and professional goals, a current resume or curriculum vitae (CV) detailing academic and professional experience, and official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. The GRE or GMAT is not required for admission. Additional requirements apply for international applicants, including English proficiency scores.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Department of Hospitality and Tourism Management offers a Master of Science (M.S.) in Hospitality Management. The Hospitality Management M.S. program is designed to educate and develop professionals, educators, and scholars for diverse career opportunities in the hospitality and tourism industry. The program provides the necessary knowledge and skills for managing the human resources, financial, technological, and service challenges facing the global hospitality and tourism industry, as well as for further doctoral studies.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Hospitality Management (online)
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition, applicants must meet the following program-specific requirements:
*   A bachelor’s degree in hospitality management or a closely related field.
*   A GPA of at least 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework.
*   Submission of official GRE or GMAT scores. (While GRE/GMAT scores are normally required, the Department of Hospitality and Tourism Management will review exceptional applications without a GRE/GMAT score, or waive the GRE/GMAT requirement, if the applicant has extensive work experience in the hospitality industry (5+ years in a management position).)
*   A statement of purpose (written essay – 250 to 500 words in length) describing the applicant’s professional goals and how the M.S. in Hospitality Management program will help achieve those goals.
*   A current professional resume or CV.

The MSLS degree prepares students to serve as leaders and innovators in an evolving information society. With an emphasis on information literacy, access, and service, the MSLS program ensures graduates are well-equipped to address the challenges and opportunities of the 21st century information professional. If an applicant’s GPA is less than a 3.0, the GRE general test is required, and the applicant must score a minimum of 300 on the combined verbal and quantitative sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing portion. Applicants must submit a statement of purpose, written in English, of not more than 500 words. The statement should address the applicant’s interest in the field of library and information science; his or her career goals; and how the MS in Library Science program at the University of North Texas will help in achieving those goals. Description: The Master of Science in Library Science (MSLS) degree is designed for those who want to prepare for careers as information professionals in the evolving information environment of the 21st century. The program focuses on the management, organization, preservation, and retrieval of information and knowledge, as well as on leadership and services in libraries and other information agencies. The coursework provides students with the foundational principles and practices of the library and information professions. The program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), the national accrediting agency for master’s programs in library and information science in the United States and Canada. Students in this program are eligible for multiple specializations that include Archives and Records Management, Children's and Young Adult Librarianship, Information Organization, Law Librarianship, Music Librarianship and School Librarianship.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), the national accrediting agency for master’s programs in library and information science in the United States and Canada.

The program emphasizes an understanding of the legal system and how information professionals support legal practice and research. The concentration prepares students to lead and innovate in the evolving landscape of legal information and technology.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Linguistics
Requirements: A master's degree in linguistics, either the M.A. or the M.S., requires prior preparation equivalent to an undergraduate minor in linguistics. Applicants are expected to be familiar with the fundamentals of linguistic analysis at the advanced undergraduate level, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and historical linguistics. In addition, applicants are required to submit the following materials directly to the Department of Linguistics: Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose indicating the applicant’s academic interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in linguistics. A writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to conduct scholarly research and write clearly and analytically. Official transcripts from all universities attended. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores, if available. (Note: GRE scores are not required for admission to the MA/MS in Linguistics programs). Additional requirements for international students can be found here.
Description: The Department of Linguistics offers a Master of Science degree in Linguistics. This degree program is designed to provide graduate training in linguistic analysis and theory, as well as in the various subfields of linguistics. Our program offers excellent training in core linguistic areas and in more specialized areas such as computational linguistics, field linguistics, and language documentation, second language acquisition, and corpus linguistics. As a graduate student, you will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty mentors, develop your own research interests, and contribute to the vibrant intellectual life of our department.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in Computational Linguistics
Requirements: Departmental requirements include: A GRE score on the verbal and quantitative sections that averages in the 50th percentile or above (or satisfactory performance on a comparable graduate entrance examination); the analytical writing section is not a factor in admission. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Applicants are expected to have completed coursework in linguistics (e.g., phonetics, phonology, syntax) and computer science (e.g., programming) or have equivalent experience prior to admission. Students who lack sufficient background in linguistics or computer science may be admitted to the program but will be required to complete specified undergraduate courses as prerequisites to graduate-level courses. These prerequisite courses will not count toward the Master’s degree. International students must satisfy all UNT international admission requirements.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Computational Linguistics (M.S.) focuses on a multidisciplinary approach to the automatic processing of human language, drawing on the fields of linguistics, computer science, and library and information sciences. Students receive a thorough grounding in all aspects of linguistic science and computational analysis as it applies to natural language. Students will become familiar with current trends in computational linguistics and apply computational linguistic techniques in courses within the Department of Linguistics, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, and the Department of Information Science. Additionally, students gain experience with a wide variety of tools and methodologies and develop the skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate solutions for a wide range of problems involving natural language. The program prepares students for careers in industry (e.g., text analytics, natural language processing, data science, language technology development) and for continued graduate study at the doctoral level.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in English as a Second Language (ESL)

Students completing the MS can also use this degree to springboard to other professional programs (e.g., law, computational linguistics, language documentation). The concentration in English as a Second Language (ESL) is ideal for those planning to teach ESL in the US or abroad, or for those who wish to pursue careers in ESL material development or curriculum design. The ESL concentration provides students with theoretical and practical training for careers as ESL teachers and specialists. Our program prepares students for positions in public and private language institutes, adult education programs, and community colleges.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in Language Documentation
Requirements: Baccalaureate Degree: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. GRE: The GRE is not required for admission. GPA: A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) describing your academic and research interests and how they align with the program's faculty and resources. Writing Sample: A writing sample (e.g., a term paper, essay, or published article) demonstrating your analytical and writing abilities, preferably on a linguistic topic. Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic abilities and potential for graduate study. Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume: A current CV or resume detailing your academic history, relevant work experience, research, publications, presentations, and any other pertinent information. English Language Proficiency: For international applicants, official scores from TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test (DET) may be required.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Department of Linguistics offers both a Master of Arts (M.A.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) in Linguistics. Within the M.A. and M.S. degrees, students can choose to pursue concentrations in Computational Linguistics, Language Documentation, or TESOL. The M.A. degree provides students with a broad knowledge of language and linguistics and prepares them to teach English as a second language, teach linguistics at a community college, or pursue further graduate work in linguistics. The M.S. degree is similar to the M.A., but it also provides students with a stronger background in quantitative methods and prepares them for careers in language-related industries, such as computational linguistics, natural language processing, or language documentation. Students are required to take a set of core courses, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Students will also complete a capstone project that allows them to apply their knowledge to a real-world problem or research question. The M.A. and M.S. in Linguistics degrees are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in linguistic theory and methods, as well as opportunities for specialized study in areas such as computational linguistics, language documentation, and TESOL. Students will develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills, preparing them for diverse careers or further academic pursuits.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering

The MS in Materials Science and Engineering is designed to prepare graduates to fill important industry and research needs. Students will focus on developing advanced knowledge and skills in the processing, structure, properties, and performance of materials, as well as the relationships between these elements. Our graduates will be able to apply advanced materials science and engineering principles to solve problems, develop new materials, and advance technologies in various fields.
The MS in Materials Science and Engineering prepares students for careers in research and development, materials production, process engineering, quality control, and management in industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and biomedical. The program provides a strong foundation for those who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering or related fields.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mathematics with a Concentration in Mathematics Education
Requirements:
Admission to the Mathematics (M.S.) program with a Mathematics Education Concentration is a two-step process:

Step 1: Apply to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School
All students must complete the application for admission to graduate school at UNT.

Requirements for ALL graduate applicants include:
*   Official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended.
*   GRE Scores (Verbal and Quantitative portions are required). Scores must be dated within five years of the application date. While there is no official minimum GRE score required, applicants whose scores are below the 30th percentile on either the Verbal or Quantitative portions will be expected to demonstrate appropriate academic ability.

Step 2: Apply to the Department of Mathematics
In addition to the requirements for graduate school, all applicants to the Mathematics (M.S.) program with a Mathematics Education Concentration must submit the following directly to the Department of Mathematics:
*   A Statement of Purpose – Must outline the applicant’s academic and professional goals and how the M.S. in Mathematics with a Mathematics Education Concentration will help the applicant achieve those goals.
*   Three letters of recommendation – At least two of which must be from faculty who can speak to the applicant’s academic potential.

Description: The Mathematics Education Concentration is designed for students who want to continue their study of mathematics and mathematics education beyond the undergraduate level. The program is specifically designed to prepare students for teaching mathematics in high schools and community colleges, for positions as mathematics specialists, and for further graduate study in mathematics education at the doctoral level. Students will gain advanced knowledge in a variety of mathematical topics. In addition, students will learn to apply research-based pedagogical content knowledge in teaching mathematics effectively. They will also learn about current issues, trends and research in mathematics education. Our graduate courses are offered in a flexible format, with opportunities for students to study face-to-face, online or in a blended fashion. Many of our courses are offered at convenient evening hours, making it possible for students who work full-time to complete the program. Students may complete the degree entirely online as well.

The MS program focuses on advanced topics in Mechanical and Energy Engineering and prepares students for careers in industry, government, or academia. Students can specialize in areas such as materials and manufacturing, thermal-fluid sciences, dynamics and controls, and energy systems. The program provides a strong theoretical foundation coupled with practical applications and research opportunities. Graduates will be equipped to tackle complex engineering challenges and contribute to innovative solutions in their chosen fields.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Merchandising and Consumer Analytics

Students will learn how to analyze consumer behavior, market trends, and retail data to develop effective merchandising strategies. The curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications, preparing graduates to excel in diverse roles within the retail, fashion, and consumer goods sectors.

Requirements: A current résumé or CV, a statement of purpose, transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, and three letters of recommendation are required. Graduates are prepared for careers in merchandising, retail management, supply chain management and digital retailing, as well as for doctoral study. A thesis option is available.

A written personal statement outlining the applicant’s educational and career objectives and how the PSM program will help achieve those objectives.

Description: The Professional Science Master’s (PSM) option in Biology, administered by the Department of Biological Sciences, combines advanced biological sciences training with marketable skills in the areas of business, communication, and project management to prepare students for leadership roles in science-related professions. The program emphasizes an internship-based, problem-solving approach to develop professionals with the scientific knowledge and business acumen to succeed in the workplace. This program is offered to students who hold a bachelor’s degree in a science field or a related area.

Admission to the PSM program requires a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry or a related field. Students should have completed a year of general chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry and physical chemistry. The department may require a student to take additional courses as prerequisites if they do not have sufficient background.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Professional Science Master's (PSM) degree option with a major in Chemistry is a non-thesis, interdisciplinary master's degree program designed to provide students with advanced training in chemistry while simultaneously developing highly valued business and professional skills required for successful careers in industrial or governmental settings. The PSM program is designed to meet the growing need for talented scientists who also possess professional skills in communication, management, and regulatory affairs.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling
Requirements: UNT's College of Health and Public Service and Toulouse Graduate School require applicants to meet the following criteria: A bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution, undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher, and GRE and/or other admission exams are not required. Specific application requirements for this program are listed below: Submit all official transcripts, a personal statement/statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum) indicating your interest in rehabilitation counseling as a profession and your professional goals, three letters of recommendation addressing your potential for success in a graduate program, your professional experience, and your ability to work with diverse populations, a resume or vita that demonstrates work and volunteer experience in human service, rehabilitation, or related fields, and successful completion of an interview with program faculty.

Graduates work as rehabilitation counselors in a variety of public and private settings, including state and federal vocational rehabilitation agencies, community rehabilitation programs, hospitals, mental health programs, supported employment programs, private practice, and insurance companies. This online program will equip you with the skills to address the social, psychological, and vocational impact of disabilities on individuals and their families. Throughout the UNT M.S. in Rehabilitation Counseling program, you will develop a deep understanding of disabilities and their impact, as well as the counseling techniques to support individuals in achieving their goals. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including: Disability and rehabilitation, Counseling theories and techniques, Assessment and evaluation, Vocational rehabilitation, Case management, Ethical and legal issues in rehabilitation, Group counseling, Family counseling, Career development, Research and program evaluation.
