Applicants who have earned a master’s degree from an accredited institution in an engineering or closely related field are exempt from the GRE requirement.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science (MS) program in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering (SME) is designed to educate students on fundamental principles and knowledge pertaining to semiconductor manufacturing process integration, device and circuit design, and manufacturing and industrial engineering. Students will gain knowledge in semiconductor manufacturing processes, semiconductor device physics, process control, cleanroom operations, testing and reliability, and the economics of manufacturing, and will learn to apply these principles to solve complex problems in the semiconductor industry. The semiconductor manufacturing industry has been expanding at a rapid pace and is expected to continue this growth for decades. The US CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 provides billions in funding for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and R&D, creating a need for a highly skilled workforce across the entire supply chain. Graduates of this program will be prepared to fill critical roles in semiconductor manufacturing, research and development, and management within the semiconductor industry, contributing to the economic growth of the DFW metroplex, the state of Texas, and the nation.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Social Work (MSW)
Requirements:
Admission to the MSW program is limited to applicants who show promise for successful graduate study and and professional social work practice. The admissions committee reviews all applications submitted to the program. An applicant must submit an application packet directly to the Department of Social Work as well as an application to the Toulouse Graduate School (TGS).
TGS Application Packet Requirements:
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended.
A Statement of Purpose (no more than three double-spaced pages describing your interest in social work, experience, and professional goals).
Resume/vita outlining academic background, paid and volunteer work experience, and any professional or community service.
Three letters of recommendation (at least two should be academic or professional; letters from friends/family will not be accepted).
GRE General Test scores if undergraduate GPA is below 3.0.
Department Application Packet Requirements:
A Social Work Addendum Application (available at socialwork.unt.edu).
A writing sample is not required for admission.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Concentration: Direct Practice with Families and Children, Administrative and Community Practice
Description: The Master of Science in Social Work (MSW) program at the University of North Texas is a nationally accredited program designed to prepare students for advanced social work practice. The UNT MSW Program is a generalist curriculum with concentrations in Direct Practice with Families and Children, and Administrative and Community Practice. The program offers face-to-face and online options. Students can enroll full-time or part-time. The program prepares students for leadership in multiple practice settings. MSW graduates may choose to become licensed social workers in Texas (LMSW and LCSW).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Sociology
Requirements:
Applicants for the M.S. and Ph.D. programs should apply through the Toulouse Graduate School. Application details and deadlines are available at the Toulouse Graduate School Application webpage. Additional materials, such as those listed below, should be submitted electronically through the Toulouse Graduate School’s online application system.

Official Transcripts: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Applicants must have completed a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.

Three Letters of Recommendation: Sent from academic faculty members or others who can evaluate the applicant’s potential for success in graduate school.

International Student Applicants: All international applicants must meet the UNT international admission requirements found on the Toulouse Graduate School website. Additionally, international students must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores according to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School Requirements.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Department of Sociology offers the Master of Science degree in Sociology. The M.S. program is designed to provide advanced training in sociological theory, research methods, and statistics. It prepares students for a variety of professional positions, including research analysts, data scientists, policy analysts, program evaluators, and administrators in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector. The M.S. degree also serves as excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in sociology or a related social science field.
CostPerCredit: $617.33 - $1282.67 per credit hour (2023-2024 academic year estimate)
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Travel Grants

ProgramName: Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology
Requirements: In addition to the requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the department: Satisfactory scores on the GRE General Test, taken within the last five years. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing interest in the field of speech-language pathology, professional goals, and relevant experiences. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential, work ethic, and ability to complete graduate-level work. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Completion of specific prerequisite coursework in communication sciences and disorders or related fields. Details can be found on the department website.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Department of Speech and Hearing Sciences offers a Master of Science degree program in Speech-Language Pathology that is designed to prepare students to practice as speech-language pathologists. The program requires 57 credit hours of graduate course work beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are typically full-time and graduate within two years after beginning graduate-level courses. Our graduates work in a variety of settings, including public schools, hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and private practices. After completing the MS degree, students are eligible to apply for Texas state licensure and national certification from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). Students who do not have an undergraduate degree in communication sciences and disorders may be admitted into the program. These students must complete undergraduate prerequisites prior to beginning graduate-level courses. These prerequisites can be completed at UNT as a post-baccalaureate student or at another university. If you have questions about prerequisites, please email us at shs-advising@unt.edu.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology program at UNT is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700. Our program meets the educational requirements for the Speech-Language Pathologist license in Texas.
CostPerCredit: Approximately $617.41/credit (Texas Resident, full-time average for 9 SCH), $1262.74/credit (Non-Resident, full-time average for 9 SCH)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Taxation and Data Analytics
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Master of Science (MS) in Taxation and Data Analytics is designed to prepare students for professional careers in taxation using data analytics. This program will develop skills in the areas of tax planning, tax compliance, tax research, tax technology and data analytics. This includes developing and interpreting data models, data visualization, and the ability to apply current and emerging data analytic techniques to solve taxation problems. This program combines both tax and data analytics courses within the G. Brint Ryan College of Business and the College of Engineering. Upon completion of this program, students will be prepared for careers in public accounting, corporate taxation, and governmental agencies, and will be able to sit for the CPA exam in Texas.
ScholarshipType: Texas Public Education Grants (TPEG), UNT Tuition Benefits, UNT Research Assistantships, UNT Teaching Assistantships, UNT Service Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Audiology (AuD)
Requirements: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Applicants must submit a separate application to the UNT Health Science Center via the Communication Sciences and Disorders Centralized Application Service (CSDCAS) at www.csdcas.org. A minimum of 25 observation hours in audiology is required. A minimum of 3 letters of recommendation is required. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required. TOEFL/IELTS: If English is not the applicant's native language, the applicant must demonstrate English proficiency as specified by the UNT Health Science Center.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of North Texas is a four-year clinical doctorate designed to prepare students for professional practice in audiology. The curriculum meets the academic and clinical requirements for licensure as an audiologist in Texas and for national certification by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). The program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences related to hearing and balance, as well as extensive clinical training in all areas of audiology. Students complete a minimum of 75 semester credit hours of academic coursework and 2000 hours of supervised clinical experience, including a full-time externship during the fourth year. Our students gain clinical experience in a variety of specialty areas including cochlear implants, pediatrics, educational audiology, and private practice settings. Students also have the opportunity to engage in research across a wide range of interests including electrophysiology, psychoacoustics, speech perception, hearing aids, and vestibular assessment. The UNT Au.D. program is committed to excellence in education, research, and clinical practice, preparing students to be leaders in the field of audiology.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of North Texas is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $150.00/credit hour; Non-Resident: $558.00/credit hour (2023-2024 Designated Tuition)

ProgramName: Doctor of Business Administration (DBA)
Requirements: Admission to the DBA program is based on a review of the entire application file. Strong applicants will have relevant work experience, excellent academic records, leadership potential, and outstanding critical thinking and communication skills. In addition to the Graduate School requirements, applicants must provide: Online Application and Application Fee, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, Official GMAT or GRE scores are required, with the exception of waivers. Please note the UNT Graduate School requires official scores. Personal Statement, Resume/CV, Three letters of recommendation, For international applicants, proof of English language proficiency.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) is a professional doctorate designed for senior managers and executives seeking to apply advanced academic theory and rigorous research to practical business problems. Unlike a Ph.D. program, which primarily prepares graduates for academic research careers, the DBA focuses on developing scholar-practitioners who can bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world business challenges. The UNT DBA program emphasizes research that directly contributes to business practice, policy, and strategy. Our graduates are equipped to lead organizational change, innovate business models, and address complex problems with data-driven insights. They often pursue roles in senior management, consulting, or specialized research within corporations, government, or non-profit organizations.
Accredidation: AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (for the G. Brint Ryan College of Business)

ProgramName: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Performance
Requirements: The DMA program is designed for the highly talented musician who has demonstrated exceptional promise through previous academic degrees and performance. It is a three-year residency degree that combines comprehensive coursework and intensive instruction for the highest artistic and academic achievement. Areas of study include Music History, Music Theory, and other music-related courses. Students seeking the DMA degree must audition for entrance, in addition to meeting the standard UNT TGS and College of Music requirements. All graduate applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s general admission requirements: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution; Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours or a 3.0 on all undergraduate work; Official transcripts from all universities attended; Official scores for English Language Proficiency (ELP), if required (International applicants); Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores, if required by your program of interest. Graduate students wishing to apply to any degree program in the College of Music must complete two applications: the UNT Toulouse Graduate School application and the College of Music graduate application. In addition to the online application, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the College of Music (via the online application form): Curriculum Vitae/Resume – an overview of your academic and performance/professional experience; Statement of Purpose – a statement of your academic and professional goals, including a discussion of your interest in the UNT College of Music. (Maximum of 500 words). DMA applicants must also submit (in addition to the above): Repertoire List – a representative list of your previous performance repertoire; Writing Sample (DMA Performance only) – a paper written on a musical topic (e.g., from a music history/theory course); Interview/Audition.
Department: College of Music
Fees: Approximately $6,187.50/Semester or $12,375/Year (for Texas Residents, based on 9 credit hours/semester)
Fees.1: Approximately $6,187.50/Semester or $12,375/Year (for Texas Residents, based on 9 credit hours/semester)
Description: The DMA in Performance is the most advanced music performance degree offered at UNT, preparing students for careers as performing musicians and artist-teachers at the highest level. Students develop expertise in their principal applied area of study, gaining a breadth of knowledge across music history, theory, and literature, and a deep understanding of repertoire. Throughout the program, students refine their musical and technical skills, interpretative abilities, and scholarly research while developing a distinctive artistic voice. Opportunities abound for students to perform as soloists, in chamber ensembles, and in large ensembles in a wide range of styles, genres, and historical periods. Students receive intensive private instruction, participate in master classes, and have access to UNT’s world-class facilities and performance venues. Upon completion of the DMA in Performance, students will be prepared to assume positions in college/university music departments, professional symphony orchestras, opera companies, touring ensembles, and other performance venues.
CostPerCredit: Approximately $740.50/credit hour (for Texas Residents, including per-credit-hour tuition and mandatory fees)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Minimum GPA of 3.0 in Master’s degree coursework. Official GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. Required Application Materials: Toulouse Graduate School application, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of intent, Professional vita or resume, Writing sample (a research paper, critical essay, or similar academic text), Portfolio of creative works (or a statement about why a portfolio is not included and alternative documentation), Interview (by invitation, after review of application), International students must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores (unless exempted).
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Fees: Resident: $5,524.00/Semester, Non-Resident: $12,024.00/Semester (based on Fall 2023 - Spring 2024 Graduate Estimated Bills for 9 credit hours)
Fees.1: Resident: $5,524.00/Semester, Non-Resident: $12,024.00/Semester (based on Fall 2023 - Spring 2024 Graduate Estimated Bills for 9 credit hours)
Description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education at the University of North Texas provides an advanced course of study that is focused on art education as a broad field of inquiry and practice, including, but not limited to, K-12 schooling contexts, post-secondary education, museums and community arts organizations. The curriculum is designed to educate scholars who will contribute to research, theory, policy and practice in art education locally, nationally and globally.

The faculty members in the Department of Art Education and Art History are active researchers, practitioners and educators whose work reflects an extensive range of approaches to research, diverse theoretical and methodological perspectives, and varied areas of emphasis related to learning and teaching in art. Faculty interests include critical studies, social justice, curriculum development, culturally responsive pedagogy, teacher education, community art education, visual culture, disability studies, and contemporary art practices in education. Students are encouraged to pursue an individualized course of study that aligns with their intellectual interests and professional aspirations within the broad scope of the field of art education. The program emphasizes both disciplinary breadth and individualized depth through a flexible curriculum of foundational studies, advanced seminars and independent research.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $800.00/credit hour, Non-Resident: $1,450.00/credit hour (based on Fall 2023 - Spring 2024 Graduate Estimated Bills for 1 credit hour)
ScholarshipAmount: TGS Doctoral Fellowships: $20,000 annually for up to two years.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Graduate), Fellowships (Doctoral, Research), Merit-based, Departmental

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Behavioral Science
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and the following program requirements: Minimum 3.0 GPA in previous work. GRE scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) submitted directly from ETS. GRE scores must be less than 5 years old. There is no minimum score requirement; however, competitive applicants typically score above the 50th percentile on the verbal and quantitative sections. Three letters of recommendation. Required Documents: Curriculum Vitae or Resume, Statement of Purpose, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. For information about the application and admission process, including admission to the Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and for international students, visit the UNT Graduate Admissions website.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Concentration: Basic Behavior Analysis, Applied Behavior Analysis
Description: Doctoral students in Behavioral Science are trained in the experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and behavioral neuroscience. Students are expected to conduct original research that advances the basic science of behavior and/or addresses socially significant problems. Our doctoral program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for careers in academia, research, or practice. Many of our graduates become university professors, researchers, or clinical practitioners. The program emphasizes a strong foundation in research methodology, experimental design, and quantitative analysis, preparing students to be leaders in the field.
ScholarshipAmount: TGS Doctoral Fellowship: $20,000/year (plus full tuition waiver and health insurance); Emerald Eagle Doctoral Fellowship: $24,000/year (plus full tuition waiver and health insurance)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Service Assistantships, Fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Requirements: Minimum GPA: 3.0, Official GRE scores, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose (required for both PhD and MS applicants), Current resume or curriculum vitae, Supplemental Application Form (Required by department)
Department: College of Science
Description: The Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with a strong background in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, genetics, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the program offers students the opportunity to conduct research in diverse areas, including: Protein structure and function; Enzymology and metabolism; Gene regulation and epigenetics; Cell signaling and communication; Neurobiology and development; Cancer biology; Infectious disease; Biotechnology and synthetic biology; Bioinformatics and computational biology. Our faculty members are highly collaborative and committed to mentoring students in both experimental and theoretical approaches. Students gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge techniques and instrumentation, preparing them for successful careers in academia, industry, and government. The program culminates in the completion and defense of a doctoral dissertation based on original research.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships, Travel Grants, Dissertation Fellowships, Emergency Grants, One-Time Grants

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Robert B. Toulouse School of Graduate Studies and must also meet specific program requirements. All application materials must be submitted through the Toulouse Graduate School Application portal. Program Requirements for Admission: Students must have a master’s degree in a biological science or a closely related field, or a bachelor’s degree in a biological science or a closely related field with a minimum of 24 semester credit hours in biological sciences, 6 semester credit hours of calculus or statistics, and 8 semester credit hours of chemistry. An applicant with a master’s degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.5 on all previous graduate work. An applicant with a bachelor’s degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Submission of Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. Successful applicants generally have scores above the 50th percentile on all three sections (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing). A statement of purpose outlining academic background, research interests, and career goals. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or research abilities. A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. Evidence of research experience (e.g., publications, presentations, research projects). International applicants must also meet the English Language Proficiency requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School.
Department: Department of Biological Sciences, College of Science
Fees: Resident: $5,550/Semester ($11,100/Year); Non-Resident: $10,134/Semester ($20,268/Year). Based on 12+ credit hours for Fall/Spring 2023-2024.
Fees.1: Resident: $2,700/Semester ($5,400/Year); Non-Resident: $7,740/Semester ($15,480/Year). Based on 12 credit hours for Fall/Spring 2023-2024.
Description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Biology. Our graduate students are fully integrated into research activities and benefit from state-of-the-art facilities and instrumentation, strong faculty mentoring and abundant research and teaching assistantships. Students pursue research in areas ranging from ecology, evolutionary biology and behavior to environmental science and toxicology to cell and molecular biology and physiology. Our students are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry and government agencies.
CostPerCredit: Resident Tuition: $225/Semester Credit Hour; Non-Resident Tuition: $645/Semester Credit Hour (additional mandatory fees apply per semester).
ScholarshipAmount: $20,000 for 9 months (stipend for full-time Teaching/Research Assistantship)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology with a concentration in Exercise Physiology
Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program requires that the applicant possess either a master’s degree in biology or a closely related field, or a bachelor’s degree in biology or a closely related field and meet the requirements set forth by The Graduate School for unconditional admission. Applicants for the doctoral degree program will be evaluated on the basis of a thorough assessment of their academic background, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, curriculum vitae/resume, and research interests. While a master’s degree is desirable, it is not required for admission into the Ph.D. program. Specific requirements include: Graduate School application and application fee. Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Official GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores. While there is no minimum GRE score for admission, successful applicants typically score above the 50th percentile in the verbal and quantitative portions of the examination. The Analytical Writing portion of the GRE is also considered. International applicants: Official TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for international applicants unless exemption criteria are met. See The Graduate School website for current exemption criteria. Statement of Purpose: This document should indicate your area of interest in biology and identify at least three faculty members whose research expertise aligns with your interests. Curriculum Vitae or Resume. Three letters of recommendation commenting on the applicant’s academic and/or research abilities.
Department: College of Science
Fees: Resident: $5,653.64/Semester; Non-Resident: $11,623.64/Semester (Estimated for 9-12 hours per Fall/Spring semester)
Description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers graduate work leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology. The PhD program offers advanced study and research in a variety of areas of biological sciences. Admission to the PhD program is contingent upon approval of the faculty and the chair of the department. The PhD program is a research degree and requires a minimum of 60 semester hours (36 semester hours of course work and 24 semester hours of dissertation). The department offers concentrations in biochemistry, cell biology, ecology, environmental sciences, genetics, microbiology, physiology and plant sciences.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Fellowships, Grants

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate degree in biomedical engineering or a related field (e.g., mechanical engineering, materials science, electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry or health sciences), a GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework and a 3.5 GPA in any graduate coursework, and strong GRE scores. Qualified applicants with a master’s degree from an ABET-accredited program may be admitted without the GRE requirement. To be considered for admission to the Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. program, prospective students must have: A baccalaureate degree in biomedical engineering or a related engineering/science/math field from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework. Strong applicants will generally have a GPA of 3.5 or higher. A graduate GPA of at least 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for any graduate coursework. Official GRE scores (verbal and quantitative sections) generally above 150. A TOEFL score of at least 79 (internet-based), or an IELTS score of at least 6.5, if English is not your native language. All applicants are required to submit a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. students work in research laboratories focusing on understanding and solving biomedical problems related to human health. Students enrolled in the Ph.D. program in Biomedical Engineering will take a set of core courses and then pursue advanced coursework and research in a chosen area of specialization. This program prepares students for careers in academia, industrial research and development, and government research laboratories.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Service), Fellowships, Tuition Waivers

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Business
Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. in Business Administration requires a master’s degree in business or related field from an accredited university. Applicants with undergraduate degrees in business will be considered, but may require additional coursework. All applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements: Resume/Curriculum Vitae, Statement of Purpose/Letter of Intent, GRE or GMAT scores, Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Concentration: Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Logistics and Supply Chain Management, Marketing, Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management, Strategic Management
Description:
A Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Business from the G. Brint Ryan College of Business at the University of North Texas prepares you for a career as a university professor and researcher. As a student in the program, you will develop expertise in research methods and theories, and learn how to conduct independent and original research. You will learn how to produce high-quality scholarly research in your primary concentration, enabling you to contribute to knowledge generation and dissemination. A Ph.D. in Business from UNT enables you to make a significant impact on your field of study. Upon graduating, you will be prepared for a career at a research-intensive institution as a tenure-track faculty member. Our graduates typically find placements at AACSB-accredited business schools in the U.S. and around the world.

Admission to the program is highly selective, and applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record, competitive GRE or GMAT scores, strong letters of recommendation, and a demonstrated interest in pursuing academic research. The program is full-time, requiring a significant commitment of time and effort over four to five years to complete. Students are required to take 69 credit hours for the PhD. After the first year, students can apply for an in-residence master’s degree, which usually requires them to take 30 credits to meet the requirements of the master's degree. Students are typically provided with financial support, which includes a stipend and tuition waiver, in exchange for working as a teaching or research assistant. The financial support package also typically includes health insurance.

To learn more about individual concentrations and their requirements, please visit the G. Brint Ryan College of Business website.
Accredidation: The G. Brint Ryan College of Business is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB Accreditation is the hallmark of excellence in business education, and has been earned by less than five percent of the world’s business programs.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemistry
Requirements: In addition to the general admission requirements of The Graduate School, applicants for the PhD program in Chemistry must meet the following requirements: A statement of purpose of approximately 1-2 pages describing the applicant's prior research experience, educational and professional goals and specific research interests. Three letters of recommendation. Applicants are encouraged to submit official GRE General Test scores, but they are not required for admission. A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Science
Description: UNT’s Ph.D. in Chemistry program is designed to develop students into independent, creative and responsible researchers in the chemical sciences. It offers coursework and research opportunities in all major areas of chemistry, as well as opportunities for interdisciplinary study with other sciences, materials science and engineering. Graduate students also have access to state-of-the-art instrumentation facilities in X-ray crystallography, mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance and electron microscopy. Our Ph.D. graduates are well prepared for careers in industry, government and academia.
ScholarshipAmount: $1,000 to $1,500 per semester (for Presidential Merit Scholarship for Doctoral Students)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Fellowships), Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Psychology
Requirements: All applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. The Clinical Psychology Ph.D. program requires additional materials beyond those required by the Toulouse Graduate School. Specific materials include: A personal statement that describes your interests in clinical psychology, professional goals, research experience, clinical experience, and why UNT’s program is a good fit. Three letters of recommendation (at least two from faculty who can speak to your academic and research abilities). Vita/résumé that details your academic background, research experience (e.g., publications, presentations, ongoing projects), clinical experience (e.g., practicum, volunteer work), and relevant work/volunteer history. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Official GRE general test scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing) are optional for applications for Fall 2024 and beyond. We do not accept GRE subject test scores. Minimum requirements: A bachelor’s degree in psychology or related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Completed coursework in introductory statistics and research methods with a grade of B or better. Substantial research experience (e.g., research assistant, independent study, honors thesis). Some clinical or volunteer experience is preferred.
Department: Department of Psychology
Fees.1: 4,989.90/Semester (Estimated Texas Resident Graduate Tuition & Fees - 9 hours)
Description: The UNT doctoral program in Clinical Psychology provides broad-based training in clinical psychology with an emphasis on the integration of clinical science and practice. Our APA-accredited Ph.D. program in Clinical Psychology is a generalist program that emphasizes research and clinical training in a broad range of areas within clinical psychology. These include: child, adolescent and family psychology; clinical neuropsychology; health psychology; forensic psychology; and schizophrenia/schizotypy. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge, skills and experience for entry-level professional practice as a licensed psychologist.
Accredidation: Accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA)
MinimumGreScore: above 150 verbal, above 150 quantitative, and above 4.5 writing

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Computer Science and Engineering
Requirements: Admission to UNT’s Toulouse Graduate School is a competitive process. Applicants must meet the admission requirements of both the Toulouse Graduate School and the specific degree program they are applying to. Applicants must also satisfy general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School, including official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, and English language proficiency requirements. Additional department requirements include: A UNT Graduate School Application; Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant’s academic and/or professional capabilities; A statement of purpose of not more than one page indicating the applicant’s interest in the program, research experience, and career goals; A resume or CV summarizing the applicant’s academic achievements, work experience, research publications, awards, and any other relevant experience; GRE scores are required for all applicants. The GRE must be taken within five years of the application date. Minimum scores: Verbal: 146; Quantitative: 155; Analytical Writing: 3.5; A master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field and exceptional qualifications may be admitted directly to the Ph.D. program. In this case, additional coursework may be required; A minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on all graduate work (for applicants with a master’s degree); A minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work (for applicants with a bachelor’s degree); Demonstrated research potential is highly valued. This can be evidenced by previous research projects, publications, or relevant work experience.
Department: College of Engineering
Description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science and Engineering at the University of North Texas is a research-intensive degree designed to produce highly qualified individuals capable of making significant contributions to the field of computer science and engineering. The program emphasizes deep theoretical understanding, advanced research methodologies, and practical application, preparing students for leadership roles in academia, industry, and government research institutions.
Students in the CSE PhD program will engage in cutting-edge research across a wide array of areas, including but not limited to: artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, software engineering, computer networks, computer architecture, bioinformatics, and robotics. The program fosters a collaborative environment where students work closely with faculty mentors on innovative projects, contribute to scientific literature, and present their findings at national and international conferences. Graduates are equipped with the skills to conduct independent research, develop new technologies, and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in computer science and engineering.
ScholarshipType: Texas Public Education Grant (TPEG), Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Students, Graduate Tuition Scholarships, Assistantships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counseling Psychology
Requirements: Application to the PhD program in Counseling Psychology will include: GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing portions of the Graduate Record Examination must be submitted. While there is no minimum required score, competitive applicants will typically score at or above the 50th percentile on the Verbal and Quantitative sections); Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; A curriculum vitae (CV); A personal statement that addresses your professional goals, experiences relevant to counseling psychology, and how the UNT Counseling Psychology program will help you achieve your goals (limit your statement to 5 double-spaced pages); A writing sample (scholarly writing, e.g., master’s thesis, research paper, publication) that demonstrates your ability to review and synthesize literature, develop a research question, and critically analyze a topic in counseling psychology; Completed graduate application (UNT online application). Preference will be given to applicants who have completed a master's degree in counseling or a closely related field (e.g., marriage and family therapy, social work, school psychology). Applicants with a master's degree in psychology or a related field (e.g., educational psychology, human development, developmental psychology) who have not completed graduate-level clinical coursework or supervised practicum experience may be required to complete additional coursework prior to full admission to the PhD program.
Department: College of Education
Description: The UNT Ph.D. in Counseling Psychology program emphasizes an ecological and multicultural perspective in its training of counseling psychologists. We prepare students for careers as counseling psychologists in academic settings (e.g., faculty positions), hospitals and medical settings, university counseling centers, community mental health centers, forensic settings, and independent practice. The program is committed to training psychologists who are competent in both research and practice and who can integrate these two areas of competence. The program emphasizes the importance of multicultural humility, social justice, and awareness of intersectionality. We seek to provide rigorous training in scientific research and evidence-based practice within a supportive and collaborative environment. This combination prepares our graduates to be effective and ethical practitioners, researchers, and educators in a diverse and global society.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of the American Psychological Association (APA). Our accreditation was reaffirmed in October 2021 for the next 7 years, with the next site visit scheduled for 2028.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counselor Education and Supervision
Requirements: Applicants to the Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision program must meet all University of North Texas and College of Education requirements for admission to graduate school, including: 1. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE): The GRE is required for admission to this program. We require a minimum combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 and a minimum Analytical Writing score of 4.0. The GRE must have been taken within the last five years. 2. Transcripts: Official transcripts of all previous college work must be submitted. 3. Resume/Vita: A current resume/vita is required. 4. Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose outlining the applicant's professional goals, research interests, and reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision at UNT is required. 5. Three Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic abilities, professional experience, and potential for success in a doctoral program are required. 6. Writing Sample: A writing sample, such as a scholarly paper or a thesis/dissertation excerpt, is required. 7. Interview: An interview with members of the Counseling and Higher Education faculty may be required.
Department: College of Education
Fees: Ranges from $5,934.34/Semester (Texas Resident, 9 hrs) to $11,466.34/Semester (Non-Resident, 9 hrs)
Fees.1: Ranges from $5,934.34/Semester (Texas Resident, 9 hrs) to $11,466.34/Semester (Non-Resident, 9 hrs)
Description: The Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision program prepares graduates to assume positions as counselor educators, supervisors, researchers, and advanced practitioners in academic and agency settings. The program is committed to developing leaders in the counseling profession who are highly competent in the areas of counseling, supervision, teaching, research and scholarship, leadership, and advocacy. Graduates are prepared for careers at the university level as faculty members who teach and supervise master’s and doctoral students, conduct research, and provide service to the profession. In addition, graduates are prepared to be supervisors and leaders in clinical settings.
Accredidation: The doctoral program in Counselor Education and Supervision is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) through March 31, 2028.
CostPerCredit: Ranges from $657.20/credit hour (Texas Resident) to $1,467.20/credit hour (Non-Resident)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Curriculum and Instruction
Requirements: Minimum 3.5 GPA on all graduate work prior to admission. GRE is NOT required. A current resume or curriculum vitae. A letter of intent that describes your purpose for pursuing doctoral study and your research interests (two to three pages). Evidence of scholarly writing ability such as a master’s thesis, research paper, or publication. If you do not have a writing sample of this type, you may complete a writing assessment set by the program faculty. Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of your academic ability and potential for doctoral work. Letters should be submitted to the Toulouse Graduate School directly from the recommender. Complete the Toulouse Graduate School application. Official transcripts from all institutions attended. International applicants: please see requirements at the Toulouse Graduate School.
Department: College of Education
Concentration: ESL Education, Early Childhood Education, Educational Technology, Elementary Education, Literacy, Mathematics Education, Research, Science Education, Social Studies Education, Special Education, STEM Education, Teacher Education
Description: UNT’s Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction develops leaders, educators, scholars, and researchers who can make significant contributions to the field of curriculum and instruction in various contexts. In this program, students develop expertise in a specialization (e.g., literacy, mathematics education, science education, educational technology, early childhood education, teacher education, etc.) while also gaining a deep understanding of philosophical, historical, and sociological perspectives of curriculum, teaching, and learning. Students explore issues relevant to curriculum and instruction, conduct original research, and disseminate knowledge through presentation and publication. This program helps students develop the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare them for leadership roles in various educational settings, including higher education, schools, and professional organizations.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Leadership
Department: College of Education
Description: The Ph.D. in Educational Leadership at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare reflective practitioners, researchers and scholars for leadership positions in higher education or K-12 school districts. This doctoral program requires a minimum of 66 post-master’s semester hours, including a dissertation. The program culminates in a dissertation on an original research project that contributes to the knowledge base of educational leadership. Graduates are prepared for careers as researchers, professors, policy analysts, administrators and leaders in academic, K-12 and other organizational settings. This program is offered by the Department of Educational Psychology.
MinimumGreScore: Verbal and Quantitative above 50th percentile, Analytical Writing at least 4.0
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Doctoral Fellowships, Tuition Waivers, Internal and External Grants

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology
Requirements: Admission to the Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Psychology program is competitive and based on review of all application materials. Requirements include: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Minimum 3.5 GPA on all graduate work. A master’s degree in educational psychology or a related field (e.g., applied behavior analysis, school psychology, special education, child development, psychology, educational research) from an accredited institution. Applicants must possess coursework (e.g., minimum 18 hours or equivalent) that includes advanced statistics, research methods, and content relevant to educational psychology. Prior coursework and/or experience in these areas is considered during the review process. Please refer to the department’s website for additional information regarding specific prerequisites. Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores taken within five years of the application date. Competitive applicants will typically have scores at or above the 50th percentile on the Verbal and Quantitative sections. Scores on the Analytical Writing section are also reviewed. Three letters of recommendation from faculty or supervisors who can attest to the applicant's academic potential and professional experiences. Letters from employers are acceptable if they discuss skills and knowledge relevant to doctoral-level work in educational psychology. Statement of Purpose, which addresses how the applicant’s academic and professional goals align with the program’s mission, faculty research interests, and program offerings. Applicants should also discuss how their prior experiences have prepared them for doctoral study. Curriculum Vita (CV)/Resume. A writing sample, such as an academic paper, professional report, thesis, or dissertation chapter. The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to conduct scholarly writing and communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program in Educational Psychology prepares students for positions as university faculty members, researchers and applied specialists in a variety of educational and research settings. The program places an emphasis on the acquisition of knowledge of human development, learning, motivation, cognition, measurement, and statistics. Through coursework and individually supervised research, students develop the skills necessary to analyze and synthesize existing research, conduct original research, and apply educational psychology principles to a range of practical settings. Students select a faculty mentor with shared research interests. Together, the student and mentor develop a plan of study that reflects the student's individual research interests and career goals. Students graduate with a strong theoretical understanding of educational psychology and the research skills necessary to pursue their individual research agendas.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Lab, Clinical), Fellowships (Doctoral, Master's, Diversity), Scholarships (Toulouse Graduate School Scholarship, Dean of Students Scholarships, Eagle Scholarship Programs)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology with a concentration in Learning Sciences
Requirements: Complete the online application to The Graduate School and pay the application fee. Official transcripts from ALL colleges and universities previously attended. Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. A minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 undergraduate credit hours attempted. A statement of purpose outlining career goals, research interests, how this program aligns with those interests, and how the applicant’s background and experience have prepared them for doctoral study. A current resume or curriculum vitae outlining academic, research, and work experience. An academic writing sample (e.g., a published article, research report, or term paper). Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant’s academic and/or research potential. An interview (typically virtual) with program faculty may be required.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Learning Sciences Ph.D. program in the Department of Educational Psychology at UNT is a highly interdisciplinary program focused on understanding and improving learning in a wide variety of contexts. Our program emphasizes design-based research, where students work closely with faculty mentors to design, implement, and evaluate innovative learning environments and interventions. Students will develop a deep understanding of learning theories, research methodologies, and instructional design principles, preparing them for careers as researchers, educators, and learning designers in academia, industry, and government settings.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Specific qualifications

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering
Requirements:
Required application materials for this program include:
*   Three letters of recommendation
*   Official transcripts
*   Statement of Purpose
*   Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)

Department: College of Engineering
Description: Electrical Engineering Ph.D. prepares students for leadership positions in research, development, and advanced engineering in industry, academia and government. Graduates are prepared to apply knowledge and contribute to the rapidly changing world of technology. The research interests of the faculty are diverse and encompass virtually every area of electrical engineering. We provide a stimulating environment for graduate studies and research. The Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering offers specializations in Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design, Communication Systems, Computer Vision and Machine Learning, Cyber-Physical Systems, Electromagnetics, Energy and Power Systems, Micro and Nanoelectronics, Signal and Image Processing, and Solid State and Optics.
MinimumGreScore: scores above the 50th percentile in both the verbal and quantitative sections and a 3.5 or higher in the analytical writing section

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering with a concentration in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: To be admitted to the Ph.D. program, prospective students must: Satisfy the admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School. Have a M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with a minimum GPA of 3.5. Complete the Electrical Engineering Ph.D. Application. A minimum GRE revised General Test score of 153 on the verbal portion, 153 on the quantitative portion, and 4.0 on the analytical writing portion. The GRE requirement may be waived if the applicant holds a master’s degree from an accredited U.S. university with a GPA of 3.5 or higher. Three letters of recommendation. A Statement of Purpose outlining the applicant’s interest in the program and research goals. A Resume or Curriculum Vitae. For international students, a TOEFL or IELTS score is required. Refer to the International Graduate Student Admissions page for details.
Department: College of Engineering
Fees.1: Texas Resident: $5,695.74/Semester (for 9 credit hours, Fall 2023); Non-Resident: $12,619.74/Semester (for 9 credit hours, Fall 2023)
Description: The Department of Electrical Engineering offers a doctoral program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering. The program is designed to provide students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary for careers in research, academia, and industry. Students will engage in cutting-edge research under the guidance of experienced faculty members, contributing to advancements in various fields of electrical engineering. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, preparing graduates to tackle complex engineering challenges and innovate in their respective areas of expertise. Graduates of the Ph.D. program will be equipped to assume leadership roles, conduct independent research, and make significant contributions to the field of electrical engineering.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $263.33/credit hour (tuition component only, Fall 2023); Non-Resident: $663.33/credit hour (tuition component only, Fall 2023)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in English
Requirements:
For Admission to the Program:
Admission to the PhD program in English is highly selective and is made by the graduate faculty in English. The department admits students who have demonstrated scholarly excellence and who are prepared to undertake advanced research in a specialized field.
Minimum requirements for admission include:
1. A master’s degree in English or a related field from an accredited university. Applicants with a master’s degree in a related field, or with only a bachelor’s degree, may be required to take additional courses.
2. A minimum 3.5 grade point average (GPA) in graduate coursework.
3. Materials to be submitted as part of the application for admission to the PhD program in English are:
   1. Official transcripts of all previous college work.
   2. Statement of Purpose (no more than 750 words).
   3. Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume.
   4. Writing Sample (15–20 pages).
   5. Three letters of recommendation.
   6. International applicants must also submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores (see “International Admission”).
The Graduate School requires international applicants to demonstrate English language proficiency through one of several options. See the International Admission section of the Graduate Catalog for details.
Application Deadlines
Fall: January 15
Spring: October 15
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: literary and cultural studies, rhetoric and composition, technical communication, creative writing
Description: The PhD in English program provides advanced study in English, with specialization possible in literary and cultural studies, rhetoric and composition, technical communication, and creative writing. Students develop sophisticated research, analytical, and communication skills suitable for careers in academia, professional writing, and related fields. The program emphasizes scholarly inquiry, critical thinking, and original contribution to the field of English studies. The doctoral degree in English is designed to offer a balance between historical and theoretical approaches to literary, linguistic, and rhetorical studies, while also providing the opportunity to study and practice creative writing and technical communication. The program aims to prepare students for careers as university faculty, independent scholars, writers, editors, and researchers in various professional fields.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships (Teaching, Research), Merit-based scholarships, Research fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science
Requirements: An earned master’s degree in an environmental science-related field or a bachelor's degree in a closely related science, engineering or social science field. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all previous graduate work. GRE (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) scores are required. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing the applicant's research interests and career goals. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic and research abilities. A current curriculum vitae or résumé. International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements.
Department: College of Science
Fees.1: Resident: $7,130/Year (for 18 credit hours over 9 months, estimated); Non-Resident: $16,778/Year (for 18 credit hours over 9 months, estimated)
Description: The Ph.D. in Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad and comprehensive education in environmental science. The program emphasizes advanced knowledge of environmental systems and processes, the development and application of quantitative skills, and the critical evaluation of environmental issues and solutions. Students will conduct original research that contributes to the scientific understanding of environmental problems and their solutions. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, government, industry, and non-profit organizations where advanced expertise in environmental science is required.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $396.11 per credit hour; Non-Resident: $932.11 per credit hour (based on 2023-2024 estimates for 18 graduate hours)
ScholarshipAmount: $1,000 (TGS Summer Research Fellowship), $15,000-$25,000 per year (TGS Doctoral Fellowship and other competitive graduate fellowships), up to $500 (Travel Grants)
ScholarshipPercentage: Tuition waivers for up to 9 hours of coursework for graduate assistants (0.5 FTE); tuition waivers for up to four years for TGS Doctoral Fellowship recipients.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Ecology and Conservation Biology
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and provide the materials specified below for their application file to be considered complete. Required application materials include: CV or resume, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Official GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing), Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International applicants must also provide a TOEFL or IELTS score. A score of 79 on the TOEFL iBT or 6.5 on the IELTS is required. Please visit the Graduate School Admissions page for more information.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science is a multidisciplinary program designed for students seeking advanced training in the scientific foundations of environmental analysis and problem-solving. This program provides students with the opportunity to conduct independent, original research under the mentorship of faculty, contributing to the advancement of environmental knowledge. Students will specialize in one of seven concentrations, allowing for focused study in their area of interest. The Ph.D. program emphasizes critical thinking, research methodology, data analysis, and scientific communication, preparing graduates for leadership roles in academia, government, industry, and non-profit organizations. The Ecology and Conservation Biology concentration focuses on the study of interactions among organisms and their environment, biodiversity, ecological processes, and the conservation of natural resources. Students will explore topics such as population dynamics, community ecology, ecosystem function, landscape ecology, and conservation genetics, preparing them for careers in research, wildlife management, habitat restoration, and environmental policy.
MinimumGreScore: above the 50th percentile on all three sections (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Grants, Loans, Work-Study

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Geoscience
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Environmental Science Ph.D. program, you must first apply to the Toulouse Graduate School. The Toulouse Graduate School requires a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Official transcripts of all previous college work must be submitted. Specific admission requirements for the Environmental Science Ph.D. program include: Completion of a master's degree in environmental science, a natural science, or a related field, or a bachelor's degree in one of those areas with significant relevant work experience. Minimum combined verbal and quantitative GRE scores of 300 (new score scale) or 1000 (old score scale). Scores must be less than five years old. (See GRE waiver criteria below) A current resume or curriculum vitae. A Statement of Purpose explaining your background, interests, and professional goals related to environmental science. Three letters of recommendation. International students must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Environmental Science. This degree program prepares students for careers as scientists in academia, industry, or government agencies. Students completing the degree program will have the knowledge and skills necessary to address complex environmental problems using an integrative scientific approach. Students are able to pursue a concentration in Geoscience as part of this program.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Human Ecology
Requirements: Admission to the Environmental Science Ph.D. program requires applicants to have an M.S. degree, or its equivalent, in environmental science or a related discipline. Exceptionally qualified applicants may be admitted to the Ph.D. program directly from a B.S. or B.A. degree. The GRE revised General Test is required for all applicants. A GRE score of 150 on the verbal and 150 on the quantitative reasoning sections and a 3.5 on the analytical writing section is expected. Applicants for the PhD in Environmental Science program must have an overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all undergraduate and graduate work OR a 3.5 GPA on all graduate work.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Environmental Science Ph.D. program is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers addressing complex environmental issues. Students will receive training in both theory and application of environmental science. Research areas include environmental assessment, ecology, toxicology, environmental chemistry, conservation, water quality, microbiology and human ecology. The Ph.D. program prepares students for careers in academia, environmental consulting and government agencies. Students are trained to become independent researchers and effective communicators of their research. Graduates from our program have been very successful in securing highly desirable positions. Our graduates are employed in faculty positions at universities, as research scientists in government agencies (e.g., USEPA), and as consultants in the private sector.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Doctoral Fellowships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Science Education Research
Requirements: Minimum Requirements for Admission: Baccalaureate or master's degree from an accredited institution. A master's degree is highly encouraged but not strictly required. Students entering with a bachelor's degree must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) on all work attempted while those entering with a master's degree must have a minimum GPA of 3.5 (on a 4.0 scale) on all work attempted at the master's level. GRE verbal and quantitative scores are required for all PhD applicants. There is no minimum score required, but competitive applicants typically score above the 50th percentile on both sections. Scores must be less than five years old at the time of application. The GRE requirement may be waived for exceptional master’s students already enrolled in our department’s program. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. All applicants must submit the following documents to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all institutions attended, GRE scores, Letter of intent / Statement of Purpose: (1-2 pages in length) indicating your qualifications for pursuing a Ph.D. in Environmental Science, your research interests and experience, and your career goals. Include the names of faculty members with whom you would like to work. Note: This is an important part of your application. Make sure to clearly state your research interests and identify faculty members you are interested in working with. CV / Resume: A list of educational, professional and research experiences, publications, presentations, awards, and other relevant information. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to your academic ability, research experience, and/or professional experience. International applicants must submit a copy of their academic evaluation, financial statement and other documents specific to international student applications.
Department: College of Science
Description: The PhD in Environmental Science offers research-based doctoral training for students interested in careers addressing complex environmental issues. Students develop an interdisciplinary research program that emphasizes quantitative skills and a strong disciplinary foundation in a focus area within environmental science. This allows our students to pursue research at the interface of basic and applied science while addressing environmental problems. The program prepares students to become leading scientists and professionals in governmental agencies, environmental consulting firms, non-governmental organizations, industry, and academia. The PhD program will provide you with an interdisciplinary approach to environmental issues, cutting-edge research skills in your concentration area, and the ability to think critically and solve complex environmental problems.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $20,000/year for Dean of the Graduate School Doctoral Fellowships
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Doctoral Fellowships, Recruiting Fellowships, Travel Grants, Research Grants

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Toxicology
Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program is based on the recommendation of the Environmental Science Program faculty. All applicants must meet the general admission requirements for graduate studies outlined in the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog. In addition, applicants must meet the following program requirements: A master’s degree in environmental science or a related discipline from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree may be admitted directly to the PhD program under exceptional circumstances. A GPA of at least 3.0 on all work leading to the master’s degree and on any work attempted beyond the master’s degree. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree seeking direct admission to the PhD program must have a GPA of at least 3.5 on all undergraduate work. Submission of GRE scores (general test). International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. See the Graduate Admissions section of this catalog for accepted methods of demonstrating English language proficiency. Applicants are encouraged to contact specific faculty members regarding research interests. All doctoral programs also require a CV or resume, a statement of purpose, and most doctoral programs require at least three letters of recommendation. Other general graduate admissions requirements include an application for admission, application fee, and official transcripts.
Department: College of Science
Description:
The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in Environmental Science with a concentration in Toxicology. This doctoral program requires a minimum of 60 credit hours beyond the master’s degree, or 90 credit hours beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students entering with a master’s degree may transfer up to 30 hours of graduate coursework, provided the coursework is appropriate for the degree and was completed within the previous seven years.
The PhD program in Environmental Science is designed to prepare graduates for positions in academic, industrial, or governmental organizations. The curriculum provides students with a broad and fundamental knowledge of current concepts in environmental science. The PhD degree emphasizes scientific research and allows students to specialize in a particular area of environmental science, such as toxicology, ecology, environmental chemistry, or others. Students are expected to complete their dissertation research, pass the qualifying exam, and successfully defend their dissertation during their course of study.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Research-based, Project-based (e.g., Dissertation Completion, Travel, Research Grants)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Health Sciences
Requirements:
Admission to the doctoral program requires an undergraduate degree and a master’s degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts of all college-level work must be submitted to the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition, the applicant must meet the following minimum requirements:
* A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on all undergraduate work or a 3.5 on all graduate work.
* A minimum combined score of 300 on the verbal and quantitative portions of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) and a minimum score of 3.5 on the analytical writing portion. The GRE must have been taken within five years of the date of application.
* Three letters of recommendation submitted directly from the person providing the recommendation.
* Statement of purpose (one page) indicating the applicant’s interest in the program, career goals and experience relevant to the program.
* Resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The PhD in Health Sciences is an interdisciplinary doctoral degree that prepares students for academic, research and leadership positions in health sciences. The program offers a broad base of didactic knowledge and opportunities for applied research related to the complex issues in health sciences. The program will advance the student’s knowledge, research and leadership skills to address current and emerging public health issues. The doctoral program provides a didactic foundation in critical thinking, research methods and statistics, and epidemiology and public health. Students in the program will be able to apply theory to practice; design and conduct applied research and evaluation; analyze, interpret and disseminate research findings; and communicate health sciences related information to diverse audiences. The PhD in Health Sciences will prepare students for leadership roles to address the needs of public health and healthcare organizations and agencies, governmental entities and private industry.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Higher Education
Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities attended; GRE scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) taken within the last five years (no minimum required score for the GRE, but students are encouraged to have competitive scores to ensure consideration); Official TOEFL or IELTS scores (for international applicants); Statement of Purpose (1-2 pages); Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Résumé; Writing Sample (e.g., academic paper, published article, or other scholarly work); Three letters of recommendation.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Ph.D. in Higher Education at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare individuals for leadership, teaching, and research positions in colleges and universities, as well as positions with state and federal agencies and organizations related to postsecondary education. Graduates of the program are prepared to serve as administrators in a variety of postsecondary settings; as faculty in master’s-level higher education and student affairs programs; and as researchers/analysts in institutional research and policy settings. The program emphasizes the development of research and scholarship skills, and provides students with a broad understanding of the historical, philosophical, political, social, cultural, and economic foundations of higher education, as well as the organizational and leadership dimensions of colleges and universities. Areas of study include, but are not limited to, student affairs administration, college teaching, higher education management, higher education finance, higher education law, and the history and philosophy of higher education. The program also offers opportunities for individualized study through electives, independent studies, and dissertation research. The Ph.D. in Higher Education requires a minimum of 66 semester hours beyond the master’s degree, including 15 hours of core courses, 15 hours of research courses, 15 hours of electives, and 21 hours of dissertation. All students complete a doctoral qualifying examination prior to beginning dissertation work. All degree requirements must be completed within a period of 10 years.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in History

An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and a 3.5 GPA or better on any graduate work. Applicants who do not meet these GPA requirements may be admitted on probation, at the discretion of the department. See “Graduate Academic Standing” in the Graduate School section of this catalog. 3. For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 on the internet-based test (iBT), or an IELTS score of 6.5. This requirement may be waived for international students who have earned a degree from an accredited U.S. institution or from a foreign institution in which English is the official language of instruction. 4. Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) are required. Test scores older than five years will not be accepted. Waivers are not available. 5. Three letters of recommendation addressing the applicant’s academic potential and qualifications. 6. A curriculum vita/resume. 7. A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic and career goals. 8. A writing sample, such as an excerpt from a research paper or master’s thesis.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Political Science requires students to develop theoretical knowledge and research skills across two major subfields within political science. Students receive methodological training in a variety of quantitative and qualitative techniques. The program trains students for careers as university professors and researchers, as well as for positions in government and non-profit organizations.
