Students choose two of the following major subfields: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, and public law. In addition, students may select an optional cognate/minor in a field closely related to their major subfields.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Public Administration and Management
Requirements:
The Toulouse Graduate School has final authority on all admissions. To be admitted to the PhD in Public Administration and Management program, applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Toulouse Graduate School and the following program requirements:
*   Application forms must be completed online.
*   Application must be accompanied by non-refundable application fee.
*   Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
*   Official scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test taken within the last five years.
*   A current résumé or curriculum vitae.
*   A statement of purpose (1,000 words maximum).
*   A writing sample.
*   A current master's degree in public administration or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Students with a master's degree in a related field who have not completed a significant portion of core MPA course work will be required to take additional course work to fulfill requirements.
*   A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0.
*   A minimum GPA of 3.5 on master's-level work.
International applicants must also meet general UNT international admission requirements.
Recommendations for admission are made by the graduate committee to the Toulouse Graduate School after consideration of all application materials, including the following: GRE scores, undergraduate and graduate GPAs, a statement of purpose, writing sample, resume and relevant work experience. Applicants are evaluated competitively.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Fees: $4,954.00/Semester (Texas Resident, based on 9 credit hours, 2023-2024 academic year)
Fees.1: $4,954.00/Semester (Texas Resident, based on 9 credit hours, 2023-2024 academic year)
Description: The PhD in Public Administration and Management is an advanced degree for students seeking careers in university teaching, research and public service. Graduates will be prepared to conduct theoretical and applied research on important issues facing public and nonprofit organizations; teach courses in public administration, management, public policy, and urban affairs; and apply scholarly knowledge to improve the practice of public service and management. The program builds on a strong commitment to quality teaching and research in the Department of Public Administration in the College of Health and Public Service.
ScholarshipAmount: $2,000 per semester for two semesters ($4,000 total) for doctoral students (Toulouse Graduate School Fellowship)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Sociology
Requirements: To be admitted to the PhD program in Sociology, you must meet the following criteria: Master’s degree in sociology or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree but no master’s degree in sociology or a related field may be admitted conditionally and must complete specific courses before continuing. A minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale on all previous graduate work. Three letters of recommendation from faculty members or others familiar with your academic and professional work. Official TOEFL or IELTS scores for applicants whose native language is not English.
Department: College of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences
Description: Our doctorate in sociology provides students with a strong theoretical and methodological foundation in the discipline and the opportunity to specialize in an area of interest. We prepare students for positions in teaching and research, as well as for work in applied settings. Graduates of our program work in colleges and universities, research centers, and nonprofit organizations, as well as in state and federal government. The program faculty are committed to creating an environment where students engage in an intensive, yet supportive, intellectual community.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Special Education
Requirements: Master’s degree in Special Education or a related field (or bachelor's degree in Special Education with an emphasis in deaf and hard of hearing) from an accredited institution. Minimum overall GPA of 3.5 in master’s level courses (or 3.25 in bachelor’s level if applying directly from bachelor's degree with an emphasis in deaf and hard of hearing). Evidence of at least three years of professional experience in special education or a related field. Three letters of recommendation. All applicants must submit additional application materials directly to the Department of Educational Psychology. The department will contact you regarding these additional materials after you complete the ApplyTexas application.
Department: College of Education
Description: The UNT Doctoral program in Special Education provides advanced study in an area of focus related to special education, as well as general knowledge in research methodology, statistics and higher education teaching. Our doctoral students prepare for roles as university professors, researchers, and educational leaders and administrators. The Ph.D. in Special Education provides students with in-depth knowledge and skills in teaching, research, and service. Throughout the program, students will engage in relevant coursework, research experiences, and teaching opportunities. Doctoral students complete a minimum of 60 post-master's credit hours, including 15 hours of core coursework, 15 hours of research courses, 15 hours in an area of emphasis, 9 hours of teaching experience/internship, and 6 hours of dissertation. After coursework is completed, students are required to pass comprehensive examinations and successfully propose and defend a dissertation.
ScholarshipType: Departmental scholarships, Graduate Assistantships, TGS scholarships, Presidential Graduate Student Scholarships, Research Fellowships, Dissertation Grants, Travel Grants, McNair Scholars

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Data Analytics in Economics
Requirements: Admission to the certificate program requires the student to meet the general admission requirements for graduate study at UNT.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description:
The Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Data Analytics in Economics is offered in the Department of Economics. This certificate is designed for individuals who have completed a bachelor’s degree and are looking to enhance their quantitative and analytical skills in data analytics as applied to economics. The certificate is also suitable for students pursuing a master's or doctoral degree who wish to gain a deeper understanding of advanced data analytics tools and methodologies relevant to economics without committing to a full master's degree in economics or data analytics.
The certificate program provides students with practical skills in economic data analysis, econometric modeling, machine learning techniques, and data visualization. Students will learn to apply these tools to analyze economic data, make informed decisions, and solve complex economic problems. The program emphasizes hands-on experience with industry-standard software and real-world datasets, preparing graduates for careers in data science, economic consulting, financial analysis, and research roles in both the public and private sectors.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $398/credit ($98 Tuition + $300 Designated Tuition). Non-Resident: $1099/credit ($799 Tuition + $300 Designated Tuition).
ScholarshipType: TGS Fellowships, Travel Grants, Competitive Scholarship Program (Tuition Waivers), Departmental Scholarships/Assistantships, External Funding Opportunities

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Humanities Pedagogy
Requirements: Admission to the Advanced Humanities Pedagogy Graduate Academic Certificate program is through the Toulouse Graduate School. Students must be either a current UNT graduate student or apply for admission to a UNT graduate degree program. In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants for the Advanced Humanities Pedagogy Certificate must submit: A statement of purpose (500-750 words) that describes their interest in the certificate, any relevant experience, and how the certificate aligns with their academic and professional goals. A Curriculum Vitae or Resume (CV).

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Management in Libraries and Information Agencies
Requirements: Minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Statement of Purpose. Resume. Three letters of recommendation. The GRE is not required for admission to this program. Students must have completed 18 hours of graduate work in information science or a related field (or equivalent). Please note: Students who have already earned the UNT MS in Library Science (LS) or Master of Information Science (MIS) are not eligible to apply. Apply through the Toulouse Graduate School ApplyTexas application.
Department: College of Information
Description:
The Advanced Management in Libraries and Information Agencies Graduate Academic Certificate from the University of North Texas is designed for information professionals who wish to expand their leadership and management skills and knowledge. This online program enhances the management skills of librarians and other information professionals, preparing them to take on leadership roles within libraries and information agencies.
As a student in the program, you’ll focus on the essential foundations for effective library and information center management, including information policy, human resources, budgeting, fundraising, grant writing and strategic planning. These skills are vital in today’s rapidly changing information environments and will provide you with the tools necessary to excel in leadership positions.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships, Fellowships, Travel Grants, Emergency Aid, University Scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Manufacturing
Requirements: A master’s or bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work, or a 3.0 or better on previous graduate work. An applicant who holds a master's degree (or higher) is considered to have met the GRE requirement. The GRE is not required for admission for students with a master's degree or higher. The Graduate School requires official GRE scores. Recommended GRE scores include a verbal score of 146, a quantitative score of 146, and an analytical writing score of 3.0. Applicants must hold an undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials science and engineering, industrial engineering, electrical engineering, or related fields. Students with degrees in other fields may be admitted to the certificate program but may be required to take additional undergraduate courses to prepare them for graduate-level work. International applicants need to meet the university's English language proficiency requirements.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Advanced Manufacturing provides an opportunity for graduates with a bachelor’s degree in engineering or a closely related field to enhance their understanding of advanced manufacturing processes and systems. The certificate provides skills in fundamental manufacturing sciences and the development of new manufacturing processes/systems, with an emphasis on interdisciplinary collaboration. Students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to contribute to the rapidly evolving field of advanced manufacturing, which encompasses areas such as additive manufacturing, smart manufacturing, and sustainable manufacturing.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in AI in Education
Requirements: The requirements for admission to the GAC in AI in Education are consistent with requirements for all other graduate certificates, master's and doctoral degrees in the Department of Learning Technologies. In addition to the application for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, applicants must satisfy these requirements: GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Completion of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. International students are also required to submit additional materials including the TOEFL/IELTS scores if they have not earned a bachelor's degree from a U.S. institution. A current resume or curriculum vitae, documenting academic and professional history. A letter of intent/statement of purpose (no more than 2 pages), describing your professional and academic background, experience, and interests in the area of artificial intelligence in education, and how this certificate will help you achieve your professional goals. The statement should demonstrate your ability to articulate ideas in a clear and concise manner. No GRE is required for this certificate program.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in AI in Education provides students with foundational and advanced knowledge of artificial intelligence concepts, applications, and ethical implications within educational contexts. This certificate is designed for educators, instructional designers, curriculum developers, and professionals in related fields who seek to integrate AI technologies effectively into teaching, learning, and administrative processes. Students will explore cutting-edge AI tools, machine learning principles, natural language processing, and data analytics relevant to education, preparing them to innovate and lead in the evolving landscape of AI-driven education.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $381.00 per credit hour; Non-Resident: $781.00 per credit hour
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Assistantships, University-level Scholarships, College/Departmental Scholarships, Grants, Loans, Work-Study

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Analytics Project Management
Requirements: Admission to the Toulouse Graduate School. Minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Statement of Purpose. GRE scores are not required. Two letters of recommendation (optional).
Department: College of Business
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Analytics Project Management is a 12-hour certificate designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to be an analytics project leader. With increasing pressure to create value through analytics and a significant shortage of analytics project managers, students will be prepared to lead such projects in organizations upon completion of this certificate. The curriculum covers the tools and techniques necessary for project execution, as well as the unique aspects of managing analytics projects and how they differ from traditional projects.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Applied Behavior Analysis
Requirements:
Students must meet the following minimum admission requirements set by the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Behavior Analysis.

Toulouse Graduate School Requirements
*   Baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution
*   Undergraduate GPA of 2.8 or higher overall, or 3.0 in the last 60 hours
*   GRE (General Record Examinations) Not Required (effective Fall 2021)

Department of Behavior Analysis Requirements
*   Statement of Purpose (Required)
*   Resume (Required)
*   Three (3) Letters of Recommendation (Required) - These letters should be from individuals who know you professionally and can speak to your academic abilities and work ethic.
*   Official transcripts from all institutions attended
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Applied Behavior Analysis (GAC-ABA) at the University of North Texas is designed to provide students with the academic coursework required to sit for the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) examination. The program emphasizes ethical practice, evidence-based interventions, and practical application of behavioral principles. The UNT GAC-ABA program is verified by the Association for Behavior Analysis International® (ABAI®) as meeting the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) examination. Upon completion of the GAC-ABA program, students will be able to apply behavior analytic principles to assess and treat socially significant behavior, design and implement evidence-based behavioral interventions, conduct ethical practice as a behavior analyst, analyze and interpret data to make informed treatment decisions, and communicate effectively with clients, families, and interdisciplinary teams.
Accredidation: Verified by the Association for Behavior Analysis International® (ABAI®) as meeting the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® (BCBA®) examination.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Applied Sociology
Requirements:
Application requirements for the GAC in Applied Sociology are identical to those required for admission to the UNT graduate school, with the following exceptions:
A bachelor’s degree in Sociology or a related field (e.g., Political Science, Social Work, Psychology, Geography, Communication Studies, Public Health, Criminal Justice).
A minimum 3.0 overall GPA or a minimum 3.0 GPA on the last 60 hours of coursework leading to the bachelor’s degree.
Students who are already admitted to a UNT graduate program (e.g., M.A., Ph.D.) and are in good standing with the graduate school are eligible to apply for the GAC in Applied Sociology without submitting additional application materials.
Department: Department of Sociology
Fees: Approx. $4,334.04 for the entire 12-hour program (Texas Resident, 2023-2024 academic year)
Fees.1: Approx. $4,334.04 for the entire 12-hour program (Texas Resident, 2023-2024 academic year)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Applied Sociology provides students with knowledge and skills relevant to applying sociological knowledge to real-world problems. The certificate can be completed as a stand-alone program or in conjunction with a master's or doctoral degree in sociology or related fields. The program prepares students for careers in research, policy analysis, program evaluation, and community development in governmental, non-profit, and private organizations. The certificate requires 12 graduate credit hours. The Applied Sociology certificate prepares students to apply sociological theory and research methods to analyze social problems, develop and evaluate interventions, and communicate findings to diverse audiences. Graduates will be equipped to work in various settings, including government agencies, non-profit organizations, and private businesses, as researchers, analysts, evaluators, and consultants.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $1,000 per semester (UNT/TAMS Excellence Scholarship); Up to $500 (Graduate Student Travel Grant); $15,000 award + tuition/fees waiver (Deans Doctoral Fellowship)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Archival Management
Requirements:
For admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Archival Management, applicants must have:
*   A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work.
*   Official Transcripts: Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   Resume: A current professional resume or CV.
*   Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing your academic and professional background, your professional goals, and how the certificate program will help you achieve those goals.
*   Recommendation Letters: Three letters of recommendation addressing the applicant’s academic and/or professional preparation for graduate work.
*   GRE General Test: The GRE is not required for admission to the Archival Management certificate program.
*   Writing Sample: A writing sample (8-10 pages) that demonstrates research skills and ability to write at the graduate level.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Archival Management is designed for students interested in a focused course of study that offers a solid foundation of theoretical and practical training in all aspects of archival work. It provides an excellent credential for those seeking entry-level professional positions and for those already working in archives who wish to enhance their qualifications. It is intended for individuals who have already earned a master's degree or are currently enrolled in a master's degree program.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: ~$675 per credit hour; Non-Resident: ~$1191 per credit hour (based on 2023-2024 rates for 1-3 SCH in the College of Information)
ScholarshipType: Institutional (e.g., TGS Legacy Scholarship, UNT Tuition Grant), Departmental, Travel Grants, External (includes merit-based and need-based options)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Art Museum Education
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Artificial Intelligence
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate program in Artificial Intelligence is open to students holding a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. Additional requirements for admission to the Artificial Intelligence Certificate include: Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or a closely related field. Minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to this certificate program. Proficiency in a high-level programming language such as C++, Python, or Java. Successful completion of undergraduate courses in Data Structures, Discrete Mathematics, and Algorithms. Applicants who do not meet these requirements may be considered for conditional admission on a case-by-case basis. They may be required to complete specific prerequisite courses before being fully admitted to the program.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Artificial Intelligence is designed for post-baccalaureate students who want to develop or expand their knowledge and skills in this rapidly growing field. Students will learn the fundamental concepts and practical applications of AI, including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision. The program emphasizes hands-on experience with AI tools and technologies, preparing students for careers in various industries or for further graduate study. Courses taken for this certificate may be applied to the Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence program, contingent upon program requirements and advisor approval.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Autism Intervention
Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and apply for admission to the GAC in Autism Intervention (GACI) through the Department of Counseling and Higher Education. Applications are reviewed for fall admission only.
Minimum requirements for admission to the GAC in Autism Intervention are:

    Master’s degree in a mental health, education, or related field with a GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 undergraduate hours and in all graduate work; or a bachelor’s degree in a mental health, education, or related field with a GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 undergraduate hours.
    GRE general test scores. However, the GRE requirement may be waived if the applicant holds a master’s degree in a mental health, education or related field with a GPA of 3.5 or higher on all graduate work.
    A current resume or curriculum vitae.
    A personal statement regarding the applicant’s interest in working with individuals with autism spectrum disorders and outlining their professional goals.
    Three letters of recommendation addressing the applicant’s academic and professional qualifications for success in graduate study and professional work with individuals with autism spectrum disorders.
    Interview with a departmental faculty member. This interview may be held virtually.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Certificate in Autism Intervention is an advanced graduate program for professionals who work or wish to work with individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This 15-hour certificate provides training to graduate students, teachers, speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, social workers, school psychologists, board-certified behavior analysts, and other professionals who support individuals with autism spectrum disorder. It includes coursework and supervised practicum experiences relevant to various intervention strategies for individuals with ASD across the lifespan. The program is offered online. Graduates of this certificate will be prepared to work as practitioners in schools, hospitals, clinics, and private agencies that provide services for individuals with ASD.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Big Data and Intelligent Systems
Requirements: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Big Data and Intelligent Systems is open to students who have been admitted to a graduate degree program at UNT or hold a master’s degree in computer science or a related area (e.g., computer engineering, information science, mathematics, statistics). Students must meet the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. Students are expected to have a strong background in data structures, algorithms, and programming. Students with an insufficient background may be required to take remedial courses. Applicants are required to submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. A minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 undergraduate hours and in all graduate work is required. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit a TOEFL score of 79 on the internet-based test (iBT), an IELTS score of 6.0, or a PTE Academic score of 53. International applicants must provide proof of financial support. A Statement of Purpose is required. A current resume or CV is required. No GRE is required for admission to this certificate program.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Big Data and Intelligent Systems is designed for students who desire to enhance their understanding of big data systems, intelligent systems, and analytics, and how they apply to the real world. This certificate is well suited for students with a background in computer science, computer engineering, information technology, or a related field. Upon completion, students will be able to apply advanced knowledge in the areas of big data analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to tackle real-world problems. The program also prepares students for careers in the growing fields of data science and artificial intelligence.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Children's and Young Adult Library and Community Services
Requirements:
Admission to the certificate program requires:
* An earned bachelor's degree.
* Graduate School admission (see the UNT Graduate Catalog for details).
Departmental requirements for certificate admission include:
* An official, current copy of your Vita/Resume (uploaded to the MyGradSchool application portal).
* A Statement of Purpose outlining your professional experience, reasons for seeking admission to the program, and future career goals (uploaded to the MyGradSchool application portal).
* Official GRE scores are NOT REQUIRED.
* International applicants must provide TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE scores as outlined on the International Admissions website.
Department: College of Information, Department of Information Science
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Children's and Young Adult Library and Community Services prepares students for careers working in public and school libraries, and other community organizations that serve children and young adults. Students completing this certificate will gain knowledge and skills for managing, evaluating, and designing services to children and young adults. The program emphasizes community outreach, literacy, advocacy, technology, collection development, and programming in different settings.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Community College Leadership
Requirements:
Graduate School Requirements:
* An earned bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
* A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum 3.0 GPA in all graduate coursework.
* GRE is NOT required.

Program Requirements:
* Submit an online application through the ApplyTexas portal.
* Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Community College Leadership program provides an opportunity for master’s and doctoral degree holders to acquire a graduate certificate in Community College Leadership. The certificate prepares graduates for leadership positions within community colleges. The program focuses on providing knowledge and skills that promote success in leadership roles in the community college context. The program requires 15 graduate credit hours of coursework in educational administration. All courses are delivered online.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Computational Linguistics
Requirements: Application to the Toulouse Graduate School through ApplyTexas. (A non-refundable application fee is required.) Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. An academic curriculum vitae (CV) or resume outlining academic history, professional experiences, publications, and presentations. A statement of purpose (1-2 pages) describing your academic background and interests, professional experiences, and career goals and how the Certificate in Computational Linguistics will help you achieve those goals. Three letters of recommendation from faculty or professionals who can address the applicant's academic preparedness and research potential for graduate study. Official GRE General Test scores (verbal, quantitative, analytical writing) (recommended for applicants whose GPA is below 3.0). International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Description:
Computational linguistics is an interdisciplinary field between computer science and linguistics. It focuses on developing computer models of natural language to solve language-related problems. Examples of computational linguistics applications include spell checking, grammar checking, machine translation, spam filtering, text summarization, speech recognition, and information extraction.
The Certificate in Computational Linguistics at UNT is designed for students who are interested in developing advanced computational linguistics skills. The certificate targets graduate students in linguistics, computer science, and related areas. Our curriculum offers a solid foundation in computational linguistics theory and applications with a balance between theoretical and practical training. We encourage students to gain hands-on experience by completing projects on authentic computational linguistics problems using real-world data and open-source software tools.
Upon completing the certificate program, students will be able to demonstrate:
*   Solid understanding of computational linguistics theory and applications
*   Ability to implement computational linguistics techniques to solve real-world problems
*   Experience using open-source computational linguistics software tools
*   Skills in evaluating computational linguistics systems

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Cultural Heritage Stewardship
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Cultural Heritage Stewardship (CHS) at the University of North Texas provides students with knowledge and skills to preserve, manage, and interpret cultural heritage. The certificate is offered primarily online, with an option for some face-to-face courses. The certificate is designed for students seeking entry-level positions in cultural heritage organizations or current professionals looking to advance their careers. Courses focus on the theories, principles, practices, and technologies used in cultural heritage stewardship. Students learn how to manage cultural heritage resources, engage with diverse communities, apply ethical practices, and utilize relevant technologies. The program culminates in a capstone project where students apply their knowledge to a real-world cultural heritage challenge.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Analytics
Requirements:
To apply for this certificate program, you must:
*   Be admitted to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School.
*   Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
*   Have a minimum 2.8 undergraduate GPA on a 4.0 scale or 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work.
*   Have completed an introductory programming course in Python or R with a grade of B or higher.
*   Have completed an introductory statistics course with a grade of B or higher.
*   Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   International applicants must meet additional requirements.
Department: Department of Business Information Technology
Description: Designed for business professionals seeking to enhance their knowledge and skills in the growing field of data analytics, the Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Analytics will introduce students to the analytical skills and business insight required to convert raw data into meaningful and actionable information. This certificate is valuable to students with varied educational backgrounds including business, sciences, humanities, and fine arts. The curriculum will focus on developing statistical programming skills to facilitate the analysis of large datasets, an understanding of fundamental data visualization techniques, and the ability to interpret and communicate results effectively within a business context.
ScholarshipAmount: Varies; up to $3,000 per semester (Texas Public Education Grant), up to $1,000 per semester (General Academic Scholarship) for eligible graduate students.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Engineering
Requirements:
Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Engineering program is competitive. Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School and additional program requirements listed below.
Program Admission Requirements:
*   Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
*   Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the last 60 undergraduate hours.
*   Background in computer science, information science, mathematics, statistics, or a closely related field. Applicants with backgrounds in other fields may be admitted on a conditional basis and may be required to complete specific prerequisite courses.
*   Personal Statement: A statement of purpose outlining career goals and reasons for pursuing the certificate.
*   Résumé/CV: Highlighting academic background, relevant work experience, and any research or projects.
*   Letters of Recommendation (optional): Applicants may submit up to three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with their academic or professional qualifications.
*   Applicants are encouraged to submit GRE scores, though they are not required.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Engineering provides students with an in-depth understanding of the principles, techniques, and tools required to design, implement, and manage robust and scalable data engineering solutions. The certificate aims to equip students with the necessary skills to address the growing demand for professionals who can build and maintain data pipelines, data warehouses, and data lakes effectively. The curriculum focuses on practical applications and hands-on experience, preparing students for successful careers in data-intensive industries.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science is a two-step process. First, students must apply to the Toulouse Graduate School. Second, they must apply directly to the Department of Computer Science and Engineering for program acceptance. Departmental Admission Requirements: In addition to the requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School, students seeking the Data Science Graduate Academic Certificate must meet the following departmental requirements: 1. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with an adequate undergraduate GPA (generally, a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale in the last 60 undergraduate hours and any graduate work). 2. Undergraduate preparation for the certificate program is satisfied by earning a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, data science, information science, mathematics, statistics or a related field. 3. Students who have not earned a bachelor's degree in a related field may be admitted to the certificate program provisionally upon recommendation of the department. These students will be required to demonstrate competency through examinations, coursework or other evidence in the following areas: calculus, linear algebra, basic probability and statistics, data structures, and object-oriented programming. 4. Students must submit the following directly to the Toulouse Graduate School: Official transcripts from all universities attended. GRE is not required for this certificate. A statement of purpose outlining academic interests, relevant experience and career goals. A current resume or CV. Two letters of recommendation (optional but recommended).
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Data scientists are in high demand and needed across industries. Become a part of this growing field through the University of North Texas’ online Graduate Academic Certificate in Data Science. As a student in this program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare you for careers in data science. Our courses cover topics such as data visualization, data mining, machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, and programming. Through the Data Science Graduate Academic Certificate, you will learn to apply computational and statistical analysis to large data sets. Other topics include: Data collection and cleansing, Data visualization, Data mining, Data-driven decision making, Machine learning, Deep learning, Statistical analysis, Programming, Natural Language Processing, Artificial intelligence.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics is granted through the Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. No GRE required.
Department: Frank W. and Sue Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: As the digital landscape expands, the ability to analyze and interpret data from online communication channels becomes increasingly vital for organizations. The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Communication Analytics is designed to equip students with the skills to strategically collect, analyze, and apply data to improve digital communication strategies. This certificate offers a focused curriculum that covers areas such as web analytics, social media analytics, data visualization, and ethical considerations in data analysis. Graduates will be prepared to leverage data-driven insights to optimize campaigns, enhance user engagement, and make informed decisions in a variety of communication-related roles. This certificate is ideal for professionals seeking to advance their careers in marketing, public relations, corporate communication, or related fields, and who wish to specialize in the analytical aspects of digital communication.
Accredidation: The University of North Texas is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate, master’s and doctoral degrees.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Travel Grants, Tuition Waivers

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School and specific requirements for the certificate. For admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Applicants who do not meet the minimum GPA may be admitted to the certificate program on probation by the department. Applicants for the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Content Management must meet the specific requirements for admission to the master’s program in the Department of Information Science or have a graduate degree in a related field and be in good academic standing. This includes: Satisfactory score on the GRE General Test, if required by the Department of Information Science. Resume Statement of Purpose outlining the applicant’s interest in the program and career goals. Three letters of recommendation are required for the master's program. For the GAC, only two are needed if the applicant doesn't have a graduate degree. If the applicant already has a graduate degree, recommendations may be waived. (This is for the MS/PhD program applicants and may be required for the GAC. Consult with department) For international applicants, a TOEFL or IELTS score is required. Additional Information: Students who have been admitted to a master’s or doctoral program at UNT in good standing may pursue a GAC concurrently. No separate application or fee is required. Students should apply via the Graduate School online application or complete the 'Add a Graduate Academic Certificate' form.
Department: College of Information
Description: The graduate academic certificate in Digital Content Management prepares students for a career in the dynamic field of digital content. The program will provide students with competencies to create, manage, preserve and disseminate digital content and assets for various types of organizations using a variety of formats and platforms. Students will acquire the skills necessary to identify and implement best practices for digital content creation, acquisition, and curation. The certificate can be completed in conjunction with an M.S. degree in Information Science or as a stand-alone certificate.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management
Requirements: To be admitted to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management, you must meet the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all graduate work. The GRE is not required for admission to this certificate program. For international applicants, official TOEFL (minimum score of 79) or IELTS (minimum score of 6.0) scores are required. If you are a current UNT student and want to add this certificate to your degree plan, contact your academic advisor.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Curation and Data Management addresses the growing demand for professionals skilled in managing digital assets throughout their lifecycle. This 12-hour certificate program provides students with the foundational knowledge and practical skills needed to curate, preserve, and provide access to digital data in various institutional settings. Students will learn about data governance, metadata standards, digital preservation strategies, and the ethical considerations involved in managing digital information. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with relevant tools and technologies, preparing graduates for roles in libraries, archives, museums, government agencies, and corporate environments. The certificate is suitable for current information professionals seeking to enhance their skills, as well as for graduate students interested in specializing in digital curation and data management.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Field of study, Activity-based, Graduate Assistantships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Retail Merchandising
Requirements:
To be admitted to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Retail Merchandising program, a student must have:
An undergraduate degree with an overall GPA of 3.0 or better in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a GPA of 3.0 or better on all previous graduate coursework.
A minimum of a 3.0 GPA in all merchandising courses or related courses.
Official transcripts from all higher education institutions attended.
International students must submit a TOEFL score of 79 on the internet-based test or an IELTS score of 6.0. An English language proficiency exam waiver is available for international applicants who have completed an undergraduate degree at an accredited U.S. institution or from an approved English-speaking country. Please consult the International Admissions website for more information.
A personal statement of career goals and objectives related to the Digital Retail Merchandising program.
A resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Three letters of recommendation.
Applications are accepted for Fall, Spring, and Summer semesters.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: This certificate is an 18-credit-hour program offered through the Department of Merchandising and Digital Retailing. This certificate will provide students with specialized knowledge in digital retail merchandising, including retail buying, product development, global sourcing, and e-commerce. Students will gain an understanding of current technologies and strategies used in digital retail, including data analytics, social media marketing, and omnichannel retailing. This certificate is designed for individuals seeking to enhance their skills for career advancement or those who wish to transition into the fast-paced and evolving digital retail industry. The certificate can also be stacked to meet degree requirements for the Master of Science in Merchandising. A 3.0 GPA is required for all certificate courses. All courses must be completed within 6 years.
ScholarshipType: Assistantships, Fellowships, Scholarships, Grants (Need-based, Research, Travel)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Social Science
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Social Science requires successful completion of a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and a minimum 3.0 GPA in previous graduate coursework. Students are also required to submit a statement of purpose outlining their interest in the program and its relevance to their academic and career goals. Students who do not meet these minimum requirements may still be considered for admission on a probationary basis, based on a holistic review of their application materials.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Social Science introduces graduate students to the skills necessary to conduct research and analyze digital social data using computational methods. The certificate emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of digital social science, drawing on insights from computer science, statistics, and the social sciences. Students will gain practical experience with various computational tools and techniques, including data collection, data management, data analysis, and data visualization. Upon completion of the certificate, students will be equipped to analyze digital social data, interpret their findings, and communicate their results effectively.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $672.09/credit hour (estimated 2024-2025 for 9 credit hours); Non-Resident/International: $1227.65/credit hour (estimated 2024-2025 for 9 credit hours)
ScholarshipType: TGS Scholarships, TGS Fellowships, Departmental Scholarships, UNT Academic Scholarships, UNT General Scholarships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Sociology
Requirements: To be admitted to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Sociology, prospective students must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School and hold a bachelor's degree. Students are also required to: Have a 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Digital Sociology provides advanced training in the theoretical and methodological approaches to understanding and analyzing the relationship between digital technologies and society. Students will gain critical skills in areas such as social media analysis, digital data collection and analysis, and the ethical implications of digital research. This interdisciplinary certificate is designed for graduate students and professionals seeking to enhance their expertise in digital sociology for academic, research, or professional careers.
ScholarshipAmount: Varies, typically $1,000 to $2,000 for one year for Certificate Scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Dual Credit Teaching in Mathematics
Requirements:
Departmental requirements are in addition to the University requirements listed in the Graduate Catalog. All applications are submitted through the Toulouse Graduate School. Specific departmental requirements for admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Dual Credit Teaching in Mathematics program are:
* A graduate application (through the Toulouse Graduate School)
* Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
* Bachelor's degree in mathematics or a closely related field from an accredited institution
* Undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 hours of undergraduate work
* Proficiency in written and spoken English, demonstrated through one of the following: TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, or Duolingo English Test (see UNT's Graduate Catalog for specific score requirements)
* A letter of intent indicating why the student wishes to pursue the certificate (Statement of Purpose)
* Three letters of recommendation
* Resume
Department: College of Science
Fees.1: Estimated $7,382/Year (Resident) or $13,942/Year (Non-Resident) for 12 credit hours, based on 2023-2024 rates
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Dual Credit Teaching in Mathematics is offered through UNT Dallas, in the Department of Mathematics. It is designed to prepare current high school teachers to meet the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) 18 graduate credit hour requirement needed to teach dual credit courses in Mathematics at the high school level. Courses completed in this certificate will fulfill the 18-hour requirement.
CostPerCredit: $443.42 - $843.42 per credit hour (depending on residency, based on 2023-2024 rates for 12 credit hours)
ScholarshipType: TGS Fellowships, TGS Scholarships, Travel Grants, Academic Achievement Scholarships, Assistantships (Teaching Assistant, Research Assistant, Graduate Assistant)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Economic Geography
Requirements: Applicants must be in good standing as graduate students at UNT in a degree-seeking program or have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. If the applicant is not a current UNT graduate student, they will need to satisfy the minimum requirements for admission to the UNT Graduate School.
Department: Department of Geography and the Environment
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Economic Geography provides graduate training in the spatial aspects of economic systems and development. Students will learn about topics such as economic globalization, regional development, sustainable development, consumption, and production systems and will gain skills in economic data analysis and visualization. The certificate is designed for students already enrolled in graduate programs at UNT (e.g., MS or PhD in Geography or other social sciences) as well as post-baccalaureate students in North Texas. Courses required for the certificate may count toward a Geography graduate degree.
CostPerCredit: $722/credit hour (Resident, estimated for 9 hrs); $1300/credit hour (Non-Resident/International, estimated for 9 hrs)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Research-focused, Diversity-focused, Assistantships, Fellowships, Grants

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy Accounting
Requirements:
All applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s admission requirements. Additionally, applicants for the Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy Accounting must meet the following program requirements: Applicants must satisfy one of the following requirements:
* Hold a master’s degree in accounting or taxation from an AACSB-accredited institution with an overall GPA of 3.0 or higher in the master’s degree.
* Hold a bachelor’s degree in accounting from an AACSB-accredited institution with an overall GPA of 3.0 or higher in the bachelor’s degree.
* Hold a bachelor’s degree in business administration with a major in a field other than accounting from an AACSB-accredited institution with an overall GPA of 3.0 or higher in the bachelor’s degree, and have successfully completed a minimum of 21 hours in upper-division accounting coursework (3000-level and above) with a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
* Hold a bachelor’s degree from an AACSB-accredited institution with an overall GPA of 3.0 or higher and submit a satisfactory GMAT or GRE score.
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy Accounting provides professional development for energy industry accountants and auditors to enhance their knowledge in the complex area of energy accounting. The certificate will address issues related to oil and gas, utilities, alternative energy and environmental accounting. The certificate consists of 12 graduate credit hours. Graduates of the program will be able to: Demonstrate an understanding of current financial accounting, auditing and taxation issues applicable to companies in the energy industry. Demonstrate knowledge of current issues in financial reporting as it applies to the energy industry. Demonstrate an understanding of internal controls and risk management issues in the energy industry. Demonstrate an understanding of ethical issues within the energy industry.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy
Requirements: To be admitted to the Energy Graduate Academic Certificate program, a student must meet the following criteria: Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Have a minimum GPA of 2.8 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework, or a minimum GPA of 3.0 on any previous graduate coursework. Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: UNT's Department of Energy and Environmental Policy (ENEP) offers a Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy. Students interested in energy policy have a unique opportunity to gain knowledge and experience in energy issues and policy. The certificate can be standalone or complement another graduate degree. The certificate requires 12 credit hours (4 courses). The certificate program allows students to specialize in areas relating to energy, renewable energy, and fossil fuels. Students gain foundational knowledge and understanding of energy-related topics across multiple disciplines. Courses cover topics such as: U.S. and international energy policy, energy demand, energy economics, renewable energy, energy conservation, environmental issues, and energy security. The Graduate Academic Certificate in Energy provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills in current energy issues that are critical in today's energy landscape. These skills are highly valued by employers in both the private and public sector.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Environmental Ethics and Science
Requirements: For admission, students must have been admitted to a graduate degree program in Philosophy, Environmental Science, or a related field; or, if not seeking a graduate degree, have a 3.0 overall undergraduate GPA and apply directly to the certificate program via the Toulouse Graduate School. Students must satisfy all requirements as outlined in the Graduate Catalog.
Department: Department of Philosophy, College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Environmental Ethics and Science introduces students to the core philosophical concepts, theories and debates in environmental ethics, and provides students with basic training in environmental science. The Certificate integrates ethical theory, policy, and scientific method, and is designed to provide students with the interdisciplinary knowledge and skills needed for a variety of occupations that require both scientific literacy and ethical problem solving related to the environment. The Certificate serves a wide range of students including those working in federal or state government, NGOs, and the private sector; current or prospective graduate students who wish to add a credential in environmental ethics and science; and individuals who wish to pursue the Certificate as a stand-alone credential. The Certificate requires 15 credit hours of graduate course work (9 hours in philosophy courses and 6 hours in environmental science courses) and can be completed in approximately 1.5-2 years.
ScholarshipType: Teaching fellowships, Research assistantships, Tuition waivers, Grants, Scholarships, Fellowships, Loans, Dissertation Completion Scholarships, Professional Development Scholarships, Conference Scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Event Management
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution; A minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work; Official transcripts from all institutions attended; A personal statement, no more than 750 words, detailing why you are interested in the program and how it aligns with your professional goals; Resume or CV; GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores are not required for admission to this program.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Event Management provides comprehensive training and knowledge necessary to successfully plan, implement, and manage a wide range of events. This certificate is designed for professionals seeking to enhance their careers in the event planning industry, or for individuals looking to gain specialized knowledge in this growing field. The program emphasizes strategic planning, operational logistics, risk management, marketing, and sustainability in event contexts. Students will learn how to design, execute, and evaluate various types of events, including corporate meetings, conferences, festivals, and social gatherings. The curriculum also covers budgeting, vendor negotiations, sponsorship acquisition, and the application of technology in event management. Graduates will be equipped with the skills and expertise to pursue leadership roles in event management, hospitality, tourism, and related sectors.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Gender, Feminism and Environmental Justice
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in any previous graduate work. Applicants must provide official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. Statement of Purpose (approximately 500 words) describing the applicant’s interest in the certificate and in Gender, Feminism and Environmental Justice more broadly, and indicating how the certificate will contribute to the applicant’s academic and/or professional goals. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV) Writing Sample (approx. 10 pages) related to the applicant’s academic/professional interests in Gender, Feminism, and/or Environmental Justice. The GRE is NOT required for admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate program in Gender, Feminism and Environmental Justice.
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Gender, Feminism, and Environmental Justice (GFEJ) is designed for students who want to develop skills and knowledge to engage in scholarly research, public policy, and advocacy that addresses the gendered and racialized dimensions of environmental problems and environmental movements. The certificate is housed in the Department of Women's and Gender Studies and is available to all graduate students at UNT as well as post-baccalaureate students not currently enrolled in a UNT graduate program. Students must apply for admission to the certificate program. Current graduate students who wish to add the certificate may do so by submitting a certificate application to the Toulouse Graduate School after completing at least 9 credit hours toward their graduate degree and having a minimum 3.0 graduate GPA. Non-degree seeking students may apply to the Toulouse Graduate School as post-baccalaureate students.
ScholarshipType: Academic Merit-based, Financial Need-based, Fellowships, Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Graduate)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
Requirements: Admission to the GIS Certificate program is limited to students who: Have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Are currently enrolled in an UNT Health Science Center graduate degree program, or have been admitted to a UNT Health Science Center graduate degree program. Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 in undergraduate work. Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae highlighting previous academic training and/or relevant experience. Provide a statement of purpose outlining professional interests and goals and reasons for pursuing the GIS certificate. Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Request official GRE scores be sent to the UNT Health Science Center (code 6909). The GRE requirement may be waived if the applicant has a master’s degree or higher from an accredited U.S. institution or has a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. Note: TOEFL or IELTS score may be required for international applicants. Consult with Admissions for details.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is designed for those who wish to enhance their skills in GIS science and technology. This certificate is beneficial for individuals currently in a graduate program who wish to strengthen their GIS skills, or for individuals not currently in a graduate program but desire to obtain graduate-level GIS skills for career enhancement. The certificate is offered through the School of Public Health. Students completing the certificate may be interested in pursuing careers in Public Health, Environmental Science, Urban Planning, Emergency Management, etc.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Data Science
Requirements:
Admission to the GAC in Health Data Science is restricted to applicants who have been admitted to a master’s or doctoral degree program in the College of Health and Public Service (HPS) or the College of Engineering (COE) at UNT. Individual departments/colleges may have specific requirements. It is best to contact the department for specifics.

Application Requirements:
- Official Transcripts
- Statement of Purpose
- GRE General Test Scores
- Three Letters of Recommendation
- Resume or CV
Department: College of Engineering and College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Data Science provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills necessary for working with health data, and for understanding and applying data science methods in the health domain. The courses cover essential topics in health data science, including health care data formats, privacy regulations, data analysis, machine learning applications, and ethical considerations. The program aims to prepare professionals for careers in health care analytics, research, and public health, equipping them to leverage data-driven insights to improve health outcomes and inform decision-making. Students will gain practical experience through projects and case studies, developing a portfolio of work relevant to the health data science field. The program is designed for individuals with a background in computer science, statistics, health sciences, or a related field, who wish to specialize in the growing area of health data science. The certificate is offered primarily online.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Information
Requirements:
Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and/or previous graduate work.
A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
Applicants must meet all general requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School.
Submit a formal letter of intent (statement of purpose) indicating why the applicant is seeking admission to a particular GAC program.
Submit a current resume or curriculum vita (CV).
Official Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
Immunization Records (for students under 22 years of age only, for more information visit the UNT Health Center website)
Evidence of English Language Proficiency for international applicants.
Department: College of Information, Department of Information Science
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Health Information is designed to provide health care professionals and individuals with a background in health care or information technology with an opportunity to acquire knowledge and skills to lead and manage the increasingly complex information technology landscape in health care organizations. The health information industry continues to expand as providers transition to digital medical records, and the health care system relies more heavily on data for decision making. These trends are fueling a demand for professionals with knowledge and skills in health information to fill a variety of roles within hospitals, medical practices, health insurance companies, public health agencies, and pharmaceutical companies. The certificate program will prepare professionals to fill roles in the areas of health informatics, health information technology, health information management, and public health informatics. The curriculum focuses on health information standards, health IT infrastructure, health data analytics, and information privacy, security, and ethics. The 15-hour certificate provides a solid foundation of knowledge and skills that can be completed as a standalone certificate or as part of the Master of Science in Information Science (MSIS) or other graduate degree programs at UNT. This certificate can be completed fully online.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Services Administration
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for the Graduate School and specific Department Requirements. Department requirements include: GRE is not required for this G.A.C. program, Official transcripts from all colleges and universities previously attended, Graduate School Application, Statement of Purpose: Required, Resume or CV: Required, and Three letters of recommendation: Required. General Graduate School requirements also include completing and submitting the online application through ApplyTexas, paying the non-refundable application fee, demonstrating English language proficiency for international applicants, and being in good standing at the last institution attended.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description:
The Graduate Academic Certificate in Health Services Administration will provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare them for leadership positions in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and managed care organizations. The certificate focuses on the administrative aspects of healthcare, such as financial management, human resources, strategic planning, and quality improvement. The curriculum is designed for working professionals seeking to advance their careers in healthcare administration.

The program consists of 15 credit hours of graduate-level coursework. The curriculum includes courses in healthcare policy, financial management, strategic planning, and human resources. Students will also complete a capstone project or internship, allowing them to apply their knowledge and skills in a real-world healthcare setting.

Upon completion of the certificate, students will be prepared to assume leadership roles in various healthcare organizations. Graduates will have the skills and knowledge to manage complex healthcare organizations, lead teams, and make sound financial decisions. The certificate is also an excellent option for students interested in pursuing a master's degree in health services administration or a related field.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Hospitality Management
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Hospitality Management program requires applicants to meet the admission requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School AND the following program requirements: Minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework. Applicants who do not meet the minimum GPA may be admitted conditionally on a case-by-case basis through a petition to the graduate advisor. Students admitted conditionally must maintain a 3.0 GPA in their first 12 hours of graduate coursework. Completion of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Additional Requirements for International Students: Demonstrate English language proficiency. Review the UNT International website for specific requirements based on your country of origin. For students with degrees from a non-U.S. institution, an official course-by-course evaluation of international transcripts through a NACES-approved agency, such as SpanTran or WES, is required. The evaluation must be sent directly from the evaluating agency to the Toulouse Graduate School. A list of NACES-approved agencies can be found at NACES.org.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Fees: Texas Resident: ~$6,392.40; Non-Resident: ~$15,056.40 (estimated total for 12 credit hours based on 2023-2024 graduate tuition and fees schedule)
Fees.1: Texas Resident: ~$6,392.40; Non-Resident: ~$15,056.40 (estimated total for 12 credit hours based on 2023-2024 graduate tuition and fees schedule)
Description: Our Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Hospitality Management provides an opportunity for working professionals or those wishing to advance their career to gain additional knowledge and skills related to management in the hospitality and tourism industry. The program can be completed online or in a face-to-face format. This 12-hour certificate program is available to both degree-seeking and non-degree-seeking graduate students. All course credit hours earned in the GAC program may be applied towards a Master of Science (M.S.) in Hospitality Management degree at UNT, should the student choose to pursue a master’s degree in the future. The program provides the students with advanced knowledge and skills in hospitality management. Students will learn the key skills and knowledge needed to manage successful businesses in the hospitality industry while taking courses designed to provide a broad understanding of the operational and administrative aspects of the field. Emphasis will be placed on developing the skills needed for management-level positions, including financial management, marketing, human resources, and strategic planning. Why pursue a GAC in Hospitality Management? Prepare for leadership roles in the hospitality industry. Enhance your management and business skills related to hospitality. Open doors to career advancement. Deepen your understanding of current trends and challenges in the hospitality sector. Connect with a network of professionals and faculty experts.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $532.70/credit hour; Non-Resident: $1,254.70/credit hour (based on 2023-2024 tuition schedule for graduate students taking 1-8 hours)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Graduate Assistantships (Teaching, Research, Administrative), Federal Work-Study, Departmental Scholarships, External Scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Instructional Design and Technology
Requirements: Minimum requirements for admission to the G.A.C. in Instructional Design and Technology include: A bachelor’s degree from an institution accredited by a recognized regional accrediting agency. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better. GRE scores are not required for admission. Two letters of recommendation. A current resume or curriculum vitae. A statement of purpose. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Application to the Toulouse Graduate School through ApplyTexas. (Note: Only master's, doctoral and certificate applicants submit the ApplyTexas application. Post-baccalaureate applicants for teacher certification or undergraduate-level courses do not). Application to the Department of Learning Technologies.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Instructional Design and Technology Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) provides candidates with expertise in the principles and practices of instructional design, current and emerging educational technologies, and strategies for effective technology integration. Candidates will acquire skills in analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation (ADDIE) of instructional materials using innovative learning strategies and technologies. This GAC can be taken by itself or can be combined with other graduate programs at UNT.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication
Requirements:
The Graduate Academic Certificate in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication is available to students who have been accepted to a graduate degree program at UNT and to students pursuing the certificate as their terminal academic objective. Applications are accepted for the fall, spring and summer semesters. To apply, complete the online application for graduate admission and send all supporting documents to the Office of Admissions. The admission application fee is $75.
Additional requirements include:
*   Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in the last 60 undergraduate hours.
*   Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA in any graduate work.
*   Three letters of recommendation. At least two letters should be from faculty familiar with the applicant’s academic work.
*   A statement of purpose (500 words).
*   Writing sample.
*   A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Fees: 6427.60/semester (estimated for 12 credit hours, Texas Resident, Fall 2024)
Fees.1: 6427.60/semester (estimated for 12 credit hours, Texas Resident, Fall 2024)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Interactive and Virtual Digital Communication is an interdisciplinary 12-credit program designed to prepare students for careers in the rapidly growing fields of interactive and virtual reality (VR) digital communication. Students will gain practical skills and theoretical knowledge in areas such as user experience (UX) design, interactive media development, virtual reality content creation, and digital storytelling. The curriculum focuses on developing proficiency in industry-standard software and techniques, fostering creativity, and understanding the principles of effective digital communication across various platforms. The program is ideal for professionals seeking to enhance their skills, recent graduates looking to specialize, or individuals interested in pursuing advanced studies in digital communication.
CostPerCredit: 535.63/credit hour (estimated average for 12-credit certificate, Texas Resident, Fall 2024)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Analytics
Requirements: An applicant to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Analytics must satisfy the following minimum requirements for admission to graduate study: A bachelor’s degree from an institution accredited by a recognized regional accrediting agency. A 3.0 grade point average (GPA) in the last 60 undergraduate semester credit hours and in all previous graduate coursework. Completion of a graduate admission application through the ApplyTexas portal and payment of the nonrefundable application fee. Official transcripts from all universities attended must be submitted to the Toulouse Graduate School. Additional application documents required for the G.A.C. in Learning Analytics (in addition to the application listed above): No GRE required, Statement of Purpose, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Current Resume/Curriculum Vitae.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Analytics provides students with knowledge and skills to understand how to collect, analyze, and report data related to learner and learning contexts in order to improve learning processes and outcomes. Learning Analytics is a growing area that has broad application in corporate, government, military, non-profit, and academic settings. The program is designed for graduate students and working professionals seeking to add expertise in learning analytics to their existing academic or professional skill sets. Students will learn the process of learning analytics from data collection to reporting, including data manipulation, visualization, statistical analysis, and ethical considerations. The program offers a core set of skills and competencies in learning analytics, but also allows students to customize their program of study to meet their own interests and career goals. The certificate is offered completely online.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Sciences
