Requirements: Admission to the learning technologies master's, doctoral and graduate academic certificate programs is a two-step process. In order to be admitted to the graduate certificate program, you must: 1. Meet the admission requirements for the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. 2. Meet the program-specific admission requirements for the graduate academic certificate in learning sciences or graduate academic certificate in instructional systems. Program-Specific Requirements for all Learning Technologies Graduate Programs (M.S., Ph.D., Graduate Academic Certificates) include: Statement of Purpose: Submit a 500-word statement describing your academic and professional background, goals, and how the program aligns with those goals. Resume/CV: Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae. Three Letters of Recommendation: Provide three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to your academic and/or professional capabilities. GRE Test Scores (Optional): GRE General Test scores (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) are optional for all Learning Technologies graduate programs. If you choose to submit scores, they may strengthen your application.
Department: College of Information
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Learning Sciences is designed to help students better understand how humans learn across a variety of contexts and age groups. This certificate is designed for a variety of students, including those who wish to enhance their professional skills in learning and development within their current professional careers, those pursuing advanced graduate degrees in various fields related to learning, and those interested in pursuing additional knowledge within the learning sciences field. The Certificate in Learning Sciences does not lead to educator certification.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Leadership, Specific talents, Field of study

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Narrative Journalism
Requirements: An earned master’s degree from an accredited institution. In some cases, a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution will be sufficient. Undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. Graduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on all graduate work. Upload a personal statement discussing academic and professional goals relevant to the field of narrative journalism (500 words). Upload a résumé/curriculum vitae (CV) Upload a writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to tell a story through narrative nonfiction. This can be published or unpublished material. (This is generally 10-15 pages for graduate students, but can be longer if needed to showcase your best work). All official transcripts must be sent from previously attended institutions directly to UNT. Three letters of recommendation. International applicants may be required to submit proof of English language proficiency. GRE is not required.
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: The Narrative Journalism Certificate is a 12-hour graduate academic certificate designed to prepare students to create compelling, in-depth non-fiction stories in both print and digital forms. The certificate is offered through the Mayborn School of Journalism and can be completed as a stand-alone certificate or in conjunction with a master’s degree in journalism. It is open to any graduate student at UNT. The certificate prepares students to work as journalists, editors, communications professionals or storytellers for a wide variety of outlets. Students will learn how to write feature stories, profiles, in-depth reports, and memoirs using journalistic reporting and research methods. Students will learn how to structure long-form narratives, how to gather information through interviews and observations, and how to effectively write for various media.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Teaching Assistantships, TGS Travel Grants, Thesis and Dissertation Grants, UNT Toulouse Graduate School scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Principal Leadership Preparation
Requirements:
Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Principal Leadership Preparation requires:
*   A master's degree from an institution of higher education accredited by an agency recognized by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB).
*   A valid Texas teacher certificate.
*   Two years of teaching experience in a public or accredited private school.
*   An official graduate transcript.
*   A current resume.
*   A letter of intent (statement of purpose) addressing professional background, leadership experience, and future career goals.
*   Three letters of recommendation commenting on the applicant's professional experience and leadership potential.
*   An interview with the admissions committee.
Department: College of Education
Fees.1: $5,139.60/Program for Texas Residents (15 credit hours, estimated for 1 semester); $11,589.60/Program for Non-Residents (15 credit hours, estimated for 1 semester)
CostPerCredit: $100/credit hour (Texas Resident tuition component); $530/credit hour (Non-Resident tuition component)
ScholarshipAmount: Ranges from $1,000 to $3,000 for some general TGS scholarships

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Program Leadership
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An overall undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 hours of coursework. A Statement of Purpose that addresses your career interests and how the certificate will help you achieve your goals. A current résumé/CV. Three letters of recommendation are required (only if your undergraduate GPA is below 3.0). Official transcripts from all institutions attended. International applicants must meet additional requirements.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Program Leadership prepares individuals who are currently serving in leadership roles in the nonprofit sector, community-based organizations, and other agencies that provide programs or services to individuals and families, or those who aspire to such positions. This graduate certificate program focuses on building knowledge and skills relevant to the supervision, management, and evaluation of social, health, and human service programs. It is designed to be completed in one year and can be delivered in a hybrid or fully online format. The certificate curriculum includes three core courses and one elective for a total of 12 credit hours.
CostPerCredit: Approximately $746.11/credit hour (Texas Resident) - $1,494.11/credit hour (Non-Resident), based on 9 credit hours for 2023-2024 estimated cost of attendance.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Proposal Writing
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Proposal Writing program requires students to meet the general admission requirements for graduate study at UNT. * Baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts must be sent directly to the UNT Toulouse Graduate School. * A GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 undergraduate hours. * Statement of Purpose that explains how the GAC will help the applicant achieve their personal and professional goals. * Students must select one of the following departments as their home department: Biological Sciences, English, Technical Communication.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Proposal Writing is an 18-credit hour program designed to help students develop the critical writing, research, and project management skills needed to effectively secure funding from government agencies, corporations, foundations, and other funding organizations. The certificate is offered through the Department of Technical Communication and is open to both degree-seeking and non-degree-seeking students. Students completing the certificate may be able to apply up to 12 credit hours toward a related master’s degree in technical communication.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Public Relations
Requirements: Admission to the Public Relations Graduate Academic Certificate program requires: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Students who do not meet the GPA requirement may be admitted provisionally. GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores are NOT required for this program. The Graduate School requires international applicants to submit proof of English language proficiency. In addition to the requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School, the following items are required for the Public Relations GAC: Statement of Purpose: Required; Resume: Required; Three letters of recommendation: Required; Writing sample: Required
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: The Public Relations graduate academic certificate program is designed for students seeking to deepen their knowledge in public relations or to add public relations skills to their existing graduate studies. Students will develop a strong foundation in public relations principles, research, strategy, and communication techniques across various platforms. The certificate also emphasizes the ethical responsibilities of public relations professionals and the evolving landscape of digital media.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Qualitative Research
Requirements:
Students interested in the Graduate Academic Certificate in Qualitative Research must first be admitted to the Toulouse Graduate School at the University of North Texas. Requirements for admission to the Toulouse Graduate School include a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the last 60 undergraduate hours.
Students interested in the Graduate Academic Certificate in Qualitative Research should also submit the following directly to the department:
*   Graduate School application
*   Unofficial transcript(s)
*   A brief statement (250-500 words) describing their interest in the Qualitative Research Certificate, any prior qualitative research experience they have, and how they anticipate using the certificate.
Department: College of Education
Description: This certificate is designed for graduate students who wish to develop expertise in qualitative research methods beyond their primary degree program requirements or for professionals who want to enhance their research skills. The certificate offers a structured curriculum that covers various qualitative approaches, data collection techniques, analysis methods, and ethical considerations. Participants will gain practical experience through hands-on projects and fieldwork, preparing them to conduct rigorous and impactful qualitative research in academic, professional, and community settings.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships/Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Doctoral Fellowships, Travel Grants, Tuition/Fee Waivers

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Rehabilitation Counseling advanced certificate
Requirements:
Admission to the certificate program requires:
1. Admission to the Toulouse Graduate School.
2. A master’s degree in counseling, rehabilitation counseling, or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
3. Minimum GPA of 3.0 in master’s course work.
4. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores – official scores required.
5. International applicants must also meet the English Language Proficiency requirements of the Toulouse Graduate School.
6. Students seeking admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Rehabilitation Counseling advanced certificate may also apply for admission to the MA in Counseling program (MA in Counseling with a concentration in Rehabilitation Counseling). In this case, applicants must meet the admission requirements for the MA in Counseling program. All certificate coursework will count toward the MA in Counseling degree.
Department: College of Education
Fees: 6833.28 (estimated total for the 12-credit program for in-state graduate students, based on an average of $569.44/credit hour including tuition and fees from TGS Cost of Attendance example)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate (GAC) in Rehabilitation Counseling advanced certificate is for master’s-level counseling graduates in any counseling specialization seeking to augment their knowledge and skills in rehabilitation counseling. This GAC allows individuals who have already completed a master’s in counseling or a related field (e.g., social work, psychology, human services) to obtain the didactic knowledge necessary to qualify to take the Certified Rehabilitation Counselor (CRC) exam. Enrollment in this GAC does not guarantee eligibility to take the CRC exam, as there are other eligibility requirements unrelated to academic preparation that applicants must meet in order to take the CRC exam. Enrollment in this GAC does not guarantee that individuals will be eligible to become a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) in Texas; individuals who are interested in LPC licensure should refer to the Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council for more information on LPC licensure requirements.
CostPerCredit: 569.44 per credit hour (for in-state, main campus graduate, based on 9 credit hour average including tuition and fees)
ScholarshipAmount: Range of $1,000 - $3,000 (TGS Competitive Scholarship), Range of $3,000 - $12,000 (TGS Excellence Fellowship)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Robotics, Mechatronics and Automation
Requirements: Admission to the certificate program requires admission to the Toulouse Graduate School. In addition to the TGS admission requirements, applicants must: Have a bachelor’s degree in engineering or a closely related field. Have a minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework. Submit a statement of purpose. Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae. Submit two letters of recommendation. Have proficiency in C++ programming language (or an equivalent). This may be demonstrated through coursework, projects, or work experience.
Department: College of Engineering
Fees: $7,458.84/Semester (for a Texas Resident taking all 12 hours in one semester, based on Fall 2023 rates)
Fees.1: $7,458.84/Semester (for a Texas Resident taking all 12 hours in one semester, based on Fall 2023 rates)
Description: A proposal for a new Graduate Academic Certificate in Robotics, Mechatronics and Automation was submitted by the College of Engineering. The proposed certificate addresses the need for engineers who are trained in developing new intelligent automated robotic systems. The 12-hour certificate will provide students with the opportunity to acquire foundational knowledge and skills in robotic systems, mechanical design, control, artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies related to industrial automation. The certificate will prepare professionals to meet the growing demands of modern industry with advanced knowledge and skills in intelligent automation and robotics, specifically focusing on the areas of Robotics, Mechatronics and Automation.
CostPerCredit: $621.57/credit hour (Texas Resident Graduate, Fall 2023 rates, based on 12 SCH load)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Rural Library Management
Requirements: Admission to the certificate program requires applicants to have been admitted to the UNT Graduate School as a graduate student. Admission to the certificate program also requires students to apply to the certificate program. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School admission requirements for all graduate students. Students must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work. The GRE is not required for admission to this certificate program.
Department: Department of Information Science, College of Information
Fees: $8,744.55 (Total for 15-credit hour program for Texas Residents, based on 2023-2024 estimated rates, including tuition and fees)
Fees.1: $8,744.55 (Total for 15-credit hour program for Texas Residents, based on 2023-2024 estimated rates, including tuition and fees)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Rural Library Management is offered by the Department of Information Science. The certificate is intended to provide practicing librarians and library staff working in rural libraries with the knowledge and skills necessary to manage the resources and provide services particular to a rural setting.
CostPerCredit: $582.97 (estimated average per credit hour for Texas Residents taking 9 credit hours/semester, includes fees, 2023-2024 rates)
ScholarshipType: Toulouse Graduate School Scholarships (Recruiting, Outstanding, Travel), Department of Information Science Scholarships, External Funding

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering
Requirements: Admissions requirements and application materials vary by program. Please review your program’s specific requirements. All applicants must meet the UNT Graduate School’s general admission requirements. In addition, applicants to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering program must meet the following program-specific admissions requirements: An earned bachelor’s degree in a STEM field of Engineering (e.g. Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Computer Engineering, Industrial Engineering, etc.), Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, or similar fields from a regionally accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. For international applicants, a TOEFL score of at least 79 (internet-based) or IELTS score of at least 6.5. Resume. Statement of Purpose (up to 500 words). Two letters of recommendation from faculty or individuals who can attest to your academic and research abilities. GRE (General Record Examination) scores are not required for admission. Applicants are encouraged to apply by the priority deadlines to ensure full consideration for scholarships and assistantships. However, applications will be accepted until the final deadlines or until the program is full. For any questions regarding the application process, please contact us at ET-GradStudies@unt.edu.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue a career in the semiconductor manufacturing industry. The program covers topics such as semiconductor device physics, fabrication processes, characterization techniques, and packaging. Students will gain hands-on experience through laboratory work and projects, preparing them for the challenges of working in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry. This certificate can be pursued as a stand-alone credential or as part of a master’s degree program in related engineering fields at UNT.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Specialist in Aging
Requirements:
Students must meet the admission requirements of The Graduate School and the following program requirements:
Baccalaureate degree in any discipline with a minimum 2.8 undergraduate GPA
Current enrollment in a UNT graduate degree program or master's degree (any discipline) from an accredited university
Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended
Statement of Purpose that describes why you are interested in the Specialist in Aging G.A.C.
Two letters of recommendation from faculty, supervisors, or others who can attest to the applicant's academic and/or professional potential.
Resume or CV
Department: Department of Public Health and Recreation in the College of Education
Description: The Specialist in Aging Graduate Academic Certificate is a 15-credit-hour program offered through the Department of Public Health in the College of Health and Public Service. The program is designed for students who already hold a master’s degree and wish to specialize in the field of gerontology or those who are currently seeking a master’s degree in a related field. Students completing the program will gain knowledge and skills relevant to working with older adults in a variety of settings. The certificate is offered primarily online. The College of Health and Public Service is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Accredidation: The College of Health and Public Service is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Storytelling
Requirements: Applicants must submit an application for admission, official transcripts, and other supporting documents to the Toulouse Graduate School. Applicants must meet the admission requirements for a Master's degree (unless waived by the department and Graduate School). Departmental requirements are: Application to the Toulouse Graduate School, All official transcripts, GRE scores (optional), A Statement of Purpose, A writing sample demonstrating scholarly research and writing, An academic CV/Resume.
Department: Mayborn Graduate Institute of Journalism
Fees: $11,968/Year (estimated for 18 credit hours, Texas Resident graduate student)
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Storytelling provides foundational and advanced studies in the theory and practice of storytelling across different genres and media. Students learn to research, develop, produce and perform stories for specific audiences and purposes and across platforms including traditional performance venues, audio, film, television and digital media.
CostPerCredit: $664.89/credit hour (estimated average for Texas Resident graduate student taking 18 hours/year)

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
Requirements: Prospective students seeking to earn the GAC in TESOL must meet the following requirements: 1. Hold an earned bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. 2. Have a 3.0 GPA or higher on the last 60 hours of undergraduate work and in all previous graduate work. 3. Submit a short personal statement (300-500 words) describing your academic and professional background, your interest in the GAC in TESOL, and your professional goals. 4. Submit an unofficial copy of your transcript, or transcripts, from all colleges and universities attended. (The Graduate School requires official transcripts be submitted at the time of application.) 5. International students must meet requirements for admission to the Graduate School, including TOEFL or IELTS scores. (GRE is not required.) 6. Graduate School application. 7. Graduate School application fee.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) provides advanced training in linguistics and applied linguistics to individuals who plan to teach English to non-native speakers of English in the U.S. and abroad. The certificate may be pursued alone or in conjunction with a Master of Arts or Ph.D. in Linguistics. Students can pursue the certificate as a stand-alone certificate, or combine the certificate with another graduate degree. The curriculum includes courses in linguistic theory, research methods, and applications of linguistics to language teaching. The Certificate in TESOL also includes a practicum component that provides hands-on teaching experience for students to apply their knowledge. Students in the program have opportunities to gain practical experience through supervised teaching assignments and internships, preparing them for diverse careers in ESL/EFL instruction, curriculum development, and language program administration.

ProgramName: Graduate Academic Certificate in Technical Writing
Requirements:
Admission to the Graduate Academic Certificate in Technical Writing requires:
*   An undergraduate degree from an accredited institution.
*   An overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale on the last 60 hours of undergraduate coursework OR an overall GPA of 3.0 on any graduate work completed.
*   A minimum score of 4.0 on the Analytical Writing section of the GRE, or a writing sample of 5–10 pages, or a graduate degree.
*   A statement of purpose (1–2 pages) outlining your career and academic goals and how this certificate will help you achieve them.
*   Current resume or curriculum vitae.
*   All applicants must submit additional application materials through the UNT Toulouse Graduate School.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Fees.1: Resident: $11,040.50 for 15 credit hours; Non-Resident: $22,488.50 for 15 credit hours
Description: The Graduate Academic Certificate in Technical Writing prepares students for careers in technical communication and helps them improve their skills in the workplace. The certificate provides advanced instruction in the rhetorical principles and practices of designing, writing and editing professional documents for both print and digital delivery. It is an excellent credential for individuals working in professions that require strong communication skills, for students completing a graduate degree at UNT, or for professionals with undergraduate degrees who wish to gain graduate-level credentials in technical writing.

ProgramName: Certificate of Advanced Study in Library Science
Requirements: Admission to the Certificate of Advanced Study program in Library Science requires: A master’s degree in library and information science (or equivalent) from an American Library Association-accredited program with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Demonstrated professional library experience. Three letters of recommendation. Statement of purpose. Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV) is required. Official transcripts for all college course work. GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. International applicants must submit a TOEFL score of 79 or an IELTS score of 6.5. Applicants who have completed an undergraduate degree at an accredited U.S. institution are exempt from this requirement.
Department: College of Information
Description: This certificate is for students who have a master’s degree from an American Library Association (ALA) accredited program and wish to broaden or update their knowledge, specialize in an area not covered by their master’s degree, or to prepare for doctoral study. Students take 21 hours of graduate level courses from a personalized curriculum developed in consultation with a faculty advisor.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Departmental, Research, Teaching, Travel, International student specific

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting,
Department: College of Business
Description: The accounting program helps students prepare for a variety of careers in accounting, finance and business, including positions as CPAs, auditors, tax accountants, financial analysts and forensic accountants. The Bachelor of Science degree in accounting prepares students to pursue certification as a CPA in Texas or in other states that require 150 hours of college credit. The program satisfies the undergraduate requirements for admission to the Master of Science degree in accounting or the MBA with a concentration in accounting. The BS in accounting provides a broad understanding of accounting issues for those who plan to pursue careers in accounting and business. In addition, the program serves as a strong foundation for students who plan to pursue graduate studies in accounting, business, or law. The program is accredited by AACSB International.
Accredidation: Accredited by AACSB International.
ScholarshipType: Academic Merit, Leadership, Extracurricular Activities, Special Talents, Financial Need

ProgramName: Accounting, BS/MS
Requirements: Students should apply to the BS/MS program during their junior year. They must have completed at least 60 hours toward a bachelor's degree at the time of application. Students must apply for admission to the College of Business, G. Brint Ryan College of Business Department of Accounting, and the Toulouse Graduate School. The requirements for admission to the BS/MS program are: Overall GPA of 3.25 or greater; GPA of 3.25 or greater in all accounting courses (ACCT 3110, ACCT 3210, ACCT 3310, ACCT 3410 and ACCT 4400); GPA of 3.25 or greater in all professional field of study courses (BANA 2010, BANA 2030, BCIS 3610, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 3770, MGMT 3830 and MKTG 3650); Applicants must complete the GMAT or GRE (with a combined verbal and quantitative score of 300 on the revised GRE or 1000 on the old GRE, or a GMAT score of 500) and must apply for graduate admission to the Toulouse Graduate School. Students must satisfy the minimum requirements for admission to the graduate program.
Department: College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Science/Master of Science in accounting (BS/MS) program is designed for students seeking to qualify for the Uniform CPA Examination while simultaneously earning both a bachelor’s degree and a master’s degree in a focused and efficient timeframe. The BS/MS accounting program offers high-ability students the opportunity to earn both degrees in as little as five years. Students applying for the BS/MS accounting program must select a graduate major: Accounting, MS, or Taxation, MS. For specific requirements for these programs, please refer to the College of Business, Department of Accounting, website. Admission to the BS/MS program is competitive and requires a separate application from the general university admission process.

ProgramName: Acoustics (Minor)
Department: College of Science
Description: The minor in acoustics is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a basic understanding of acoustical principles. The minor is offered by the College of Engineering and the College of Music in collaboration with the Department of Physics. Students completing this minor will gain knowledge in the measurement, analysis, and perception of sound, and will be prepared to apply this knowledge to a wide variety of careers including architectural acoustics, audio engineering, environmental noise, and biomedical acoustics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Addiction Studies,
Department: College of Education
Description: Addiction is one of society's most complex and challenging problems. It is an epidemic that impacts individuals, families, communities, and nations. The University of North Texas has developed a comprehensive Bachelor of Science degree in Addiction Studies to prepare students to be leaders in the addiction profession. This program provides a strong foundation in addiction theory, prevention, treatment, and recovery. Students will learn about the biological, psychological, sociological, and spiritual aspects of addiction, as well as the legal and ethical considerations of working with individuals and families affected by addiction. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practices, cultural competence, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Upon completion of the program, students will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the addiction field, including addiction counselor, prevention specialist, case manager, and recovery coach. The program also provides a solid foundation for graduate studies in addiction, counseling, social work, and related fields.

ProgramName: Addiction Studies (Minor)
Requirements: A minimum of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced, is required for the minor. A minimum of 6 advanced hours must be completed at UNT. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required on all courses that apply to the minor. Students must meet the university requirements for minors. Courses to be applied to the minor may not be taken on a pass/no pass basis. The minor is open to all majors. The minor is only available to undergraduate students. Students interested in a minor in Addiction Studies should contact the Department of Behavior Analysis.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Fees: $6,373.00/Semester (based on 15 SCH for Texas Resident Undergraduate, 2023-2024)
Description: The Addiction Studies minor, housed in the Department of Rehabilitation and Health Services, provides students with an understanding of addictive behaviors. The minor is designed to serve students interested in working in the addiction field. The curriculum provides core competencies required for certification as an LCDC (Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor) in Texas. Students are responsible for verifying specific certification requirements with the Texas Health and Human Services Commission.
CostPerCredit: $424.87/Credit (estimated, based on 15 SCH for Texas Resident Undergraduate, 2023-2024)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Advertising,
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in advertising emphasizes creativity and problem-solving skills in developing advertising messages for a variety of media. Students learn strategic planning, media placement and research in preparation for careers as advertising professionals. Advertising faculty members have extensive professional experience and actively engage students in creative work and research. Many students gain professional experience through internships at advertising agencies or with corporate marketing departments. The major prepares students for careers in media planning, account management, creative services, production, research and other areas in advertising.

ProgramName: Advertising (Minor)
Department: College of Business
ScholarshipType: Presidential Scholarships, UNT Excellence Scholarships, Transfer Excellence Scholarships, various departmental scholarships, private scholarships

ProgramName: Aerospace Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Aerospace Studies minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of aerospace power and its role in national security. Students will learn about the history of air power, the development of military aviation, and the organization and operations of the United States Air Force and Space Force. The minor complements a wide range of academic majors, offering a unique perspective on leadership, global affairs, and technological advancement within the aerospace domain. It also serves as an excellent foundation for students considering a commission in the U.S. Air Force or U.S. Space Force through the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC) program, though enrollment in AFROTC is not required to pursue the minor.

ProgramName: Africana Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Africana Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a systematic and critical understanding of the experiences of African peoples in the United States, Africa, and the Caribbean. Drawing primarily upon the insights and methods of the social sciences and humanities, the curriculum focuses on topics such as the history of African peoples, socio-economic and political developments, cultural forms, and gender issues. The minor provides an excellent foundation for students interested in careers in teaching, government, law, social work, business, journalism, or public policy. It is also an excellent option for students planning to pursue graduate studies in Africana studies or related fields.

ProgramName: American Sign Language (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

ProgramName: American Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The American Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a broad understanding of American culture through a wide variety of courses in the humanities, social sciences and fine arts. The minor helps students develop critical and analytical skills that prepare them for a variety of careers in fields such as business, education, government, journalism, law, public administration, and social work. The minor in American Studies offers a strong background for graduate study in American Studies, history, literature, and other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in anthropology requires a minimum of 120 credit hours, 42 of which must be advanced, and fulfillment of the university's core curriculum requirements. The degree program is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the four fields of anthropology: archaeology, cultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology and physical anthropology.

ProgramName: Anthropology (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
CostPerCredit: Resident Undergraduate: $399.66/semester credit hour (combined tuition and fees for Fall 2023 / Spring 2024 / Summer 2024)

ProgramName: Associate of Applied Science in Applied Arts and Sciences, B
Requirements: Admission to the university is a separate administrative process governed by the university’s Office of Admissions. For admission requirements, deadlines and instructions, please see Undergraduate Admission under the Admissions section of this catalog or visit the website for the Office of Admissions. This program is designed for students who are highly motivated to earn a bachelor's degree but have some college credit, or extensive experience (such as military or vocational training), and have been unsuccessful in achieving a bachelor's degree.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences (BAAS) is an interdisciplinary degree designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Arts and Sciences (AAAS), Associate of Applied Science (AAS) or other applied associate’s degree and desire to complete a bachelor’s degree. The degree provides an opportunity for career and technical education courses to apply toward a bachelor’s degree program. Students must complete 36 hours of upper-division courses, of which 18 hours must be in one of the following specializations or 18 hours of upper-division courses approved by an advisor if no specialization is chosen or available. The remaining 18 hours of upper-division courses may be chosen from other specializations offered through the BAAS program or from other approved upper-division course work in order to complete the 36 hours.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Behavior Analysis,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) provides students with a strong academic background, including conceptual knowledge of behavior analysis and practical skills for working in areas requiring the application of behavior analytic principles. Applied behavior analysis is the scientific study of human behavior with a focus on understanding why people do what they do and how to help people acquire new skills and change behavior. The curriculum is designed to provide coursework needed for students to become a Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst® (BCaBA®), an undergraduate-level certification provided by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB®). Students graduating with this degree will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the field, including those working with individuals with autism spectrum disorder and related disabilities, traumatic brain injury, organizational behavior management, and behavioral medicine. The program prepares students for graduate study in behavior analysis or other related fields.

ProgramName: Applied Gerontology (Minor)
Requirements: A minor in applied gerontology is available to all undergraduate students. Students must complete 18 semester hours of course work, with a minimum of 9 hours at the advanced level. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required on all courses counted toward the minor. A minimum grade of C is required for all minor courses. Students must complete: ADSU 3000, ADSU 3010, ADSU 4100. Choose 9 hours from the following: ADSU 4000, ADSU 4010, ADSU 4050, ADSU 4060, ADSU 4070.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Applied Gerontology minor provides students with a broad knowledge base regarding the process of aging and older adults. Students gain an understanding of the physiological, psychological, and sociological aspects of aging, and learn about policy, services, and programs for older adults. This minor is an excellent complement to many majors across the university (e.g., health studies, psychology, sociology, hospitality, recreation, business, public health, nursing, nutrition, social work).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art Education,
Requirements: Admission to the university is a separate process from admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design. Consult the Admission section of the catalog for more information. Admission to CVAD B.A. and B.F.A. Programs: Freshmen must be admitted to the university. Transfer students must be admitted to the university. CVAD requirements for admission for freshmen and transfer students are listed below. Freshmen: Must have a high school cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale. Transfer students: Must have completed 12 or more transferable hours, have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (including all transfer work), and be in good standing at the last institution attended. Students not meeting the above requirements will need to submit a portfolio for review for admission to the college. Contact the CVAD Dean’s office for more information. Admission to the university and the CVAD undergraduate program does not guarantee admission into a particular undergraduate major within the college. Specific program/major admission requirements are listed under their corresponding program pages in the catalog.
Department: College of Visual Arts & Design
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Art Education is a professional degree providing a strong studio-based curriculum with a focus on preparing highly qualified art teachers for all levels of public and private schools. This degree combines professional education and studio art to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to become successful art educators. Art education majors will develop their artistic voice through study in a broad range of studio disciplines including drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, new media, and ceramics. The Art Education program is designed to fulfill the requirements for the Texas All-Level (EC-12) Art Teacher Certification.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Major-specific, Residency-specific, Extracurricular involvement-specific

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History,
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Concentration: Art Museum Education, Fashion History, Pre-Art Conservation
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Art History provides students with a broad and deep education in art and its history. The program prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, cultural institutions, and education, or for advanced studies in art history, museum studies, or related fields. Students develop critical thinking, visual analysis, research, and writing skills as they explore art from diverse cultures and periods.
CostPerCredit: $690.44/Credit Hour (for 9 hours, Texas residents, Fall 2023/Spring 2024 average)

ProgramName: Art History (Minor)
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: This minor is designed to supplement other majors. The student who majors in art studio, communication design or visual art studies will find the minor in art history gives breadth to a course of study and prepares the student for graduate work in art history. Students who major in other areas will find the minor in art history a useful and enlightening complement to other majors.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence,
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a first-time in college student, applicants must be a graduate of an accredited high school or possess a GED certificate, meet the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) requirements (completion of the Foundation, Recommended, or Distinguished high school program), and submit official transcripts from all high school(s) attended. Applicants must submit official test scores from the SAT or ACT; however, a test-optional pathway is available for eligible applicants.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Artificial Intelligence prepares students for careers in the rapidly growing field of AI, including machine learning, deep learning, data science, robotics, computer vision, natural language processing, and other emerging AI areas. This program offers a comprehensive curriculum covering the theoretical foundations, algorithms, and practical applications of AI. It emphasizes hands-on experience through projects and laboratory work, equipping students with the skills to design, develop, and deploy intelligent systems. Graduates will be prepared for various roles in industry, government, and research, as well as for further graduate studies in AI and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology,
Requirements: Complete 45 semester hours of college coursework, including the UNT core courses, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75. Complete all pre-major course requirements (ASLP 1040, BIOL 1710, BIOL 1720, PSYC 1630, TECM 2700) with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75. ASLP 1040 and PSYC 1630 must be completed with a minimum grade of C or better. Achieve a minimum grade of C or better in all pre-major courses (ASLP 1040, BIOL 1710, BIOL 1720, PSYC 1630, TECM 2700) and other courses taken for the major.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: This major prepares students for graduate study and careers in audiology and speech-language pathology by providing a strong science-based foundation. Graduate study is required for certification and licensure as an audiologist or speech-language pathologist. The faculty are committed to providing students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue a graduate degree and to succeed as professionals. The curriculum combines basic science courses with general education and core courses in communication disorders. Students who successfully complete the undergraduate program are prepared to enter graduate programs in audiology (Au.D.) and speech-language pathology (M.S.).
ScholarshipType: academic achievement, demonstrated financial need, participation in specific organizations or activities, or because of a particular field of study

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aviation Logistics,
Requirements: Students must meet the admission requirements for the College of Engineering. All students must meet university admission requirements. In addition to university requirements, the College of Engineering has specific academic requirements for unconditional admission directly into a major. For assured admission, freshmen entering the College of Engineering must meet the same academic qualifications as listed in the general Undergraduate Admission section of the catalog, but with higher math readiness. Freshmen must be calculus ready to be admitted into an engineering major. Calculus ready means eligible to enroll in MATH 1710 Calculus I (C or better in MATH 1650 Pre-Calculus or MATH 1600 Elementary Probability and Statistics, or MATH 1710 placement test).
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Aviation Logistics program at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare students for management and operational careers in the aviation industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in aviation, business, and logistics principles, focusing on the unique challenges and opportunities within the aerospace sector. Students will gain expertise in areas such as airline operations, airport management, supply chain logistics, regulatory compliance, safety management, and aviation finance. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and leadership skills, equipping graduates to effectively manage resources, optimize operations, and contribute to the efficiency and sustainability of aviation organizations. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, hands-on projects, and opportunities for internships, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the global aviation industry and be prepared for diverse roles in airlines, airports, MROs (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul facilities), aerospace manufacturing, and governmental agencies.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $50/credit hour (base tuition); Non-Resident: $457/credit hour (base tuition)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry,
Requirements:
First-time freshmen are students who have earned a high school diploma (or GED) and who have completed fewer than 12 college credit hours after high school graduation.

Applying for Admission:
Apply online using the ApplyTexas Application at goapplytexas.org or the Common App at commonapp.org.
Send Official High School Transcript
Send Official ACT/SAT Scores (UNT ACT school code 4240, UNT SAT school code 6481)

Automatic Admission:
Freshmen are automatically admitted to UNT if they meet one of the following requirements:
Beginning Fall 2023, students in the top 10% of their graduating class will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the top 25% of their class who have an SAT score of 1030 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 20 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the top 50% of their class who have an SAT score of 1130 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 23 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.
Beginning Fall 2023, students graduating in the third quartile (50.1-75%) of their class who have an SAT score of 1230 (Math + Critical Reading) or an ACT composite of 26 or higher will be automatically admitted to UNT.

Individual Review:
Applicants who do not meet the above automatic admission requirements will be reviewed individually for admission. Applicants for individual review are generally strong students who may not meet automatic admission requirements. When conducting an individual review, the Admissions Office considers a number of factors, including high school courses and grades, SAT/ACT scores, essays, extracurricular activities, leadership positions, community service, work experience, special talents, and other factors.
Department: College of Science
Description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical and physical processes that occur within living organisms. It is a fundamental discipline that is at the heart of the biological sciences. The interdisciplinary nature of biochemistry means that students are well prepared for careers in fields such as health care, forensics, environmental science, and pharmaceutical research and development. The Biochemistry BA program provides a solid foundation for further study in graduate or professional school. The Biochemistry program is designed to provide students with a strong background in the molecular sciences and quantitative skills. The curriculum includes courses in general and organic chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, and biochemistry. Through laboratory experiences, students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills that are essential for success in a wide range of careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry,
Requirements: You may be admitted to UNT as an entering freshman if you meet ONE of the following requirements: 1. Assured Admission: Rank in the top 25% of your high school class AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); OR have an SAT score of 1200 or higher (combined Critical Reading and Math scores) or an ACT composite score of 26 or higher AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP). 2. Individual Review: If you don't meet the assured admission requirements, your application will be reviewed individually. To be considered for individual review, you must: Rank in the top 50% of your high school class AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); OR have an SAT score of 1030 or higher (combined Critical Reading and Math scores) or an ACT composite score of 20 or higher AND satisfy the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP); AND have a minimum of a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Additional items such as essays, letters of recommendation, and a resume may be requested. SAT or ACT scores are required for freshman applicants unless specifically stated otherwise for certain waivers.
Department: College of Science
Description: The biochemistry program offers students the opportunity to learn about the chemical processes occurring in living systems. Biochemistry is a central science that bridges biology and chemistry. Understanding biochemistry is critical to making advances in fields such as medicine, biotechnology, agriculture and environmental science. In addition to gaining a fundamental understanding of life processes, the biochemistry major prepares students for graduate study in biochemistry, chemistry or cell/molecular biology, or for professional schools such as medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine. It also provides an excellent foundation for immediate employment in biotechnology, pharmacology, environmental science or laboratory research.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Specific talents or interests

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biology,
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Biology is a liberal arts degree primarily intended for students preparing for careers in the health professions, secondary teaching, environmental sciences, or business. This program emphasizes a broad background in biology with supporting work in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Students may apply for admission to graduate programs in various areas of biology and the health sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology,
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Biology is designed for students who desire a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics. The curriculum provides the necessary breadth of knowledge and training in the major areas of biology to prepare students for successful entry into graduate school, medical and other health-related professional programs, or science-related careers. All students are advised to meet with an academic advisor in the Department of Biological Sciences each semester. A comprehensive listing of all requirements can be found in the current University of North Texas Undergraduate Catalog and by consulting with an academic advisor.

ProgramName: Biology (Minor)
Department: College of Science
Description: The minor in biology requires a minimum of 18 hours in biology, of which 6 hours must be advanced (3000- or 4000-level).
ScholarshipType: Federal Pell Grant, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant, Federal Work-Study, Texas Public Education Grant, Texas Grant, Texas Educational Opportunity Grant, UNT Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering,
Requirements:
All students officially admitted to the university will be admitted to the College of Engineering and will be advised by the college staff. During the first two years, students in the Biomedical Engineering program follow a common pre-professional curriculum. Students formally apply for admission to the professional program within the department after successful completion of the pre-professional curriculum.
Admission to the professional program requires completion of at least 30 semester hours of course work applicable to the biomedical engineering degree with a minimum 2.5 GPA in all math, science and engineering courses taken at UNT and a minimum 2.5 overall GPA in all courses taken at UNT. Transfer students with 30 or more hours must also meet these requirements based on all courses taken at UNT. All students must complete ENGR 1304, PHYS 1710/1730, CHEM 1410/1430, MATH 1710, MATH 1720, and ENGR 2304 with a minimum grade of C.
Students must meet with their academic advisor to formally apply to the professional program.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Biomedical Engineering combines fundamental engineering principles with biology and medicine to create new knowledge and technology to improve health outcomes and quality of life. Biomedical Engineers apply engineering concepts and methods to solve problems in biology and medicine. This can include the design of medical instruments, artificial organs, prostheses, and systems that deliver health care. The biomedical engineering curriculum provides students with a strong background in engineering science and design, mathematics, and physical and biological sciences and provides the necessary foundation for a career as a practicing biomedical engineer or for graduate studies in engineering, medicine, or other health sciences.
Accredidation: The Biomedical Engineering Program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

ProgramName: British and Irish Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The British and Irish Studies minor provides students with the opportunity to examine the interdisciplinary aspects of British and Irish culture. The minor examines the rich traditions and enduring impact of two of the world’s most influential cultures. The program is designed for students seeking to complement their major with studies in British and Irish history, literature, politics, and culture.

ProgramName: Business Analytics, BBA
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: Business analytics is the practice of iterative, methodical exploration of an organization’s data, with an emphasis on statistical analysis, to drive decision-making. Business analytics is used to gain insights that inform business decisions. Analytics tools and techniques are used to explore data, understand past performance, and predict future outcomes. The BBA in Business Analytics prepares students to work in any industry to improve business performance using data-driven insights. Students learn how to collect, manage and analyze data and interpret the results to provide decision makers with the insights needed to improve business processes and grow revenue.
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

ProgramName: Business Analytics (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: A minor in Business Analytics for non-business majors is awarded to students who complete 18 hours in approved courses. Minor Requirements: Minimum 2.0 GPA in minor courses. Minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses completed at UNT. Must have completed 60 hours. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. None of the minor courses may be taken pass/no pass. Students must complete the statistics prerequisite with a C or better prior to enrolling in BANA 3000.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business

ProgramName: Business Computer Information Systems (Minor)
Department: College of Business
Description: The Minor in Business Computer Information Systems provides students with foundational knowledge in information systems relevant to business operations. Students will gain an understanding of database management, systems analysis and design, and business programming concepts, preparing them for roles where technology intersects with business strategy. This minor complements a wide range of majors by enhancing students' analytical and technical skills in an increasingly data-driven world.

ProgramName: Business Integrated Studies, BBA
Requirements: Admission to the university is the first step toward becoming a student at UNT. Detailed information is available at https://admissions.unt.edu/apply. In addition to satisfying university admission requirements, students must meet minimum requirements to be admitted to the G. Brint Ryan College of Business as a business major. To declare a business major, students must meet the following requirements: Be in good standing with the university; Have completed a minimum of 45 semester credit hours; Have completed the following courses with a minimum grade of C in each: ACCT 2010/2020, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100/1110, DSCI 2710/2810, MATH 1190/1321, and ENGL 1310/1320; Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all college credit hours attempted.
Department: College of Business
Fees: Texas Resident: $10,200/Year; Non-Resident: $20,010/Year (for 15 credit hours/semester, tuition & mandatory fees)
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $98/credit hour; Non-Resident: $425/credit hour (Tuition only)

ProgramName: Business (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: Must have a minimum 2.0 UNT GPA.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: A minor in business is offered to students in non-business majors. Students interested in this minor should contact the office of the G. Brint Ryan College of Business for advising information.

ProgramName: Business/Public Administration (Minor for non-business majors)
Department: College of Business
Description: The minor in Business/Public Administration is designed for non-business majors interested in acquiring some general business knowledge. This minor requires 18 hours of course work in general business topics that are beneficial in almost any career.

ProgramName: Catholic Campus Ministry (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry,
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in chemistry is a more flexible degree program requiring fewer total chemistry hours than the Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in chemistry. The BA degree is recommended for students preparing for careers such as those in the health professions (pre-medicine, pre-dentistry, etc.), patent law, business, science writing or secondary science teaching. Graduate study in chemistry would require taking more than the minimum number of chemistry courses required for the BA degree. Students planning graduate work in chemistry should consult with a chemistry advisor or consider the BS in chemistry degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry,
Department: College of Science
Description: The Department of Chemistry offers an undergraduate program leading to the Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science degrees. Both are designed to provide students with a strong background in chemistry, either as a terminal degree or as preparation for further professional or graduate study. Students seeking a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry can be certified to the American Chemical Society (ACS) by completing 15 hours of courses beyond the basic chemistry curriculum.
Accredidation: American Chemical Society (ACS) Approved, with certification option upon completion of specific coursework.
ScholarshipType: State Grants, Institutional Grants, General Scholarships

ProgramName: Chemistry (Minor)
Department: College of Science
Description: The minor in chemistry is designed primarily for students in biology and related health professions. The minor is also appropriate for students who wish to supplement their major with a strong background in chemistry.
CostPerCredit: approx. $379.44/credit hour (for Texas Resident Undergraduate, based on 18 SCH load, Fall 2023 rates)

ProgramName: Child Development and Family Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Education
Description: The Minor in Child Development and Family Studies requires 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). At least 9 hours must be taken at UNT. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor. For more information regarding a specific course, please consult the UNT undergraduate catalog. Required courses: CDFS 2310, CDFS 2340, CDFS 3313, CDFS 3360, CDFS 4333. One advanced CDFS elective (3000/4000 level).
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, financial need, specific talents or interests

ProgramName: Chinese (Minor)
Requirements: A minimum of 18 semester hours in Chinese courses, including CHIN 1010, CHIN 1020, CHIN 2040, CHIN 2050, and 6 advanced semester hours selected from CHIN 3010, CHIN 3020, CHIN 3030, CHIN 3040, CHIN 3050, CHIN 3060, CHIN 3070, CHIN 3080, CHIN 3090, CHIN 3091, CHIN 3092, CHIN 3093, CHIN 3094, CHIN 3095, CHIN 3096, CHIN 3097, CHIN 4010, CHIN 4020, CHIN 4040, CHIN 4050, CHIN 4060, CHIN 4070. Students must complete the language sequence through CHIN 2050 at UNT, or demonstrate equivalent proficiency by examination or transfer credit. A minimum of 6 semester hours of the 18 hours required for the minor must be completed at UNT. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required on all courses counted toward the minor.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Classical Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in Classical Studies provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the world of the Greeks and Romans and its legacy. Students choose from a range of courses in history, art history, philosophy, and classical languages. The minor allows students to apply classical perspectives to their own lives and the modern world.
CostPerCredit: 488.00 USD/credit hour (estimated average for Resident Undergraduate taking 12+ hours for 2023-2024 academic year)
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership, Community service, Program-specific

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Communication Design,
Requirements: Admission to the BFA in Communication Design is a competitive process and is based on performance in foundation-level visual arts and design courses, submission of a portfolio of work, and academic performance. Students interested in applying to the BFA in Communication Design must first be admitted to the University of North Texas. Students apply to the BFA in Communication Design upon successful completion of the Foundation Year (ART 1301, ART 1302, ART 1303, ART 1304, ART 1305, ART 1306, ART 1307 and ART 1308), and ART 2307 and ART 2308. Students must earn a grade of B or better in each of the following courses: ART 1302, ART 1303, ART 1304, ART 1305, ART 2307 and ART 2308, and maintain a minimum 2.75 GPA. Transfer students must take the equivalents of the UNT courses to be eligible to apply. All applicants must be in good academic standing. Admission to the BFA Communication Design program is for the fall semester only. Applications are due the last Friday in February. Students must submit a portfolio for review. Instructions for the portfolio and application can be found at the CVAD Communication Design website.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: Communication Design students learn to develop strategic visual solutions across various media, including print, screen, and emerging technologies. Graduates are prepared for professional practice in fields such as graphic design, interaction design, web design, app design, information architecture, user experience design, and motion graphics. Communication Design is a professional program within the College of Visual Arts and Design. Students learn design principles, theories, and processes applied to visual communication. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and creative execution relevant to contemporary design practices. Students select either a Graphic Design or an Interaction Design concentration.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, special talents, financial need

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Communication Studies program gives students opportunities to understand the communication process, to improve their communication abilities, and to apply those skills in a variety of contexts. It emphasizes the development of critical thinking, problem solving, listening, speaking, reading and writing skills. Because Communication Studies is a versatile degree, students are able to pursue a variety of careers in fields such as business and industry, government, law, education, health and social services, media, and the arts. Students acquire a strong theoretical and practical knowledge of the communication discipline. Emphasis is on acquiring effective communication skills in interpersonal, group, organizational, public and intercultural settings. The program helps students develop skills in analyzing, designing and evaluating messages.
ScholarshipType: Institutional, State, Endowed, Departmental, General Academic, Distinguished, Transfer, Non-resident tuition waivers

ProgramName: Communication Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in Communication Studies provides students with a broad understanding of the role of communication in society and in human interaction. Course work in the minor focuses on communication theory, research and processes, and develops students’ abilities to think critically about communication problems, messages and effects.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership, Special talent, Institutional, Departmental, External

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering,
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Computer engineering is a discipline that bridges electrical engineering and computer science, combining hardware and software aspects. Computer engineers design and develop computer systems and other technological devices. The computer engineering curriculum includes topics such as computer organization and architecture, microprocessors, digital logic design, computer networks, and embedded systems. With a degree in computer engineering, students can pursue careers in areas such as computer hardware design, embedded systems development, network engineering, and cybersecurity.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree program in Computer Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science,
Requirements: UNT is test-optional for students applying for fall 2024 and beyond. If you choose not to submit test scores, we’ll make an admission decision based on your high school GPA and class rank, if available. Some students who choose not to submit test scores may be required to participate in an admission interview. If you choose to submit test scores, they can be used in your admission review process if they meet our requirements or can be considered for scholarship eligibility. UNT also uses the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) which states that all students are eligible for automatic admission if they graduate in the top 10% of their high school class. The required documents for freshman applicants are: Application for admission (ApplyTexas or Common App), Official high school transcript, Official SAT or ACT scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and beyond), Application fee or fee waiver.
Department: College of Engineering
Fees: $11,560/Year (estimated for Texas Resident, full-time undergraduate, 2023-2024 academic year)
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science requires 120 credit hours for the degree. It has a strong math and science component and requires a minor outside the department. This degree is designed to prepare students for careers in applications programming, database administration, information technology, web development, research and development, and advanced studies in computer science. Graduates may work in government, education, business or industry.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $343/semester hour; Non-Resident: $733/semester hour (tuition component, excludes other fees)
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, financial need, leadership, special talent, specific major

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science,
Requirements: Students interested in declaring a major in Computer Science or Information Technology must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements for the university. Admission to the university is based on the strength of academic preparation and performance in high school. A freshman applicant is eligible for admission if they meet the general admission requirements. Automatic Admission criteria include: top 10% class rank, OR a minimum of 1030 on the SAT (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math) with at least a 500 in Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, OR a minimum composite score of 20 on the ACT with at least a 16 on the English and Math sections. Applicants not meeting automatic admission criteria will be individually reviewed based on high school coursework, essay, and extracurricular activities, as well as test scores and class rank. Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for all freshmen. Essay, resume, and letters of recommendation are optional and will be reviewed if submitted.
Department: College of Engineering
Fees: Resident: $4,366.00/Semester (based on 15 hours); Non-Resident: $9,916.00/Semester (based on 15 hours)
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Computer Science is designed to prepare students for a career in software development and related areas or for graduate study in computer science. Students in the program receive a solid foundation in both the theoretical and applied aspects of computer science. The curriculum includes courses in programming languages, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering. Technical electives allow students to specialize in areas such as artificial intelligence, computer graphics, computer networks, cyber security, database systems, and mobile application development. The BS program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.
ScholarshipType: Institutional, Private Donor, State scholarships; based on academic merit, leadership, artistic talent, athletic skills, and/or financial need.

ProgramName: Computer Science (Minor)
Department: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, College of Engineering
Description: A minor in computer science offers the opportunity to acquire basic understanding of problem-solving techniques using the computer. A knowledge of computer science is invaluable in today's job market, regardless of the major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Construction Engineering Technology,
Requirements:
Students must meet the university requirements for admission (see Undergraduate Admissions). Students must be admitted to the College of Engineering for this program. Students must meet the following minimum requirements for admission to the College of Engineering and degree program:
*   Completion of all courses in the Freshman Year curriculum with a grade of C or better.
*   A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50.
*   A minimum GPA of 2.50 in all math and science courses.
*   Admission to the university and the College of Engineering is required for students to take courses beyond the freshman year curriculum.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Construction Engineering Technology (CET) provides the knowledge and skills for managing the construction process. The curriculum emphasizes the application of scientific and engineering principles to the construction of civil, residential, industrial, and commercial facilities. The program provides the graduate with the technical and managerial skills for careers in construction project management, field supervision, estimating, scheduling, quality control, materials testing and inspection, and safety. The program requires 120 credit hours.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Construction Management,
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Construction Management (CM) prepares students for professional careers in the construction industry. Construction is the nation’s largest single industry and professionals working in CM apply business, scientific, engineering, and technology principles to solve the challenges associated with the delivery of complex construction projects. The CM program at UNT is a business-centric program housed in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business that focuses on the business, management, and technology of construction. Graduates will be able to contribute to project delivery immediately upon graduation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Consumer Experience Management,
Requirements: Applicants seeking admission to the Consumer Experience Management, BS program must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements of the university. Required application materials for first-year students include ApplyTexas or Common App, Application Fee, and Official High School Transcript. Official SAT/ACT Scores, Essays, and Letters of Recommendation are optional.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Fees: $5,948.50/Semester (Estimated Resident Undergraduate Tuition & Fees for 15 SCH/Semester, 2023-2024 Academic Year)
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Consumer Experience Management (CEM) focuses on the strategies and skills necessary to create positive consumer experiences in a dynamic, global, customer-centric environment. The CEM program integrates experiential learning opportunities that prepare graduates to meet the needs of diverse consumers throughout the consumer journey. The curriculum helps students develop critical and creative thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, and competencies in professional communication and teamwork. Graduates are prepared for careers that involve understanding, engaging and managing consumer experiences across various industries including retail, services, hospitality, tourism, nonprofit, and healthcare. Graduates will find jobs in organizations in areas such as consumer experience management, market research, brand management, data analysis, business development, and customer relationship management.
CostPerCredit: $396.56/Credit Hour (Estimated Resident Undergraduate Tuition & Fees, 2023-2024 Academic Year)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Converged Broadcast Media,
Requirements: Admission to the Mayborn School of Journalism for the Converged Broadcast Media major requires a minimum 2.5 GPA on all college work and an application. Students must have completed 45 semester hours of college credit, 12 of which must be UNT journalism courses including JOUR 2050 (Media Writing) and JOUR 2070 (History of American American Journalism), with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Students must also pass a skills test. Students must submit an application to the Mayborn School of Journalism by May 1 for fall admission or December 1 for spring admission.
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
