Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in Converged Broadcast Media is offered by the Department of Media Arts. The curriculum is designed to produce graduates capable of creating professional audio, video and interactive media for broadcast, streaming and online distribution. It prepares students for careers in the dynamic media production and distribution fields, including positions as producers, directors, writers, editors, photojournalists, talent, content creators, and marketing/promotions professionals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice,
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The bachelor of science degree in criminal justice provides students with an understanding of the causes of crime, the nature of offenders and victims, and the various components of the criminal justice system. The program provides the knowledge and skills necessary for effective and efficient performance in the criminal justice system and in related occupations. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to the field of criminal justice and to develop their analytical and critical thinking skills. It also serves as a foundation for graduate study in criminal justice and related disciplines.

ProgramName: Criminal Justice (Minor)
Requirements: Students must have a minimum 2.0 UNT GPA to declare the minor. The minor can be declared online via my.unt.edu. You can access the online minor/certificate declaration form through your Student Quicklinks. For additional help, please call the main CJUS office at 940-565-3450 or email cjus@unt.edu.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The minor in criminal justice is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in criminal justice or a related field, but whose major is in another area of study. The minor provides students with a foundational understanding of the criminal justice system, including law enforcement, courts, and corrections, as well as an introduction to criminal behavior and relevant social science theories. Students will develop critical thinking skills and an understanding of ethical issues in criminal justice. The minor is flexible and can be tailored to meet the individual interests of students.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Institutional, Departmental, Privately funded, Endowed

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity,
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the theoretical and practical aspects of cybersecurity. Cybersecurity is a critical field focused on protecting computer systems, networks, and data from digital attacks and unauthorized access. This program equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand, identify, and mitigate cybersecurity threats, ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of information. Students will gain expertise in areas such as network security, secure software development, cryptography, digital forensics, ethical hacking, risk management, and compliance. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience, problem-solving, and critical thinking, preparing graduates for a wide range of careers in both the public and private sectors, including roles as cybersecurity analysts, security engineers, incident responders, and forensic specialists. The program is committed to producing highly skilled cybersecurity professionals capable of addressing the complex challenges of the evolving cyber landscape.
ScholarshipType: ['Academic Scholarships', 'Competitive Scholarships', 'College, School and Departmental Scholarships']

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dance,
Requirements: All prospective dance majors must audition for the dance faculty. Acceptance into the dance program is by audition only. Acceptance into the Dance BA program is contingent upon acceptance to the university. University admission for freshmen is based on a holistic review process, considering academic performance (class rank and grades), rigor of curriculum, standardized test scores (optional for Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Summer 2025 and Fall 2025 freshman applicants), and essays (optional for Spring 2025, Summer 2025 and Fall 2025 freshman applicants).
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Fees: $6,375/Semester (Texas resident, 15 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year) or $12,750/Year (Texas resident, 30 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Dance prepares students to be critically engaged artists, articulate communicators, and thoughtful citizens, who understand the role of dance in society, and whose knowledge and experience are firmly rooted in diverse approaches to contemporary dance practices. Students develop their creative voice through choreographic research, performance, dance scholarship, and pedagogical practices grounded in equity, diversity, and inclusion. This comprehensive program encourages collaboration across disciplines, engagement in community initiatives, and the pursuit of individual passions. The BA in Dance curriculum serves as a foundation for multiple career pathways within the field of dance, including professional performance, choreography, pedagogy, community engagement, arts administration, somatic practices, and graduate studies.
CostPerCredit: $425/credit (Texas resident, effective for 15 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year) or $757.53/credit (Non-resident, effective for 15 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance,
Requirements: Admission to the Dance Program is by audition and application through the department. Students must also meet the general admission requirements of the university. All students seeking admission to the Dance program must apply directly to the university and be accepted. Students wishing to declare Dance as their major must be accepted into the Dance program by meeting the following requirements: 1. Successfully complete an audition as prescribed by the Dance faculty.
Department: Department of Dance and Theatre, College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance is a rigorous, pre-professional degree designed to develop the dance artist. The curriculum includes advanced study in various dance techniques, choreography, dance history, movement analysis, somatic practices, and performance. The goal of the program is to prepare students for professional careers in dance performance, choreography, teaching, or further graduate study. Students will engage in intensive studio work, theoretical studies, and performance opportunities, fostering critical thinking, creativity, and a comprehensive understanding of the art of dance.

ProgramName: Dance (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in Dance requires 18 hours, including 6 hours of Dance major technique courses (DANC 1515, 1516, 2515, 2516, 3515, 3516, 4515, 4516) at the 2000 level or above. Students must be able to place into at least DANC 2515 or 2516. Only students who have demonstrated dance technique ability through audition and placement during the first week of classes are eligible to enroll in these courses. Only courses with a grade of C or better count toward the minor. No more than 6 hours of upper-division courses from other departments may be applied toward the minor. For more information, contact the Department of Dance.
CostPerCredit: $521.13 per credit hour (Texas Resident, College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences) to $924.13 per credit hour (Non-Resident, College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences), for 1-11 semester credit hours.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Competitive, Excellence, Departmental, Endowed, Regents, Need-based

ProgramName: Data Analytics (Minor)
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The minor in Data Analytics introduces students to fundamental concepts and techniques in data analytics. Students gain an understanding of how data are used to support decision-making and how to apply quantitative methods and computational tools to analyze data. The minor offers practical skills in data management, statistical analysis, predictive modeling, and data visualization. Students learn to interpret data insights and communicate findings effectively, preparing them for careers in various fields where data-driven decisions are crucial. This minor can complement a wide range of majors by providing essential data literacy and analytical capabilities relevant in today’s data-intensive world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Science,
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Data Science is an interdisciplinary degree that provides students with strong statistical, mathematical and computational skills that are essential for analyzing and interpreting complex data sets. Students will gain experience with modern machine learning and statistical modeling tools and software, database management, and programming skills that allow them to integrate all aspects of the data science pipeline. A degree in Data Science prepares students for careers in fields ranging from health care, engineering, and government to finance, insurance and social media, among many others. In addition, the degree provides students with a strong foundation for graduate studies in data science or related fields.

ProgramName: Decision Sciences (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: Minimum 3.0 GPA at UNT; completion of 30 UNT hours; admission to the university; completion of DSCI 2710 (Foundations of Business Analytics) or equivalent with a minimum grade of C; completion of MATH 1680 (Calculus I) or MATH 1710 (Calculus) or equivalent with a minimum grade of C; completion of DSCI 3710 (Business Decision Support Systems) or equivalent with a minimum grade of C.
Department: College of Business

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital and Print Journalism,
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: The Digital and Print Journalism, BA program prepares students for careers in news and information industries across a wide array of formats and platforms. The curriculum emphasizes the fundamental values of journalism—truth, accuracy, fairness and independence—while teaching skills essential for success in today’s rapidly evolving media landscape. Students learn to report, write, edit, design and produce content using cutting-edge digital tools for newspapers, magazines, websites, mobile platforms, radio, television and other media. The program also provides a strong foundation in media law and ethics, critical thinking, visual communication and entrepreneurship, preparing graduates to adapt to new technologies and take on leadership roles in the field. Graduates find careers as reporters, editors, producers, content creators, social media managers, public relations specialists, fact-checkers and media entrepreneurs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Digital Retailing,
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a first-year student, you must meet the following requirements: Graduate from an accredited high school or satisfy the Texas high school equivalency requirement. Meet Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP). Submit official high school transcript. Submit official SAT or ACT scores. Scores are optional through Fall 2025. Students who apply without test scores will be evaluated through a holistic review.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: Digital retailing refers to the application of digital technology, processes and business models to enhance, improve and create value for the customer experience. Digital retailing requires the integration of technology and strategy within the retailing context to improve the shopping experience of consumers and achieve competitive advantage for retailers. The Bachelor of Science degree in Digital Retailing is designed to educate students about the strategies and processes related to successfully leveraging digital innovations within a retailing context. The program includes hands-on experience with technologies such as web analytics, mobile payment systems, digital signage, social media applications, augmented/virtual reality, and much more. Students graduating with a Digital Retailing BS degree will be well prepared to pursue careers in digital marketing, social media marketing, digital merchandising, e-commerce, mobile retailing, user experience, visual merchandising, analytics, strategy and technology. The program also helps students prepare for graduate school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts with a major in economics is designed for students seeking a liberal arts education that combines economics with a breadth of courses from other academic disciplines. This degree is especially valuable for students interested in careers in government, law, international affairs, journalism and liberal arts. Students are required to demonstrate foreign language proficiency.
ScholarshipType: Academic performance, specific talents, financial need

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics,
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The undergraduate program in economics is designed to acquaint students with the basic analytical tools and factual information necessary for understanding contemporary economic problems and policies. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in economic theory, quantitative methods and applied economics. An understanding of economic principles is valuable not only for students pursuing careers as economists in government or business, but also for those seeking careers in law, public administration, finance, business administration and other fields where decision making and policy formulation play a prominent role. The department offers a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in economics and a Bachelor of Science (BS) with a major in economics. The BBA degree provides students with a broad background in business with a major in economics. The BS degree provides a strong analytical background and is more quantitative in nature. The department also offers an Economics minor.

ProgramName: Economics (Minor)
Requirements: A minimum of 18 semester hours in economics, including ECON 1100 Principles of Microeconomics and ECON 1110 Principles of Macroeconomics. All advanced courses must be taken at UNT. A maximum of 6 semester hours of internship credit may be used for the minor. Students must meet the following requirements: A minimum overall 2.0 GPA in all courses that could count for the minor; No more than 6 semester hours of transfer credit may be applied to the minor; Students must earn a minimum grade of C in all courses counted toward the minor; Students must have a minimum overall 2.0 GPA to declare the minor.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in economics is designed for students who desire to supplement a major in another field with additional work in economics. It provides a useful background for those students whose career objectives include business or other areas where economic analysis is important. It also provides a useful foundation for graduate work in economics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering,
Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed application for admission online at ApplyTexas or the Common App, pay the non-refundable $75 application fee or submit a fee waiver request form, submit an official high school transcript or GED certificate, and complete the State of Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) requirements. UNT is test-optional for freshman applicants seeking admission for Fall 2024, Spring 2025, and Summer 2025, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required for admission consideration; students admitted without test scores will be evaluated on high school GPA and curriculum. For direct admission to the College of Engineering, an incoming freshman must meet any one of the following academic criteria upon acceptance to the university: Top 25% High School Class Rank; ACT composite score of 24 or higher (if submitted); SAT composite score of 1160 or higher (if submitted); graduated with an Associate of Science (AS) degree from a Texas public institution; or graduated from a Texas high school with the distinguished level of achievement under the Foundation High School Program (House Bill 5). The College of Engineering will also admit students without test scores into an Engineering program based on the student's high school GPA and rigorous curriculum.
Department: College of Engineering
Fees: $12,716/Year (for Texas Residents, based on 30 semester hours)
Description: Electrical engineers work in many fields, including energy, communications, computers, controls, microelectronics and manufacturing. The undergraduate curriculum provides a broad background in topics essential to the discipline of electrical engineering through a required core of courses, with opportunities to specialize through electives. The electrical engineering program prepares students to enter a diverse global workforce and succeed in graduate studies or professional careers. Graduates are able to identify and solve engineering problems, demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility, communicate effectively, apply advanced mathematics and science to engineering problems, and work effectively on multi-disciplinary teams.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Emergency Administration and Planning (Minor)
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: This minor provides students with a foundational understanding of emergency administration and planning. It is designed for students interested in careers in emergency management, disaster preparedness, response, recovery, or related fields. The minor emphasizes practical applications, critical thinking, and interdisciplinary approaches to addressing complex challenges posed by emergencies and disasters. Students will gain knowledge and skills in risk assessment, mitigation, preparedness planning, incident management, and recovery strategies, preparing them to contribute effectively to resilient communities.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident Undergraduate: $394.70 per credit hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Management,
Requirements: Applicants for Engineering Management, BS, must first apply and be admitted to the University of North Texas as an undergraduate student. University freshman admission requires graduation from an accredited high school and satisfactory scores on the SAT or ACT. In addition, for admission to the College of Engineering, applicants must meet general university admission requirements AND any of the following additional requirements: Top 25% of high school class and an SAT score of 1200 or an ACT score of 24; Top 26-50% of high school class and an SAT score of 1200 or an ACT score of 24; Top 51-75% of high school class and an SAT score of 1250 or an ACT score of 25; Top 76-100% of high school class and an SAT score of 1300 or an ACT score of 26. Alternatively, an SAT Math score of 620 or ACT Math score of 26 can satisfy requirements. Applicants not meeting the assured admission standards will be reviewed holistically by the College of Engineering.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: The Engineering Management, BS program prepares students for leadership positions that require both technical and managerial skills. This interdisciplinary degree blends engineering fundamentals with business and management principles to equip graduates with the knowledge to manage projects, teams and operations in technology-driven organizations. Students learn to optimize processes, improve efficiency, manage resources and make strategic decisions in complex engineering environments. The curriculum includes courses in engineering science, mathematics, statistics, economics, accounting, finance, marketing, organizational behavior, operations management and project management.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering Management program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: Writing and Rhetoric; Language and Literature; Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12
Description: The English department at UNT offers an undergraduate curriculum designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the English language and its literature. Students majoring in English may choose from three areas of concentration: Writing and Rhetoric; Language and Literature; and Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12. Students concentrating in Writing and Rhetoric study the theoretical and practical dimensions of writing in various contexts. They will develop their analytical, critical, and interpretive skills, preparing them for graduate work in rhetoric, professional writing, and related fields, as well as for careers in technical and business writing, editing, publishing, law, and government. Students concentrating in Language and Literature study language, literary history and traditions, and literary theory. They will prepare for graduate study in literature and related fields, and for careers in editing, publishing, and other professions demanding strong analytical, critical, interpretive, and communication skills. Students concentrating in Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12, study English language arts content and the theory and practice of teaching. They prepare for careers as secondary school teachers.

ProgramName: English (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Management (Minor)
Requirements: Students must complete 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000) hours. A minimum of 6 advanced hours must be taken in residence at UNT. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required on all courses counting toward the minor. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required on all advanced courses counting toward the minor.
Department: College of Business
Description: The Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Management minor provides students with the business and management skills necessary to launch a new venture or work for a rapidly growing existing venture. Students learn how to identify, evaluate and exploit entrepreneurial opportunities; develop business plans; acquire resources; commercialize technology; and manage fast-growing organizations. The minor is available to all non-business majors, and to business majors who are not pursuing a major in Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Management. The minor may be pursued as part of the undergraduate degree by approval of the student's major department and the G. Brint Ryan College of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science,
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science prepares students for a diverse array of careers. Graduates are qualified for positions in government agencies, private industry and environmental consulting firms. In addition, the program provides an excellent background for students who wish to pursue graduate degrees in Environmental Science, Water Resource Science and Management, or related fields. The program is designed to provide students with a strong background in science, mathematics, statistics and computer science, as well as an understanding of environmental policy and regulations. Students completing the degree will be well prepared to address current and future environmental issues.
CostPerCredit: Up to $178.50/SCH for Texas Residents; Up to $588.50/SCH for Non-Residents

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Event Design and Experience Management,
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Event Design and Experience Management (EDEM) program prepares students to become leaders in the fast-growing and dynamic global events industry. Students will learn the process of designing, planning, marketing, operating, and evaluating various types of events, including corporate events, festivals, concerts, conferences, and sports events. The curriculum emphasizes creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and sustainable practices relevant to the event industry. Graduates will be equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to create memorable and impactful experiences for diverse audiences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Fashion Design,
Requirements: General university admission requirements apply. Admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design and to the Fashion Design program is by portfolio review during the spring semester of the sophomore year for students who have successfully completed the first year of the Foundation curriculum. Further information regarding the portfolio review process and dates is available in the Fashion Design office, Art Building, Room 230.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: Students interested in a career in the fashion industry will find a dynamic and creative learning environment in the Fashion Design BFA program. The program prepares students for professional careers in the design of apparel, accessories, textiles and related fields, or for further graduate study. Students develop knowledge and skills in design, aesthetic judgment, merchandising, sourcing, and marketing. Graduates are employed in a variety of design and creative positions including apparel designers, product developers, technical designers, patternmakers, illustrators, textile designers and merchandisers for manufacturers and retailers, or they may choose to pursue graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Fibers,
Requirements: Students must meet the general university admission requirements. Admission to the B.F.A. with a major in Fibers is contingent on passing a portfolio review.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Fibers provides an in-depth curriculum of studio practice with supporting art history and critical studies course work. The program emphasizes an understanding of traditional and experimental media and processes in contemporary art. Students are introduced to a wide range of materials and techniques with opportunity for in-depth study in areas such as weaving, dyeing, surface design, non-woven fiber construction, digital textile design, and other interdisciplinary approaches. Graduates are prepared for careers as professional artists, studio assistants, designers, art educators, and for graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film, Television and Digital Media,
Requirements: To apply: 1. Complete the application for admission online at ApplyTexas or Common App. 2. Pay the non-refundable $75 application fee. 3. Submit your official high school transcript to UNT Admissions. 4. Submit your official SAT and/or ACT scores (optional) to UNT Admissions. UNT offers automatic admission to students who meet certain academic criteria. Automatic admission for freshmen with test scores typically requires a minimum SAT score of 1070 (or 1030 for tests taken prior to March 2016) or an ACT composite score of 21, combined with a specified class rank. Automatic admission for freshmen without test scores (Test-Optional) requires graduating in the top 10% of your class or graduating in the top 25% of your class with a minimum 3.0 GPA (on a 4.0 scale). If you do not meet automatic admission requirements, your application will be reviewed through an Individual Review process where an admission committee evaluates several factors, including academic preparedness, essays, unique experiences, and other information provided in your application.
Department: Mayborn College of Journalism
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Film, Television and Digital Media is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the historical, theoretical, critical and aesthetic dimensions of the moving image. Through a combination of coursework, hands-on production experiences, and critical analysis, students develop skills in storytelling, media analysis, production techniques, and ethical considerations within the evolving media landscape. The program prepares students for careers in the film, television, and digital media industries, as well as for advanced studies in media arts.

ProgramName: Finance, BBA
Department: College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration, major in Finance, emphasizes the financial aspects of managerial decisions. This program prepares students for positions in corporate finance, investment management, banking, insurance and real estate. The curriculum provides an understanding of how managers and investors can best make decisions in financial markets given different risk and return tradeoffs.

ProgramName: Finance (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements:
Minor Requirements
A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counted toward the minor.
No more than 6 semester hours of transfer credit may be counted toward the minor.
An overall GPA of 2.0 must be maintained on all courses attempted in the minor at UNT.
A minimum of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level).
Students must complete at least 6 hours of advanced courses at UNT.
Students must meet all prerequisites for minor courses.

Other Requirements
A student completing a minor in Finance must be a non-business major. Students earning a business major are not eligible to complete a minor in Finance.
No minor is offered in finance for finance majors or business majors.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Department of Finance offers a minor in finance for non-business majors. The minor provides an understanding of financial decision-making for managing individuals' and organizations' financial assets and liabilities, and the functioning of financial markets. It helps prepare students for careers in banking, real estate, personal financial planning, corporate finance, and the financial services industry generally.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Financial Planning,
Department: College of Business
Fees: Resident: $6,098/Semester; Non-Resident: $16,478/Semester (estimated undergraduate tuition and required fees for 15 credit hours, 2023-2024)
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Financial Planning prepares students for successful careers in financial planning and provides the academic background necessary to sit for the Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) examination. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in personal financial planning, investment, risk management and insurance, employee benefits and retirement planning, estate planning and income tax planning. The financial planning curriculum provides the academic background necessary for students to pursue graduate studies in financial planning, law or business. It also provides the academic background necessary to sit for the CFP® examination, the globally recognized professional certification in financial planning.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $406.53/credit hour; Non-Resident: $1098.53/credit hour (estimated undergraduate tuition and required fees for 15 credit hours, 2023-2024)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: ~$390.40/credit hour (based on 15 hours); Non-Resident: ~$757.20/credit hour (based on 15 hours)
ScholarshipType: Academic, Leadership, Talent-based, Institutional, Competitive, Departmental

ProgramName: French (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description:
A minor in French requires a minimum of 18 hours, including 12 advanced hours. A minimum of 6 hours of advanced work must be completed at UNT.

Course Requirements:
FREN 1010, FREN 1020 (unless placement test shows competency)
FREN 2040, FREN 2050
FREN 3010, FREN 3020, FREN 3030, FREN 3040, FREN 3060, FREN 3070, FREN 3080
FREN 4010, FREN 4020, FREN 4030, FREN 4040, FREN 4050, FREN 4060, FREN 4070, FREN 4080

For more information, see the French section of the World Languages, Literatures and Cultures page in this catalog.

ProgramName: General Business (Minor for non-business majors)
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The General Business minor is designed for students who are not majoring in business but want to develop a general understanding of business principles. It provides students with a broad overview of essential business functions such as management, marketing, finance, and information technology. This minor can complement a wide range of non-business majors, enhancing career opportunities by adding a valuable business perspective.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: General Geography, Urban and Regional Planning
Description: A major in Geography helps students develop a global perspective on environmental and social issues, including climate change, natural hazards, land use, population change, cultural diversity, and urbanization. Students develop spatial thinking and problem-solving skills, and acquire proficiency with geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sensing technology to analyze geographic data. Graduates find career opportunities as urban and regional planners, environmental consultants, GIS analysts, demographers, cartographers, location analysts, and teachers. Our graduates also pursue graduate studies in geography and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geography,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: Applied GIS, Atmospheric Science, Environmental Geography, Urban and Regional Planning
Description: Geography is the study of earth as the home of humankind. Geographers investigate the spatial patterns and processes associated with human and natural phenomena. Geographers use various methods, including fieldwork, remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), global positioning systems (GPS), qualitative methods and statistical analysis. Geographers often address questions such as: Where are things located? Why are they located there? What are the consequences of their location? How are places formed? Geography offers a unique perspective for understanding complex global, regional and local issues, such as global warming, environmental degradation, natural hazards, economic development, political instability, urbanization and cultural conflict. Students in geography are prepared for a wide variety of careers in government, the private sector and education.

ProgramName: Geography (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in geography requires 18 semester hours, including at least 9 hours at the advanced level (3000- or 4000-level). A grade of C or better is required in all courses counted toward the minor. The minimum UNT GPA for minor courses is 2.0. This minor is designed to: Provide a basic understanding of geographic concepts and principles. Offer an opportunity to explore various aspects of the discipline, such as physical geography, human geography, geographic information science, and environmental studies. Enhance a student’s major by providing a broader perspective on spatial relationships and processes. Develop skills in spatial analysis and critical thinking. Courses completed to satisfy university core curriculum requirements may not be counted toward a minor. For more information about courses required for the minor, contact the Department of Geography and the Environment.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Department of World Languages, Literatures and Cultures offers a Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in German. The German program offers students the opportunity to acquire proficiency in German and an in-depth understanding of German and German-speaking cultures within a global context. The German major helps students develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural communication, and cultural analysis as they prepare for a variety of careers or for further study.

ProgramName: German (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Fees: $11,112/Year (Estimated for Academic Year 2023-2024, 12 hours/semester for Texas Resident Undergraduate)
Description: The minor in German introduces students to the German language and to selected aspects of the literature and cultures of German-speaking countries. The minor requires a minimum of 18 semester hours in German with a GPA of at least 2.0 (C) in all courses counted toward the minor. A minimum of 6 semester hours must be taken at UNT.

ProgramName: Health and Wellness Studies (Minor)
Requirements: A minimum GPA of 2.0 UNT and 2.0 Major GPA is required.
Department: College of Education
Fees: Resident: $11,848/Year (estimated for 30 SCH); Non-Resident: $22,204/Year (estimated for 30 SCH)
Description: The minor in Health and Wellness Studies promotes the development of knowledge and skills necessary to improve the health and well-being of individuals and communities. This interdisciplinary minor allows students to apply concepts of health promotion, disease prevention, and behavior change to a variety of professional and personal settings. Students will gain an understanding of health disparities, cultural competence, and ethical considerations in health and wellness. The minor prepares students for careers in public health, health education, corporate wellness, community health, and other related fields, or for further graduate study.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Academic scholarships, Departmental scholarships, Freshman scholarships, Transfer scholarships, Continuing student scholarships, Athletic scholarships, Art scholarships, Music scholarships, Theatre scholarships, Leadership scholarships

ProgramName: Health Services Administration (Minor)
Requirements: Students who wish to pursue a minor in Health Services Administration must be in good academic standing and have a minimum 2.5 overall GPA. Students pursuing this minor who have a major outside the College of Health and Public Service must have a minimum 2.5 GPA in the major. Students must also earn a C or better in all courses counted toward the minor. Students must apply for admission to the minor through the Department of Health Services Administration. Students will be admitted to the minor based on overall academic performance and space availability in the minor.
Department: College of Health and Public Service

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health, Wellness and Community,
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Health, Wellness and Community prepares students with the knowledge and skills to promote health and prevent disease for individuals, families and communities. The interdisciplinary curriculum addresses a wide range of health-related topics including nutrition, physical activity, mental health, substance use, chronic disease prevention and health disparities. The program emphasizes community health promotion strategies, health education, program planning and evaluation, and advocacy. Graduates are prepared for careers in public health agencies, non-profit organizations, corporate wellness programs and healthcare settings, or for graduate studies in public health, health administration, or related fields.
CostPerCredit: $388.67/Semester Credit Hour (estimated average for 15 SCH, Texas Resident)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in History provides students with an understanding of the past and the skills needed to interpret historical events. Through rigorous coursework, students learn to analyze primary and secondary sources, develop critical thinking abilities, and communicate effectively both orally and in writing. The program prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, government, museums, archives, and business. It also provides a solid foundation for graduate study in history or related disciplines.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Federal Grants, State Grants, Departmental

ProgramName: History (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in history requires 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced. The department requires that 6 of the 18 hours must be in United States history; 3 hours must be in European history; and 3 hours must be in non-Western history. At least 9 hours must be taken at UNT. All courses counted toward the minor must be passed with a grade of C or better. Only one internship (HIST 4090) may count toward the minor.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Home Furnishings Merchandising,
Requirements:
All students seeking a BS degree in Home Furnishings Merchandising are required to satisfy the following requirements for admission to the College of Merchandising:
	*   Satisfy University requirements for admission.
	*   Have a minimum 2.5 cumulative UNT GPA.
	*   Have completed a minimum of 30 semester hours.
	*   Achieve a minimum C in each merchandising course.
	*   Complete MKTG 3650 with a C or better.
Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Home Furnishings Merchandising program prepares students for various positions in the residential and contract segments of the home furnishings industry. Students develop an understanding of home furnishings products and materials, product sourcing and distribution, merchandising, retail operations, sales, and entrepreneurial practices. The program offers a broad education in merchandising with a strong emphasis on business and marketing. This program includes a business minor and a required professional internship in the home furnishings industry. The department maintains close ties with the home furnishings industry, providing students with numerous opportunities for professional development and industry engagement.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, special talents, or financial need

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management,
Requirements: Students are admitted to the university as pre-majors. Students are admitted to the Hospitality Management program after successful completion of HMGT 1460, HMGT 2460, FINA 1307, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, MATH 1190, DSCI 2710 and junior standing (60 earned hours). Students must meet the following criteria: An overall 2.5 UNT GPA, A minimum grade of C in each of the following courses: HMGT 1460, HMGT 2460, FINA 1307, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, MATH 1190, DSCI 2710.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in hospitality management prepares students for leadership positions in the largest service industry in the world. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in business and management practices applicable to the hotel, restaurant, tourism, convention, club, casino and other segments of the hospitality industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Science,
Department: College of Education
Fees: $9,366.82/Year (Texas Resident, estimated 15 credit hours/semester tuition + mandatory fees for 2023-2024)
Description: The Department of Human Development and Family Science offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Human Development and Family Science designed to prepare students to work effectively with individuals and families in diverse settings. This program is for students interested in careers that focus on the development of individuals and families across the life span and within the context of diverse family structures and community systems. The curriculum offers opportunities to gain knowledge and skills in understanding individual and family dynamics, promoting healthy relationships, and addressing contemporary issues facing families. Students will also learn about child development, family theories, interventions, ethics, and research methods. The program integrates theory, research, and practice to equip students with the competencies needed for various professional roles, including family life education, social services, youth development, and early childhood education. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions in agencies, schools, hospitals, and non-profit organizations or for continued graduate studies in related fields. This academic program is accredited by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for meeting the high standards for the Provisional Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
Accredidation: National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for meeting the high standards for the Provisional Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $270.65/credit hour (tuition only); Non-resident: $730.65/credit hour (tuition only). Other mandatory fees per credit hour also apply.
ScholarshipType: Institutional, private and state-funded scholarships, academic scholarships, departmental scholarships

ProgramName: Human Resource Management, BBA
Requirements: Students are evaluated for admission based on two factors: (1) high school performance and (2) standardized test scores (SAT or ACT). Applicants with an SAT score below 970 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math) or an ACT composite score below 18 will not be admitted under individual review.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: Human resource management involves the effective utilization of people to achieve organizational and individual goals. Students will acquire the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully meet the challenges facing today's human resource management professionals including strategic human resource management, human resource planning, staffing, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and HR information systems.
Accredidation: College of Business (AACSB International accredited)

ProgramName: Human Resource Management (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: Minimum 18 hours. Courses must be completed with a minimum grade of C. A minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses comprising the minor. A student must be in good standing with the university to declare a minor. A student may not declare a minor in their major department. Students must meet the GPA requirements for the minor in order to graduate with the minor. Required courses (9 hours): MGMT 3720 Human Resource Management (3 hours), MGMT 3830 Compensation and Benefits (3 hours), MGMT 4800 Selection and Staffing (3 hours). Elective courses (select 9 hours): MGMT 3850 Labor and Industrial Relations (3 hours), MGMT 4470 Global Human Resources (3 hours), MGMT 4810 Training and Development (3 hours), MGMT 4820 Employment Law (3 hours), MGMT 4850 Organizational Behavior and Design (3 hours), MGMT 4880 Human Resource Analytics (3 hours).
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Human Resource Management minor is designed to provide students with an understanding of various aspects of human resource management, including staffing, training and development, compensation, and legal issues. The minor requires a minimum of 18 semester hours with a minimum of 9 advanced hours from the courses listed below. All 18 semester hours for the minor must be completed at UNT.
CostPerCredit: Undergraduate Resident: $407.72/Credit Hour; Undergraduate Non-Resident: $857.72/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Information Science,
Department: College of Information
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in Information Science provides an understanding of the concepts, systems, and tools for organizing, accessing, and using information. Students learn how to analyze, design, and manage information systems and services in a variety of organizational settings. Students also gain skills in information organization, information retrieval, information technologies, and user experience design. The degree provides opportunities for students to apply these skills in internships, research projects, and other experiential learning activities.
The Information Science, BS degree prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as data analysis, information management, knowledge management, library and information services, user experience design, and digital asset management. Graduates are prepared for positions in public and private sector organizations, including corporations, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and educational institutions. The degree also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in information science and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Information Technology,
Requirements:
General Admission Requirements
Freshman applicants must be graduates of an accredited high school or must have completed the equivalent of a high school education in an approved setting. All freshman applicants are required to submit an official high school transcript, official SAT or ACT scores, and a completed application for admission. Homeschool transcripts must be accompanied by an approved homeschool diploma or certification of completion.

The university reserves the right to deny admission to any applicant if, in the judgment of the university, the applicant is not an acceptable candidate for admission.

Assured Admission Policy
A freshman applicant will be admitted to the university if they meet the following assured admission requirements:

Rank in the top 25 percent of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 20 or an SAT total score of 1030 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the second quarter (26-50 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 23 or an SAT total score of 1130 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the third quarter (51-75 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 26 or an SAT total score of 1240 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the fourth quarter (76-100 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 29 or an SAT total score of 1360 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Applicants who are not eligible for assured admission may be reviewed for admission on an individual basis. Individual review takes into consideration academic rigor, extracurricular activities, essays, and other relevant information.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Information Technology provides an interdisciplinary and applied course of study in the development, deployment, and management of information technology and information systems. The BA in IT prepares students to assume professional positions with a variety of technical and leadership responsibilities across a wide range of organizations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Studies,
Requirements: Apply online using ApplyTexas or Common App. Pay the non-refundable $75 application fee. Submit official high school transcript. UNT reviews applications based on a holistic review process that includes academic rigor, essay, extracurricular activities, and test scores (if submitted). Test scores are not required for admission for summer/fall 2024 and spring 2025. If you wish to be considered for admission without SAT/ACT scores, you must submit an essay and resume to be considered.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description:
Do you have a wide variety of academic interests and want to develop critical thinking skills across different subjects? The Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that allows students to combine three "focus areas" of study from different academic disciplines.

This degree plan is specifically designed to give you flexibility and independence to tailor your academic path based on your passions and career goals. You'll work closely with an academic advisor to select three 18-hour focus areas that align with your interests, career aspirations, and educational goals. The ability to integrate multiple fields of study is a valuable asset in today's dynamic job market.

This unique approach not only broadens your knowledge base but also enhances your problem-solving abilities, communication skills and critical thinking, preparing you for a wide range of career paths or graduate studies. Whether you are passionate about the arts, sciences, humanities, or a combination, the B.A. in Integrative Studies empowers you to build a degree that truly reflects your intellectual curiosity and professional ambitions.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Departmental affiliation

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Integrative Studies,
Requirements: Students interested in majoring in Integrative Studies should contact the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences advising office. For information about general admission to UNT and how to apply, see the Undergraduate Admissions website. To apply to UNT as a freshman, you will need to submit the following: Complete the ApplyTexas application (or Common App). Pay the $75 application fee or request a fee waiver. Submit official high school transcripts. Submit official college transcripts (if applicable). Submit official SAT or ACT scores.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that gives students the opportunity to combine three academic areas of study into a single degree. This degree is designed for students who want to develop a broad knowledge base and skillset rather than specialize in one particular field. The unique combination of coursework provides students with a holistic view of several disciplines, thus giving graduates a wider range of career and/or graduate school options. This degree is especially well suited for students who want to build custom curricula in preparation for specific career fields not addressed by a single traditional major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies,
Requirements: Students interested in declaring a major in Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies may do so once they have fulfilled all university core curriculum requirements.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies BA program offers a flexible curriculum focusing on critical thinking, research skills and writing while engaging in the theory and practice of art, design and visual culture. Students cultivate an understanding of art and design within broad historical, theoretical and social contexts, and gain a wide range of skills applicable to the professional world. The degree prepares students for a variety of careers in fields that utilize art and design in an interdisciplinary context, such as non-profit administration, museums and galleries, community engagement, arts advocacy, education, communications, entrepreneurship, and publishing. The degree also provides excellent preparation for graduate study in a range of fields, including art history, visual culture, museum education, and arts administration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Interior Design,
Requirements: General university admission requirements. In addition to meeting university requirements, students must declare a major in the College of Visual Arts and Design and satisfy any specific program requirements to pursue a degree in the college.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: Interior design is a creative, technical and analytical process used to develop interior environments that are healthy, safe, enjoyable and productive. The profession focuses on the building envelope and human interaction within that space. Interior designers have expertise in space planning, aesthetics, building codes, universal design, sustainable design, lighting, acoustics, materials and furnishings, and professional practice. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in residential, commercial and institutional design firms. The program culminates in a senior studio capstone experience and portfolio.
Accredidation: The Interior Design program at the University of North Texas is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA), 206 Grandville Ave., Suite 350, Grand Rapids, MI, 49503.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: Asian Studies Track, European Studies Track, Global Issues Track, Latin American Studies Track, Middle East & North African Studies Track
Description: The international studies major is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the international community and global issues. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in government, non-profit organizations and business, and for graduate study in international relations, law, public administration, international business and related fields. The curriculum includes course work in the humanities, social sciences, business and foreign languages related to global issues, specific world regions and cross-cultural understanding. All international studies majors are required to demonstrate third-year proficiency in a foreign language.

ProgramName: International Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Italian (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description:
The minor in Italian consists of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). Students must have completed ITAL 1010 and 1020 (or equivalent proficiency) prior to beginning the minor. The minor requires a minimum UNT GPA of 2.0.
A minor in Italian develops a student’s appreciation of Italian language and culture while complementing studies in a variety of fields such as art history, international studies, political science, history, literature, music, business and film.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese,
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Japanese provides students with proficiency in Japanese language as well as a rich background in Japanese history, culture and literature. Students are also encouraged to develop competency in a second foreign language beyond the university’s foreign language requirement.
CostPerCredit: $520.20/credit hour (Non-Resident undergraduate, plus fixed semester fees)

ProgramName: Japanese (Minor)
Requirements: To declare a minor, students must have a minimum 2.0 GPA.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Japanese minor provides students with the linguistic and cultural background to interact with Japanese-speaking communities and pursue various careers. A minor in Japanese requires a minimum of 18 hours, including 6 advanced hours. No more than 6 hours of Japanese may be counted toward both the minor and another major or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses counting toward the minor. Required courses: JAPN 2040 - Intermediate Japanese I (3 hours) JAPN 2050 - Intermediate Japanese II (3 hours) JAPN 3040 - Advanced Japanese I (3 hours) JAPN 3050 - Advanced Japanese II (3 hours) Plus 6 hours of Japanese at the 3000-4000 level. Up to 6 hours may be JAPN 3000.

ProgramName: Jewish and Israel Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Minor in Jewish and Israel Studies requires 18 hours, 12 of which must be advanced (3000/4000) level, drawn from an approved list of courses. The minor is offered by the Department of History, and is housed within the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism,
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
Concentration: Broadcast Journalism, Digital and Converged Journalism, News and Feature Journalism, Photojournalism
Description: The Department of Journalism offers students instruction and professional preparation in the many varied aspects of journalism. Students are prepared to enter a wide variety of journalism careers including jobs in news, photojournalism, visual communication, editing, web design and development, data visualization, magazine, broadcast, and multimedia journalism. The curriculum emphasizes professional courses, internships and a strong liberal arts background with a major that encourages students to complete a minor in another field. The department also offers graduate degrees.

ProgramName: Journalism (Minor)
Requirements: Students wishing to declare a minor in Journalism must be in good standing with the university and have a cumulative UNT GPA of at least 2.5. The admission process, as outlined in the Mayborn School of Journalism section of the catalog, includes completion of JOUR 1210 with a grade of C or better, completion of a Writing, Rhetoric, and Literacies core course (or equivalent) with a grade of B or better, and submission of a formal application to the Mayborn School of Journalism.
Department: Mayborn College of Journalism
Description: The Journalism minor gives students the opportunity to learn critical thinking, research, writing, reporting and multimedia storytelling skills for a variety of media professions. This minor is open to all students on campus, regardless of major. The minor offers flexibility for students to explore their interests in areas such as digital and broadcast journalism, strategic communications, or sports media. It also offers students an opportunity to learn current digital skills, including video, audio, social media and data journalism. By gaining knowledge and experience in journalism, students enhance their major while also improving their critical thinking, writing, and communication skills, which are vital for careers in any field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology,
Requirements: Admission to the Kinesiology program Students must meet the university admission requirements (see Undergraduate Admission). Students who enter UNT as freshmen will be directly admitted into the Kinesiology program provided they meet UNT's general admission requirements. Transfer students and students changing majors will be admitted to the Kinesiology program if they meet the following requirements: Minimum 2.5 overall GPA. Completion of 30 semester hours. Completion of CHEM 1410/1412 and BIOL 2301/2302 (or equivalents) with a minimum grade of C.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Department of Kinesiology offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Kinesiology. Students in this program are prepared for careers in health, fitness and wellness, sport management, and allied health professions. Emphasis is placed on human movement, health, fitness, and sport from a scientific, behavioral, and socio-cultural perspective. The undergraduate program in Kinesiology provides a broad background in exercise science, public health, and human movement studies and is designed to lead to entry-level positions in fitness, health, and sport professions, as well as prepare students for graduate study or professional schools. The Kinesiology undergraduate program offers three concentrations, allowing students to tailor their academic experience to their specific career interests.

ProgramName: Latino/a and Mexican American Studies (Minor)
Requirements: Students must declare the minor with the Department of History, located in Wooten Hall 217.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Latino/a and Mexican American Studies (LMAS) program offers a 18-hour undergraduate minor in interdisciplinary scholarship. Students completing the minor will develop a critically informed understanding of the histories, cultures, politics, and social experiences of Latino/a and Mexican American communities in the United States and transnationally. The minor introduces students to the major theoretical and methodological approaches to Latino/a and Mexican American Studies scholarship and provides opportunities to apply these to a variety of topics and issues. Through critical analysis of race, class, gender, and sexuality in historical and contemporary contexts, the LMAS minor provides students with the intellectual tools to engage with and contribute to social justice.

ProgramName: Leadership Development (Minor)
Requirements: To declare this minor, students must have a 2.5 GPA at UNT and have completed 45 hours of coursework.
Department: College of Education, Department of Educational Psychology
Description: The Leadership Development minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to enhance the leadership competencies and capacity of students from all majors through a combination of coursework and experiential learning opportunities. The minor supports students in developing foundational leadership knowledge, skills, and abilities for a variety of contexts; understanding leadership from multiple perspectives, theories, and approaches; practicing leadership and working effectively in a team through experiential learning activities; identifying and clarifying personal values, ethics, and strengths relative to leadership; applying self-reflection and critical thinking to leadership practice; and communicating effectively and building relationships within and across diverse groups. Students will cultivate skills and experiences valuable in any profession or area of graduate study.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Talent, Leadership, Special interests, Financial Need

ProgramName: Legal Information Management (Minor)
Department: College of Information
Description: The minor in Legal Information Management provides students with a foundational understanding of the legal information profession, including the acquisition, organization, retrieval, and preservation of legal information resources. Students will develop skills in legal research, legal technology, and legal ethics, preparing them for careers in law libraries, legal departments, government agencies, and other organizations that require expertise in managing legal information. The minor is suitable for students pursuing a variety of majors, including those in political science, criminal justice, business, and information science. Students interested in the minor should contact the Department of Information Science for advising.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $438.37/SCH, Non-Resident: $803.03/SCH (for Fall 2023 undergraduate total tuition and fees per semester credit hour)

ProgramName: Legal Studies (Minor)
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The minor in Legal Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a broad understanding of the legal system and its impact on society. The minor introduces students to the nature of law, legal reasoning, legal institutions, and the role of law in various social, economic, and political contexts. It also provides students with an opportunity to explore career paths in law and related fields. The minor complements a wide range of majors by providing valuable skills in critical thinking, analytical reasoning, research, and communication. These skills are essential for success in law school, graduate school, and various professional careers.

ProgramName: LGBTQ Studies (Minor)
Requirements: Students interested in declaring a minor in LGBTQ Studies should contact the Department of Women’s and Gender Studies.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The LGBTQ Studies minor provides students with the critical skills and knowledge to understand lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer lives from an interdisciplinary perspective. This minor is designed to help students understand LGBTQ issues related to human sexuality, gender identity and expression, race/ethnicity, and social justice. The LGBTQ Studies minor provides the opportunity for students to complement their major with a focused program of study in LGBTQ history, culture, and experience. In addition, the minor prepares students for careers in LGBTQ advocacy and activism, public policy, social work, and education, among others. In a globalizing world, understanding issues of sexuality and gender is increasingly important. This minor is open to all students, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Departmental, Leadership-based, University affiliation-based

ProgramName: Logistics and Supply Chain Management, BBA
Requirements:
Admission to the professional program in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business is required for students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration degree. To be admitted to the professional program in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business, students must meet the following requirements:
* Completion of at least 45 semester hours (30 hours at UNT).
* Completion of the following courses (or their equivalents) with a minimum grade of C in each: ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, BCOM 2700, DSCI 2710, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 2240, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1400 or MATH 1710, LSCM 2800 or MGMT 2100, MKTG 2650.
* A minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted.
* A minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all courses in the professional field of study.
* Submission of a professional program application to the College of Business prior to registration for professional courses.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in Logistics and Supply Chain Management prepares students for a wide range of career opportunities in the field of logistics and supply chain management. This field involves the planning, implementation and controlling of the efficient flow and storage of goods, services and related information from the point of origin to the point of consumption. It includes the management of activities such as inventory, warehousing, transportation, distribution, purchasing, supply management, global logistics, and supply chain strategy. Students will gain knowledge and skills in these key areas, preparing them for careers in various industries, including manufacturing, retail, transportation, consulting, and government. The program emphasizes analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, as well as an understanding of global supply chain issues and sustainability practices. Graduates will be equipped to manage and optimize complex supply chain operations, contributing to organizational efficiency and competitive advantage.

ProgramName: Management, BBA
Requirements: To be admitted to the University of North Texas for the Management, BBA program, applicants must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements which include submitting an application via ApplyTexas or Common App, official high school transcripts, and paying an application fee ($75 U.S. / $85 International). SAT/ACT scores, an essay, letters of recommendation, and a resume are optional for freshman admission for 2024-2025. For admission specifically to the College of Business where the Management, BBA program resides, students must first meet university admission requirements and then additionally meet the following minimum requirements: 30 earned hours, a 2.5 UNT GPA and 2.5 overall GPA, and completion of specific courses (ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, DSCI 2710, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1710, FINA 3000, LSCM 3300, MGMT 3720, MKTG 3650) with a grade of C or better.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Department of Management offers a major in Management leading to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) degree. This major provides a broad base of knowledge regarding the management of organizations. Students are prepared for careers in management, human resource management and entrepreneurship/small business management, as well as for further study at the graduate level. The curriculum helps students develop strong critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making and communication skills applicable to managing a business operation and its human resources.

ProgramName: Management (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have a minimum 2.5 overall GPA, have completed 45 hours, and have a grade of C or better in ACCT 2010 and ACCT 2020. Students must earn a grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor. For additional information, contact the department.
Department: College of Business
Description: The minor in management is designed to provide students with an overview of the role of managers in organizations. It includes courses in the basic principles of management, organizational behavior, human resource management and strategic management. This minor is open to all university students except those majoring in business fields. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor.

ProgramName: Marketing, BBA
Requirements: Students must meet the minimum entrance requirements for the university to be admitted to the pre-business program. To be eligible for admission to the G. Brint Ryan College of Business and pursue a bachelor’s degree, a student must meet the following requirements: * Minimum UNT cumulative GPA of 2.75 * Minimum UNT GPA of 2.75 in the pre-business courses * Students must have a grade of ‘C’ or better in each of the pre-business courses. * Complete 45 semester hours of college-level work. Pre-business courses: ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, BCOM 2700, DSCI 2710, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 2620, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350, LSCM 2100, MKTG 2650.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing prepares students for a variety of careers across the marketing field. Marketing is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. Marketers play a key role in understanding customers, creating value, communicating value, and delivering value. The marketing major provides students with the fundamental knowledge needed to succeed in areas such as professional selling and sales management, digital marketing, marketing analytics, supply chain management, retail management, brand management, marketing research and advertising.

ProgramName: Marketing (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements:
Students must meet the following requirements to be admitted to the minor and declare it officially with the G. Brint Ryan College of Business:
*   Have completed 30 semester hours of college course work.
*   Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted.
*   Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted at UNT.
*   Have completed an approved mathematics course (MATH 1315, 1340, 1342, 1400, 1710, 1720, or equivalent).
*   Have completed an approved economics course (ECON 1100, 1110, or equivalent).
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The marketing minor is designed to provide non-business majors with an opportunity to acquire fundamental marketing knowledge and skills. Students completing the marketing minor will be prepared to integrate marketing concepts into their primary field of study. The minor provides an excellent supplement for students in a variety of fields such as communication, hospitality management, merchandising, journalism, music, visual arts and general studies, to name a few. The minor will help students increase their marketability in the workplace.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering,
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Materials science and engineering is an interdisciplinary field that deals with the discovery and design of new materials. Materials are at the heart of all engineering disciplines; they determine product characteristics and functionality across all aspects of our lives. Materials science and engineering majors learn about the relationships between properties, structure, processing and performance of engineering materials. This knowledge prepares students for successful careers in academia, industry and national laboratories. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Materials Science and Engineering, a Master of Science (MS) in Materials Science and Engineering, and a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering. The department also offers a minor in materials science and engineering. The BS in Materials Science and Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based, special talents or interests

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics,
Requirements: Applying to UNT for the first time is easy! Submit your application, official transcripts and required test scores. We use a holistic review process that takes into account both academic achievement and individual experiences and attributes. Assured admission for freshmen is based on high school class rank and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT). For students who do not meet assured admission requirements, we may still offer admission through our individual review process.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in Mathematics is an excellent choice for students who want a broad liberal arts education but who also want to obtain a solid grounding in mathematics. Many students pursue this degree in combination with another major in a field such as economics, computer science, business or the sciences. This degree also provides students with the background needed for teaching mathematics in grades 7-12 (with proper certification), and it can be used as preparation for graduate study in mathematics or in a related field. The BA in Mathematics requires courses in mathematics, statistics and computer science, as well as a foreign language.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics,
Requirements: Admission to the University is required for admission to a degree program.
Department: College of Science
Concentration: Secondary Teacher Certification, Standard, Computer Science concentration
Description: Mathematics is the basis for all scientific and technological advancements, which makes it a valuable degree in many fields. The UNT Department of Mathematics provides a fundamental grounding in mathematical theory, as well as opportunities to apply mathematics to real-world problems. Our bachelor's degree program is the study of quantity, structure, space, and change.
